# Wazza OS user guide: the full text

> Wazza OS runs desktop apps (GIMP, Blender, Inkscape, ONLYOFFICE, a browser and others) in virtual machines on your Linux computer, each app in a tab with its own AI agent (a Chat) that works in that app. This user guide explains every capability: install and first start, tabs and apps, Chats, agents and models, several agents at once, Drive (agents that see and use an app's screen), Computer Control, skills, files between your computer and the VMs, the Wazza OS MCP for outside agents (Claude Code, Codex and others), the command line, every setting, privacy, memory and troubleshooting.

Every page of https://os-guide.wazza.ai/ in menu order, as markdown. The index of pages: https://os-guide.wazza.ai/llms.txt

# Wazza OS

AI that works with you, in the tools you already use. Wazza OS runs a computer of its own (a virtual machine) next to yours, with real desktop apps in it, and AI agents that work in those apps beside you: you ask, they work, you watch, step in, or carry on in your own tab.

- **Real apps, safely apart.** GIMP, Blender, ONLYOFFICE, a browser, VSCodium and dozens more run in virtual machines, not on your computer.
- **Several agents at once.** Each app opens in a tab with its own Chat; agents work in parallel tabs while you keep yours.
- **Skills and personas.** Agents load know-how for each app and task, and learn your way of working.
- **Drive.** Agents see the app's screen and use the mouse and keyboard, in any app.
- **Any AI.** A plan you already pay for, an API key from one of 73 providers, a company gateway, or a model on your own computer.

- **Runs on**: Linux: Ubuntu, Debian, Fedora, openSUSE, Arch (x86-64, with KVM)

- **Install**: One command (or one package); the VM is created and managed for you

- **Agents**: Hermes, Prime Agent, Claude Code, Codex, Antigravity

- **Models**: Your plans, your API keys (73 providers), any compatible API, or a Wazza OS account

## Install

Paste this in a terminal, on the Linux computer where Wazza OS will live. It asks for your password once, for `sudo`.

```
$ curl -fsSL https://os.wazza.ai/install.sh | sh
```

To test first, without installing anything:

```
$ curl -fsSL https://os.wazza.ai/install.sh | sh -s -- --check
```

### Finds your package type

Debian, Ubuntu and their family get the `.deb`. Fedora and openSUSE get the `.rpm`. Arch and its family get the Arch package. Any other distribution gets the tarball.

### Verifies the release

Nothing installs unless the release manifest carries Wazza's Ed25519 signature and the package matches its signed SHA-256 and size.

### Resumes if cut

The package is large. If the download stops, run the command again: it continues where it stopped.

What your computer needs, other ways to install, updates and removal: [Install, update, remove](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/install.html). Your first start, step by step: [The first start](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/first-start.html).

## Connect your AI agent

Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, VS Code, Gemini CLI, Hermes and Prime Agent can work in Wazza OS through `wazza-os mcp`, the MCP server that comes with it. For Claude Code, once:

```
$ claude mcp add --scope user wazza-os -- wazza-os mcp
```

The line for each agent: [The Wazza OS MCP](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/mcp.html#connect-an-agent-from-outside). Everything an agent can do: [Every Wazza OS MCP tool](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/mcp-tools.html).

## Control Wazza OS

- **From a terminal**, on your desktop or on a server: [The command line](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/cli.html), and [Wazza OS on a server](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/cli-server.html) (with its own virtual screen).
- **From an agent**: [The Wazza OS MCP](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/mcp.html) and [Every Wazza OS MCP tool](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/mcp-tools.html).

## How it fits together

Three words carry the whole manual: **the VM**, **tabs** and **Chats**.

- **The VM** (virtual machine) is a complete Ubuntu computer that Wazza OS starts, sizes and stops for you. Apps are installed in it, not on your computer, so they never touch your own files unless you hand them over. You can have up to 8 VMs (4 running at once); most people use one, `vm-1`.
- A **tab** shows one app of the VM (GIMP, Blender, a browser, the VM's file manager…) in the Wazza OS window. Tabs work like a browser's: open as many as you like, switch, close.
- A **Chat** sits beside each app, in its tab. You write to an **agent** (the AI program that works for you) and it works in that tab's app: through the app's own tools, or by looking at the app's window and using its mouse and keyboard ([Drive](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/drive.html)). A Chat can also start other agents in other tabs.

[Getting around](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/window.html) shows the window part by part; [Glossary](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/glossary.html) defines every word.

## Capabilities

Each card says what the capability is, why or when you would use it, and who it is for. The link opens the full page: how to do it step by step, every option, the limits and examples.

WhyEvery agent has its own window, mouse and keyboard: none waits for a shared screen, and you watch any of them, or keep using your own tab, without getting in the way.

WhoAnyone with a job that spans several apps: research plus a report, assets plus a game, data plus slides.

WhatThe VM takes memory when its apps need it and gives it back when idle, within a limit you can set (by default 75 % of the memory free); processors and disk follow the same rule.

- Written for **Wazza OS 0.2.0** (build 44c5d0ea07c1, published 2026-11-03). The screenshots come from a test computer (Ubuntu 24.04, GNOME) running Wazza OS 0.2.0: alpha 2 and the builds that followed it, whose screens are the same.
- Press `/` anywhere to search every page and heading; the search works offline.
- The sun and moon button switches between dark (the default, like the app) and light.
- Words in **bold** are what Wazza OS shows on screen: a button, a tab, a menu item. Home › Sign in › API keys means: open Home, then Sign in, then its API keys tab.

# Quick start

From nothing to an agent working in an app, in about ten minutes: install, start, give your agents a model, ask a first question, then let an agent work in an app while you watch.

## 1. Install Wazza OS

Paste this in a terminal, on the Linux computer where Wazza OS will live. It finds your package type, checks the release's signature and installs it; it asks for your password once, for `sudo`:

```
$ curl -fsSL https://os.wazza.ai/install.sh | sh
```

To test first, what your computer needs, or a package to download yourself: [Install, update, remove](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/install.html).

## 2. Start it

Open **Wazza OS** from your app menu. The first start shows six short steps (about two minutes): click **Get started**, check that every line of the computer check says *ok*, skip or fill the sign-in and agent steps, keep the default apps, and click **Set up Wazza OS**, then **Open Wazza OS**. Each step in detail: [The first start](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/first-start.html).

![The first start's welcome card with Get started](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/img/first-start-1-welcome.webp)

## 3. Give your agents a model

Agents think with an AI model, which someone pays for. Pick one way (you can add the others later):

- **A plan you already pay for** (Claude, ChatGPT, Grok, Google): Home › Sign in › Logins › **Log in with …**.
- **An API key**: Home › Sign in › API keys › **+ Add key** on the provider's card, paste the key, **Check and save**. An OpenRouter key opens hundreds of models, some of them free.
- **A Wazza OS account**: Home › Sign in › **Email and password**.

![Sign in, API keys tab, the OpenRouter card open with its Paste API key field and Check and save](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/img/signin-add-key.webp)

Adding an OpenRouter key: paste it, then **Check and save**.

Details: [Sign in, plans and API keys](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/signin.html).

## 4. Ask a first question

1. Click **+** at the end of the tab strip, then **Chat** (*Ask any agent*).
2. Type a request and press `Enter`. Try one that makes the agent work in the VM: *Create a file named hello.txt in my Documents folder with today's date in it, then show me its content.*

![The agent ran a command in the VM, created the file and showed its content](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/img/chat-answer.webp)

The agent ran a command in the VM (the *Bash* row), made the file and showed it.

The agent works in the VM: it can make files, run commands and use the web there, without touching your own computer. Everything about Chats: [Chats, agents and models](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/chats.html).

## 5. Let an agent work in an app

1. Click **+**, type *gimp* in **Search apps**, click **GIMP**. It installs (a minute or so), then opens in a new tab with its own Chat on the left.
2. In that Chat, ask: *Create a new 800 x 600 image with a dark teal background and write Hello from Wazza OS in large white letters in the middle.*
3. Watch GIMP on the right: the agent uses GIMP's own tools, then checks the result.

![The agent's answer and the image in GIMP with Hello from Wazza OS on a dark teal background](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/img/drive-gimp-result.webp)

More: [Apps and tabs](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/apps.html), and how agents use an app's window: [Drive](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/drive.html).

## 6. Go further

[

### Several agents at once

One request, several apps, each with its own agent working at the same time.

Read →](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/parallel-tabs.html) [

### Files and sharing

Bring your files into the VM and get results back on your computer.

Read →](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/files.html) [

### Skills

What agents know about each app, and how they learn from your Chats.

Read →](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/skills.html) [

### Settings

Theme, resources, defaults for new Chats, and every other option.

Read →](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/settings-general.html)

# Install, update, remove

Wazza OS installs with one command on any recent Linux, or as a package of your distribution. Start it from your app menu, and it sets up the rest (its VM, its apps, its agents) on its first start.

## What your computer needs

| Need | Why |
|---|---|
| Linux on a 64-bit Intel or AMD processor (x86-64), with glibc 2.39 or newer (Ubuntu 24.04, Debian 13, Fedora 40 and later, a current openSUSE Tumbleweed or Arch) | Wazza OS is built for it. |
| Hardware virtualization (Intel VT-x or AMD-V) turned on, so `/dev/kvm` exists | The VM runs only with KVM. Most computers have it; on some it must be turned on in the firmware settings (UEFI/BIOS). |
| A desktop session with systemd (GNOME, KDE, Xfce, Hyprland, Sway…), and XWayland on Wayland desktops | Wazza OS's window and the VM's panes are X11 windows. On a server with no desktop, see [On a server](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/cli-server.html). |
| Memory: 8 GB works (the computer of this manual's screenshots had 8 GB); 16 GB or more is comfortable for 3D apps and several agents at once | The VM takes memory as its apps need it and gives it back; Wazza OS always keeps 2 GB and 10 % of your memory for your computer itself ([Memory, CPU and disk](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/memory-cpu.html)). |
| Disk: about 8 GB for Wazza OS itself, plus room for the VM's disk (it grows as you use it, by default up to half of your free space) | The package holds the VM's system image. |
| A graphics card with its driver (Intel, AMD, or NVIDIA 495 or newer) | Apps in the VM draw on it. Without one the VM still works, with slower software graphics. |
| An Internet connection | For agents' models, installing apps in the VM, updates. |

After installing, `wazza --check` says exactly what your computer has and what is missing ([What is checked](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/first-start.html#what-is-checked)).

## Install with one command

Paste this in a terminal, on the Linux computer where Wazza OS will live. It asks for your password once, for `sudo`.

```
$ curl -fsSL https://os.wazza.ai/install.sh | sh
```

To test first, without installing anything:

```
$ curl -fsSL https://os.wazza.ai/install.sh | sh -s -- --check
```

| It… | How |
|---|---|
| finds your package type | Debian, Ubuntu and their family get the `.deb`. Fedora and openSUSE get the `.rpm`. Arch and its family get the Arch package. Any other distribution gets the tarball. |
| verifies the release | Nothing installs unless the release manifest carries Wazza's Ed25519 signature and the package matches its signed SHA-256 and size. |
| resumes if cut | The package is large (about 7 GB). If the download stops, run the command again: it continues where it stopped. |

It needs free disk for the package plus about 1 GB, and checks before it starts. It downloads into `/var/tmp/wazza-install` and leaves the package there (delete it to free the space); to use another folder, put `WAZZA_INSTALL_DIR=/some/big/folder` before `sh`. To choose the package type yourself, add it after `--`: `sh -s -- tar` (or `deb`, `rpm`, `arch`). When it is done, start Wazza OS from your applications menu.

## Or download a package yourself

The packages are on Wazza's release server, `os-downloads.wazza.ai` (its older name, `downloads.tadaah.ai`, serves the same files, and is the address Wazza OS's own updater uses). Each version has four packages of the same build, one per family of Linux:

| Your system | Package | Wazza OS 0.2.0 (build 44c5d0ea07c1, published 2026-11-03): file and SHA-256 |
|---|---|---|
| Ubuntu, Debian, Linux Mint, Pop!_OS and other Debian-based systems | `.deb` | [wazza-20261103T021245Z-11af2d7099e51d8e.deb](https://os-downloads.wazza.ai/download/0.2.0-git.z1793671965.44c5d0ea07c1/wazza-20261103T021245Z-11af2d7099e51d8e.deb); `11af2d7099e51d8ee03b6605de367fadac537a333c1524d40e3c075f04130517` |
| Fedora, openSUSE | `.rpm` | [wazza-20261103T021245Z-4b39800484873c92.rpm](https://os-downloads.wazza.ai/download/0.2.0-git.z1793671965.44c5d0ea07c1/wazza-20261103T021245Z-4b39800484873c92.rpm); `4b39800484873c92acbcea271710bccc89e6e5ff80960af431a1324d740482b0` |
| Arch, EndeavourOS, Omarchy and other Arch-based systems | `.pkg.tar.zst` | [wazza-20261103T021245Z-5225f3922628ec4e.pkg.tar.zst](https://os-downloads.wazza.ai/download/0.2.0-git.z1793671965.44c5d0ea07c1/wazza-20261103T021245Z-5225f3922628ec4e.pkg.tar.zst); `5225f3922628ec4edc9b9546e255a9a612d54c9bcc8401f31cbf8eded97cb2e7` |
| Any other Linux (glibc 2.39 or newer, systemd) | `.tar.zst` | [wazza-20261103T021245Z-edd1335e2c1bda8b.tar.zst](https://os-downloads.wazza.ai/download/0.2.0-git.z1793671965.44c5d0ea07c1/wazza-20261103T021245Z-edd1335e2c1bda8b.tar.zst); `edd1335e2c1bda8b0a5515622046f39344870701c81b9a5061dc8d9609b91f00` |

Each file is about 7 GB: it carries the VM's whole system, so the first start needs no further big download. For a newer version: `https://os-downloads.wazza.ai/latest` names the current version and the Debian package's address and SHA-256 (its `files[0].url`, relative to `https://os-downloads.wazza.ai`); the other three are in the same folder, `/download/<version>/`. In a terminal:

```
$ curl -s https://os-downloads.wazza.ai/latest
$ curl -LO https://os-downloads.wazza.ai/download/0.2.0-git.z1793671965.44c5d0ea07c1/wazza-20261103T021245Z-11af2d7099e51d8e.deb
$ sha256sum wazza-20261103T021245Z-11af2d7099e51d8e.deb
```

The SHA-256 printed must be the one in the table (or in `/latest`); if it differs, the download is damaged: download it again.

> You download a package only once. After the first install, Wazza OS updates itself from the [Update page](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/update.html): it checks for a new signed version every hour, and installing it is two clicks and your administrator password.

## Install a downloaded package

### Ubuntu and Debian

```
$ sudo apt install ./wazza-*.deb
```

Write the `./` in front: it tells apt to install that file, and apt installs what it needs with it (bubblewrap, ffmpeg, Openbox, Xvfb and the other dependencies).

### Fedora

```
$ sudo dnf install ./wazza-*.rpm
```

### openSUSE

```
$ sudo zypper install ./wazza-*.rpm
```

### Arch and Arch-based systems

```
$ sudo pacman -U ./wazza-*.pkg.tar.zst
```

### Any other Linux (tarball)

```
$ tar --zstd -xf wazza-*.tar.zst
$ cd wazza-os-*/
$ ./install.sh --check
$ sudo ./install.sh
```

`./install.sh --check` only lists what your system is missing (the commands and libraries Wazza OS needs: systemd, util-linux, Python 3, Xvfb, xauth, Openbox, D-Bus, FFmpeg, bubblewrap, slirp4netns, iproute2, OpenSSL, Git). Install those with your package manager, then `sudo ./install.sh` puts the files where the packages put them. It refuses while something is missing (`--force` installs anyway).

## Start Wazza OS

Open **Wazza OS** from your app menu (Activities, the application launcher, or the start menu of your desktop). Or, in a terminal of your desktop session, run one of these (they are the same program):

```
$ wazzaos
```

`wazza-os` and `wazza` work too. Only one Wazza OS runs per user: starting it again while it runs goes to the one already running. The very first start shows six setup steps: [The first start](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/first-start.html).

## Update Wazza OS

Three ways, all keep your VMs, Chats, sign-ins and settings:

- **From Wazza OS**: Home › Update shows a new version as soon as it is out (it checks every hour); click **Download Update**, then **Install Now** ([The Update page](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/update.html)).
- **With your package manager**: download the new package and install it exactly as above, over the installed one (`sudo apt install ./new.deb`, `sudo dnf install ./new.rpm`, `sudo pacman -U ./new.pkg.tar.zst`, or the new tarball's `sudo ./install.sh`). Then quit and start Wazza OS.
- **With the install command**: run it again ([Install with one command](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/install.html#install-with-one-command)): it installs the newest version over yours. Then quit and start Wazza OS.

> **Never uninstall to update**
>
> Removing the package deletes your Wazza OS data (below). To update, or to go back to an older version, install the other package over the one you have.

Going back to an older version is a downgrade: Debian and Ubuntu do it with `sudo apt install --allow-downgrades ./older.deb`; Fedora with `sudo dnf downgrade ./older.rpm`; Arch with `sudo pacman -U ./older.pkg.tar.zst`.

## Remove Wazza OS

> **Removing Wazza OS removes your Wazza OS data too**
>
> Every package's removal stops Wazza OS and its VMs, then deletes Wazza OS's data on this computer: the VMs' disks (and every file you made inside them), Chats, sign-ins and keys, settings, caches. Your own files outside Wazza OS (Documents, Downloads, Desktop…) stay, including `Downloads/From the VM` and VM backups. Back up a VM you want to keep first ([Virtual machines › Backups](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/settings-vms.html#backups)).

| System | Command |
|---|---|
| Ubuntu, Debian | `sudo apt remove wazza-os` |
| Fedora | `sudo dnf remove wazza-os` |
| openSUSE | `sudo zypper remove wazza-os` |
| Arch | `sudo pacman -R wazza-os` |
| Tarball | `sudo ./uninstall.sh` (in the unpacked folder) |
| Any of them | `sudo wazzaos --uninstall`: removes Wazza OS with the system that installed it (apt, dnf, zypper, pacman or the tarball's uninstaller), naming each folder it deletes with its size |

To erase Wazza OS's data but keep it installed (a fresh start), use [Settings › This computer › Remove all data](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/settings-computer.html#remove-all-data) instead.


---

Page: The first start (Start here)
Address: https://os-guide.wazza.ai/first-start.html

# The first start

The very first time you open Wazza OS, six short steps check your computer, offer to sign you in, ask which AI agents you use, let you pick your first apps and set up Wazza OS's own computer (its virtual machine). It takes about 2 minutes. Every later start takes about 1 minute and goes straight to your tabs.

- **When**: Only on the very first start of Wazza OS for your user account

- **How long**: About 2 minutes, most of it the VM's first boot

- **What you need**: Wazza OS installed and started from your desktop session ([Install](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/install.html))

- **Can I change it later?**: Yes: everything you pick here is in Home › Sign in and Home › Apps

Every step except the first has **Back**: you go to the step before with every choice kept. Nothing you pick in these steps is final, and you can skip everything that is optional (signing in, the agent logins, the extra apps): Wazza OS works without them, and you add them later.

![The Wazza OS window on its first start: the welcome card in the middle of an empty dark window](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/img/first-start-1-window.webp)

The first start in the Wazza OS window. While you go through the steps, Wazza OS already starts its virtual machine in the background, so the last step is often almost done when you reach it.

## Step 1: Welcome

The first card says what Wazza OS is: your apps and AI agents, in a computer of their own. Wazza OS runs its own Linux computer (a virtual machine, "the VM") next to yours. Agents work there, in your apps, with you, and they ask before anything reaches your real computer.

![Step 1 of 6: Your apps and AI agents, in a computer of their own, with the Apps, Agents and Safe tiles and the Get started button](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/img/first-start-1-welcome.webp)

Step 1 of 6.

1. The counter and the six bars at the top show where you are: **First start · step 1 of 6**.
2. Click **Get started**.

The three tiles sum up what you get: **Apps** (office, browser, creative, developer apps and more, installed in the VM), **Agents** (Claude Code, Codex, Hermes and more, working in those apps) and **Safe** (your files are copied into the VM only when you say so; see [Privacy and security](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/privacy-security.html)).

## Step 2: Checking this computer

Wazza OS checks, in a few seconds, the six things it needs to run its VM next to your computer. Each line shows what it found and **ok**, **limited** or **missing**. When something is not right, the line says what it means and how to fix it (a command to run, or a setting).

![Step 2 of 6: Checking this computer, a list of checks each marked ok: Hardware virtualization (KVM), systemd user session, X11 display (XWayland), Chat sandbox, Graphics driver, VM display buffers](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/img/first-start-2-check.webp)

Step 2 of 6 on a computer where everything is present. The list scrolls: the sixth check, VM display buffers, is below the fifth.

1. Each check has a mark: **✓** present, **!** limited (Wazza OS works with less), **✕** missing (something does not work until you fix it).
2. Its state in words on the right: **ok**, **limited** or **missing**.
3. Click **Continue** once the check has answered (the button stays grey while it runs).

### What is checked, and what to do when a line is not ok

| Check | Why Wazza OS needs it | When it is missing: the fix the check gives |
|---|---|---|
| Hardware virtualization (KVM) | Wazza OS's VMs run only with KVM. Without it they do not start. | Turn on Intel VT-x or AMD-V (SVM) in the computer's firmware settings (UEFI/BIOS), then restart. If `/dev/kvm` exists but your account cannot open it: `sudo usermod -aG kvm "$USER"`, then log out and back in. If the module is not loaded: `sudo modprobe kvm_intel` or `sudo modprobe kvm_amd`. Inside a VM: turn on nested virtualization in the computer that runs it. |
| systemd user session | Each VM runs in a memory-capped scope of your user's systemd manager. | Start Wazza OS from your desktop session (log in through the login screen), not from `su`, `sudo` or a bare SSH session. On a server: `loginctl enable-linger "$USER"` keeps your user manager running without a login (see [On a server](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/cli-server.html)). |
| X11 display (XWayland) | The Wazza OS window and the VM's panes are X11 windows; in a Wayland session that is XWayland. Without a display Wazza OS does not open (on a server, Wazza OS makes its own virtual screen). | Install your distribution's XWayland package, turn XWayland on in your compositor (Hyprland: `xwayland { enabled = true }`; Sway: `xwayland enable`), then log out and back in. |
| Chat sandbox | Every Chat that runs on your computer (not in the VM) runs inside Wazza OS's sandbox (bubblewrap and Landlock), or does not start. | On Ubuntu: `sudo apparmor_parser -r /etc/apparmor.d/wazza-bwrap` loads Wazza OS's AppArmor rule. If the kernel refuses user namespaces: `sudo sysctl -w kernel.unprivileged_userns_clone=1` (and the same line in `/etc/sysctl.d/60-wazza-userns.conf` to keep it). If the sandbox file is missing: reinstall Wazza OS. *Limited* means Chats run under Landlock alone, with less isolation. |
| Graphics driver | The VM draws its apps on your computer's graphics card. Without a usable card the VM starts with software graphics (slower), by itself. | Intel and AMD: the kernel's driver (i915/xe, amdgpu) with Mesa; NVIDIA: its driver 495 or newer with `sudo modprobe nvidia-drm`. If the card exists but your account cannot open it: `sudo usermod -aG render "$USER"`, then log out and back in. Or set [VM resources › Graphics › GPU](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/settings-resources.html#graphics) to **None (CPU only)**. |
| VM display buffers | The VM's picture travels over a socket that needs 4 MiB buffers. Below that, VMs do not start. | `sudo sysctl -w net.core.rmem_max=4194304 net.core.wmem_max=4194304`. The package installs `/usr/lib/sysctl.d/60-wazza.conf`, which sets it at every boot; reinstall Wazza OS if that file is missing. |

You can run the same check at any time: [Settings › This computer › Check](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/settings-computer.html#check), or in a terminal `wazza --check` (see [The command line](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/cli.html#check)).

> **Continue works even when a line is missing**
>
> The first start does not stop you. But a *missing* line means that part does not work (for example no KVM: the VM does not start). Fix it first, then click **Continue**.

## Step 3: Sign in to Wazza OS (optional)

A Wazza OS account keeps your Chats, skills and settings in sync between computers, and gives your agents Wazza OS's own models (Prime Agent uses them; new Chats start on MiMo once you are signed in). You can skip it and sign in later in [Home › Sign in](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/signin.html#your-wazza-os-account).

![Step 3 of 6: Sign in to Wazza OS, with Email and password, Log in / Sign up online, Back and Skip for now](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/img/first-start-3-signin.webp)

Step 3 of 6.

1. **Email and password** opens the sign-in form below the buttons, for an account you already have.
2. **Log in / Sign up online** asks where to open the website's sign-in (for a Google account, or to create an account).
3. **Skip for now** goes on without an account. The note at the bottom left reminds you: *You can sign in later in Home › Sign in*.

### Sign in with email and password

![The sign-in form with the Email and Password fields and the Sign in button](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/img/first-start-3-email.webp)

1. Type your account's email.
2. Type your password (Enter also signs in).
3. Click **Sign in**. The card says *Signing in…*, then *Signed in.*, and the next step comes by itself. A wrong password or a network problem is shown in red under the form, in the server's own words; the password field is emptied every time.

### Log in or sign up online

![Where should it open? In the VM's browser (offered once the VM is ready) or On this computer](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/img/first-start-3-online.webp)

1. **In the VM's browser**: the website's own sign-in page opens in Wazza OS's private sign-in tab, where you log in or sign up with your email or Google; you are signed in by itself. The VM must be running for this, so during the first start the button says *Offered once the VM is ready*. When you pick it, the card notes that *the online sign-in opens in Wazza OS's private sign-in tab once your computer is set up* and goes on to the next step.
2. **On this computer**: your own browser opens Wazza OS's Google sign-in. When you land on the last page, copy its address from the browser's address bar and paste it in the field Wazza OS shows, then finish. To sign up or log in with an email instead, do it on the website, come back, and use **Email and password**.

## Step 4: Which agents do you use? (optional)

If you already pay for an AI plan, Wazza OS can use it: you log in once and your agents use your plan, with no API key. This step only notes which logins you want; each one opens after the setup, in Home › Sign in.

![Step 4 of 6: Which agents do you use? Claude, ChatGPT, Grok, Google, OpenRouter and Nous Portal, each with a Log in with button](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/img/first-start-4-agents.webp)

Step 4 of 6.

1. Click **Log in with …** for each plan you have. The button turns into **✓ After setup**; click it again to take it back.
2. Click **Continue**.

| Login | Plan it uses | Which agents can use it |
|---|---|---|
| Claude | Free, Pro or Max plan | Claude Code only |
| ChatGPT | Plus or Pro plan | Every agent: Codex, Hermes and Prime Agent with their own sign-in; Claude Code and Antigravity through Wazza OS's gateway |
| Grok | SuperGrok or X Premium+ | Every agent |
| Google | Your Google account plan | Antigravity only |
| OpenRouter | Your OpenRouter account | Every agent |
| Nous Portal | Your Nous Portal account | Hermes only |

The card also says *Hermes and Prime Agent work right away*: they need no login of their own. They still need a model to talk to: a Wazza OS account, one of these plans, or an API key. The published Wazza OS includes no shared key, so without any of the three a Chat has no model; see [Sign in, plans and API keys](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/signin.html).

## Step 5: Pick your first apps

The apps you check here are installed in the VM while it starts. You can install any other app later from [Home › Apps](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/apps.html#install-an-app).

![Step 5 of 6: Pick your first apps, a grid of apps; Git, GPU for apps, OSM places and routes, Search and Sound card drivers are already checked](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/img/first-start-5-apps.webp)

Step 5 of 6. The grid scrolls: every app of the catalog is in it.

1. The apps with a light border are Wazza OS's own defaults: they are always installed and cannot be unchecked (Git, GPU for apps: Vulkan, OpenCL and OpenGL support, OSM places and routes, Search, Sound card drivers; Wazza OS also installs the ffmpeg media tools with them).
2. Click any other app to add it (click again to take it back).
3. The number of apps in the catalog (71 in this version).
4. Click **Set up Wazza OS**.

> Each app you add takes time and disk space in the VM. Pick only what you will use today: every app stays one click away in Home › Apps.

## Step 6: Setting up your computer

The last card follows the VM's start, stage by stage, each with the time it took.

![Step 6 of 6: Setting up your computer, five stages each with a check mark and its time, and the Open Wazza OS button](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/img/first-start-6-setup.webp)

Step 6 of 6, all stages done. Here the system's first boot took 1 min 27 s; it was running while the steps before were on screen.

The stages, in order:

  - **Getting ready**: Wazza OS prepares the VM's disk and settings.
  - **Starting the virtual machine**: the VM is switched on.
  - **Starting the system**: the VM's Linux boots (the longest stage on a first start).
  - **Starting the desktop**: the VM's desktop, where your apps draw, comes up.
  - **Connecting Wazza OS**: Wazza OS connects to the VM (its files, apps and Chats).
2. Click **Open Wazza OS**. Before the VM is ready the button says *Opens when your computer is ready…*: click it anyway and Wazza OS opens by itself as soon as it is.

Wazza OS then opens [Home](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/window.html#home) on **Apps**, or on **Sign in** when you picked a sign-in or a login in steps 3 and 4 (each login you picked waits there for you). The apps you picked keep installing in the background; each one sends a notification when it is done ([Home › Notifications](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/window.html#notifications)).

## After the first start

- Every later start shows only the startup card (the stages of step 6) and then your tabs as you left them.
- Open a Chat and talk to an agent: [Quick start](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/quick-start.html).
- Connect a model if you skipped steps 3 and 4: [Sign in, plans and API keys](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/signin.html).

## Run the first start again

To see the six steps again without losing anything, run this in a terminal while Wazza OS is open, then quit and start Wazza OS:

```
$ wazza --gui setup reset-first-run
first start not done: Wazza OS shows its first start at its next start
```

Your VMs, Chats, apps and sign-ins stay. To start from nothing instead (every VM, Chat, sign-in and setting erased), use [Settings › This computer › Remove all data](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/settings-computer.html#remove-data).

On a computer you set up from a script (or many computers), `wazza --gui setup run --file setup.json` does the same choices without clicks: see [The command line](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/cli.html#set-up-without-clicks).
