Page: Getting around (Start here)
Address: https://os-guide.wazza.ai/window.html

# Getting around

The Wazza OS window has a tab strip at the top and the tab you are on below it. One tab is special: Home, with its menu on the left (Apps, Settings, Sign in, History, Update, Notifications, Feedback). Every other tab shows one app of the VM with its own Chat beside it.

## The window

![The Wazza OS window on Home, Apps page: the tab strip at the top, the Home menu on the left with the account card and the VM card at its bottom, and the Apps catalog on the right](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/img/home-apps-full.webp)

Home open on Apps, right after the first start.

1. **Explorer**: opens the side panel with the VM's files ([below](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/window.html#the-explorer)).
2. **Tabs**: one per open app (and Home). Click one to show it; drag one to move it.
3. **+** (**Show apps**): opens Home on Apps, to open or install an app.
4. **Desktop menu**: fold the Chat or the app, lock input, pop out, full screen, frame rate ([below](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/window.html#the-desktop-menu)). Grey on Home, where there is no app.
5. **Window buttons**: minimize, maximize, close. Closing the window quits Wazza OS and stops its VMs (your tabs come back at the next start).
6. **Home menu**: Apps, Settings, Sign in, History, Update, Notifications (with the number of unread ones), Feedback. Below 1024 px of width it becomes a column of icons.
7. **Account card**: *Not signed in*, or the Wazza OS account you are signed in with. A click opens Sign in.
8. **VM card**: the VM this window shows, live ([below](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/window.html#the-vm-card)).
9. **The page** of the Home menu item you picked (here Apps).

## Home

Home is the tab of Wazza OS itself. It opens on the page you pick in its menu; each page opens in the same Home tab (the tab's name follows the page: Applications, Settings, Sign in…).

| Home menu item | What it is | Page |
|---|---|---|
| Apps | Every app you can open or install, by category, with search and **Add app** | [Apps and tabs](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/apps.html) |
| Settings | Eight pages of settings | [Settings](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/settings-general.html) |
| Sign in | Your Wazza OS account, plan logins, API keys, custom APIs, web apps | [Sign in](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/signin.html) |
| History | Your past tabs and Chats, to search and reopen | [below](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/window.html#history) |
| Update | A newer version of Wazza OS | [The Update page](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/update.html) |
| Notifications | Everything Wazza OS told you | [below](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/window.html#notifications) |
| Feedback | Tell the Wazza team what went wrong | [below](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/window.html#feedback) |

### The VM card

The card at the bottom left of Home, live while Home is open:

- the VM's name and state (*vm-1 · running*);
- **CPU**: how busy the VM's processors are;
- **RAM**: the memory the VM uses, of the most it may take now (*0.9 / 5.8 GB*);
- how that limit is set (*Auto: 75% of the memory free now, never below 5.8 GB, so 5.8 GB now*; see [VM resources › Memory](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/settings-resources.html#memory));
- the graphics the VM's apps get (*OpenGL 4.2 · virgl (…)*: your graphics card, through virtualization).

## Tabs

A tab shows one app of the VM, with its Chat beside it: the agent of that Chat works in that app. Tabs keep running when you switch away: an app keeps working and its agent keeps going in the background.

![A GIMP tab: the Chat on the left with its composer and the agent and model chip, GIMP on the right](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/img/window-tab-layout.webp)

A GIMP tab, just after GIMP was installed and opened.

1. The tab, named after its app, then after the first thing you ask its Chat.
2. The tab's **Chat** ([Chats, agents and models](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/chats.html)).
3. The divider: drag it to give the Chat or the app more room. Which side the Chat is on is a setting ([General › Chat side](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/settings-general.html#tabs-and-layout)).
4. The **app**, live from the VM. Click into it and use it as on your own computer: your mouse and keyboard go to the app while the pointer is over it.
5. The composer, where you write to the agent.
6. The agent and model this Chat uses (a click opens the model window).

### Open, switch and close tabs

- **Open**: click **+**, then an app on the Apps page (or ask a Chat to open one). An app that is not installed yet installs first, then opens ([Install an app](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/apps.html#install-an-app)).
- **Switch**: click a tab. A tab an agent opened in the background carries a badge until you look at it.
- **Close**: the **×** on the tab. Its app is asked to close (it may ask you to save).
- **Reopen**: a closed tab is in [History](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/window.html#history).

### The tab card

![The card shown when hovering a tab: its title, GIMP, VM vm-1, Shown, RAM 174 MB, CPU 0% (app 130 MB, Chat 44 MB), and a small picture of the tab](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/img/window-tab-hover.webp)

Hold the pointer over a tab: a card shows its full name, its app and VM, what it uses now (memory and CPU, split between the app and its Chat) and a small picture of it.

### The tab menu

![The tab menu opened by a right-click on a tab: Add to favourites, Reload, Move to new window, Group: Add tab to new group, Sound: Mute tab and Volume 100%](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/img/window-tab-menu.webp)

Right-click a tab:

| Item | What it does |
|---|---|
| Add to favourites | Keeps the tab in History › Favourites, to reopen it in one click. |
| Reload | Restarts the tab's app (when it stopped answering, for example). |
| Move to new window | Moves the tab into a new Wazza OS window; its app and its Chat go on there. |
| Group › Add tab to new group | Puts the tab in a named, coloured group (type a name, pick a colour); the group's own menu adds tabs or **Ungroup**s them (they stay open). |
| Sound › Mute tab, Volume | Only what you hear from this tab. An agent working in it still hears the app. Only the tab you are on is heard. |
| Close tab | (on tabs that can be closed) Closes it; its app is asked to close. |

### Many tabs

When the strip is full, tabs shrink to their icons, then fold into one square that shows how many there are: click the square to see every tab and pick one. How many tabs show before they fold: [General › Tabs shown before they fold](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/settings-general.html#tabs-and-layout).

## The Desktop menu

![The Desktop menu: View: Fold Chat, Fold Desktop; Desktop: Lock input, Pop out, Full screen; FPS](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/img/window-desktop-menu.webp)

The button at the top right, left of the window buttons, on an app tab:

| Item | What it does |
|---|---|
| Fold Chat / Show Chat | Hides this tab's Chat to give the app the whole width (and back). |
| Fold Desktop / Show Desktop | Hides the app to give the Chat the whole width (and back). |
| Lock input / Unlock input | Locked, your clicks and keys no longer reach the app: watch an agent work without getting in its way. |
| Pop out | Shows the app in its own window, which you can move to another screen. Closing that window puts it back in its tab. |
| Full screen | The app fills the screen (a square at its top right opens this menu again, to leave full screen). |
| FPS | Shows the live frame rate of the app's picture, at the corner of the app. |

## The Explorer

![The Explorer panel: VM 1, Home, New file, New folder, Paste here, view buttons, and the list of the VM's home folder with names, dates, types and sizes](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/img/window-explorer.webp)

The button at the far left of the tab strip opens the Explorer over the Chat: the files of the VM (its home folder), with **New file**, **New folder**, **Paste here**, the views (list, grid, pictures, details), reload and close. Pick another running VM at the top. Double-click a file to open it in its app, in a new tab. More in [Files and sharing › The Explorer](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/files.html#the-explorer).

## History

![The History page: search tabs and chats; All, Chats, Tabs, Favourites; 0 favourites, 0 recent tabs; No workstation history yet](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/img/history-page.webp)

History before any tab was closed.

Every tab and Chat you had, by day, with its time. Filter with **All**, **Chats**, **Tabs** or **Favourites**, or type in **Search tabs and chats** (it searches names, VMs, apps and the lines of Chats). On each entry: its star (favourite), **Open** (reopens the tab, with its Chat), and **×** (deletes the entry).

## Notifications

![The Notifications page: Mark all read, Clear; filters All 10, Needs you 0, Updates 0, Agents 9; notifications of package installs completed, the VM processors notice, Sandbox guest is ready](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/img/notifications-page.webp)

Notifications after the first start: the default packages installed, the VM ready.

Everything Wazza OS told you, newest first, each with its time and the VM and tab it concerns. Short notices also appear for a few seconds at the bottom right of the window. Filters: **All**, **Needs you** (something waits for your answer), **Updates**, **Agents**. **Mark all read** clears the count on the Home menu. A notification with an action (for example **Open owning tab**) does it in one click.

## Feedback

![The Feedback page: Tell us what went wrong, a text box, Attach image, Send feedback](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/img/feedback-page.webp)

Tell the Wazza team what went wrong: what happened and what you expected. You may add one image (PNG, JPEG or WebP, at most 5 MB): drop it on the box, paste it, or **Attach image**. Click **Send feedback**. It is sent without your account; Wazza OS adds only its version.


---

Page: Chats, agents and models (Work with agents)
Address: https://os-guide.wazza.ai/chats.html

# Chats, agents and models

A Chat is where you talk to an agent: an AI program that does the work you ask in the VM, in the app of its tab, with its files and its command line. You pick the agent and the model it thinks with, and you can switch both in the middle of a Chat without losing the conversation.

> A Chat needs a model. With the published Wazza OS, add an API key, log in with a plan you have, or sign in to a Wazza OS account first: [Sign in, plans and API keys](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/signin.html). The screenshots on this page use an OpenRouter key added in Sign in.

## Open a Chat

- **A Chat on its own**: **+** › Apps › **Chat** (*Ask any agent*), the first of the Main apps. The tab is all Chat, for questions, files and command-line work in the VM.
- **A Chat next to an app**: every app tab has its own Chat on its left ([Tabs](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/window.html#tabs)). Its agent works in that app.

A new Chat starts with the default agent and model of [Settings › Chats & agents › New Chats](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/settings-chats.html#new-chats). The line above the composer says what it starts on when no default is saved.

## Write to the agent

![The composer of a new Chat: the line about the default model, the box Ask anything, or @ a file or app, the plus button, the agent and model chip Hermes, and the send button](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/img/chat-composer.webp)

The composer at the bottom of a Chat.

1. Type in **Ask anything, or @ a file or app…**. `Enter` sends; `Shift`+`Enter` starts a new line.
2. **+** adds files to your message (below).
3. The agent and model of this Chat; a click opens the [model window](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/chats.html#choose-the-agent-and-the-model).
4. Send. While the agent answers, this button becomes **Stop**.

### Add files

![The plus menu: Add to this message, From this computer (asks first), From the VM's files (vm-1)](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/img/chat-attach-menu.webp)

- **From this computer…**: your computer's file chooser opens (*asks first*: nothing is sent before you pick). The files you pick are copied into the VM for the agent and attached to your message.
- **From the VM's files…**: the Explorer opens on this Chat's VM; drag files from it onto the Chat. They are attached by their path in the VM: nothing is copied. Known issue in the published build (0.2.0): that drag is not attached yet (fixed in the next release); type `@` and pick the file instead ([below](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/chats.html#mention-a-file-or-an-app)).
- Or drop files from your file manager on the Chat, or paste them or an image: every way is in [Move files](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/files-move.html).

### Mention a file or an app

![Typing @ in the composer lists the VM's folders: wazza_os, Documents, Music, Pictures, Templates, Videos, each with its path in the VM](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/img/chat-mentions.webp)

Type `@`: a list of the VM's files and folders (and apps) opens; keep typing to narrow it, then pick one with the arrows and `Enter` or a click. The agent gets its exact path. *wazza_os* is the folder the VM shares with Wazza OS ([Files and sharing](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/files.html)).

### Slash commands

![Typing slash in the composer lists the agent's commands: /help, /model, /tools, /context, /reset, /compress](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/img/chat-slash-commands.webp)

Type `/` at the start of the box: the agent's own commands. They differ per agent; for Hermes: `/help` (list the commands), `/model` (show or switch the model), `/tools` (list its tools), `/context` (message counts), `/reset` (clear the conversation), `/compress` (sum up the conversation to save room), and more down the list.

## Follow the agent's work

![Your message: Create a file named hello.txt in my Documents folder with today's date in it, then show me its content, with the retry, copy, edit and delete buttons under it](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/img/chat-user-message.webp)

![The answer from OpenRouter (your key in Sign In), xiaomi/mimo-v2.6-flash: Thinking, a Bash row (mkdir -p ~/Documents + 2 commands) answering 2026-11-02, the message Created /home/ubuntu/Documents/hello.txt with a code block and a preview card of hello.txt, and the reply's buttons](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/img/chat-answer.webp)

An agent created a file in the VM and showed it.

1. Your message. Its buttons: **retry** (ask again), **copy**, **edit** (change it and send again), **delete**.
2. Who answers: the provider and the route (here *OpenRouter (your key in Sign In)*) and the model.
3. **Thinking**: the model's reasoning, folded (click to read it).
4. A **tool** the agent used: here *Bash*, its commands and what they printed. Tools of the app, of Wazza OS and of Drive show the same way.
5. The **message**: the answer, with code blocks (copy button) and previews of files it made.
6. A **preview** of a file in the VM: click to open it larger.
7. The answer's buttons: **copy**, **copy as an image**, **retry**, **fork** (a new Chat that starts from here), **delete**.

- **Stop**: the send button while the agent works. It stops the turn; the Chat says *Stopped.*
- **Write while it works**: what you send then waits in a queue and goes when the turn ends.
- **The tab name** becomes your first message, so you find the Chat again in the tab strip and in History.
- **The context meter** (*2% context*, bottom right) shows how full the model's memory of this Chat is ([Compact a long Chat](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/chats.html#compact-a-long-chat)).

## Choose the agent and the model

Click the agent and model chip (bottom left of the Chat). The model window opens on **Model**.

![The model window, Model tab: Apply to This chat or Default for new chats; the Agent list (Hermes default, Prime Agent, Claude Code, Codex, Antigravity, each with what it runs on); Search models with 407 models; models through Wazza OS's gateway, MiMo-V2.6-Flash selected, each OpenRouter API key, yours; Thinking On Off; Provider Auto; Refresh list; Use Hermes MiMo-V2.6-Flash](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/img/chat-model-window.webp)

The model window of a Chat on Hermes with an OpenRouter key. Under each agent: what it runs on (your OpenRouter key or your own keys, a plan, your Google account).

1. **Apply to**: **This chat**, or **Default for new chats** (the same as Settings › New Chats).
2. The **agent** (*default* marks the one new Chats use). Under each: what it needs.
3. **Search models**: type part of a name (for example *mimo*, *claude*, *free*); the count says how many match.
4. The **models** this agent can use now, grouped by how it reaches them (*Through Wazza OS's gateway*; your plans; your custom APIs), each with who pays (*OpenRouter API key · yours*). Grey rows say why they cannot be used with this agent.
5. **Thinking** **On**/**Off**: whether the model reasons before answering (better on hard tasks, slower and costlier). Shown only for models that can.
6. **Provider**: for an OpenRouter model, **Auto (Wazza OS's routing)** or one company that serves it.
7. **Refresh list** reads the models again (after you added a key, for example).
8. **Use …** applies it. Switching keeps the conversation: the new agent reads it from the start.

![The model search with mimo typed: 5 of 388 models, MiMo-V2.6-Pro, MiMo-V2.6-Flash, MiMo-V2.6-Pro-UltraSpeed, MiMo-V2.5-Pro, each through an OpenRouter API key, yours](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/img/chat-model-search.webp)

Searching *mimo*.

### The agents

| Agent | What it is | What it needs |
|---|---|---|
| Hermes | Nous Research's open agent, Wazza OS's default. Runs in the VM, works with any model. | A model: an API key, a plan login that reaches it, a custom API, or a Wazza OS account. |
| Prime Agent | Wazza OS's own agent, built in; works with any model. | The same. |
| Claude Code | Anthropic's coding agent. | Your Claude plan (Log in with Claude), or any model through Wazza OS's gateway. |
| Codex | OpenAI's coding agent. | Your ChatGPT plan (Log in with ChatGPT), or any model through the gateway. |
| Antigravity | Google's agent. Installed the first time you pick it (*not installed* until then). | Your Google account plan (Log in with Google). |

Every agent gets the same Wazza OS tools (apps, Drive, files, other agents): see [The Wazza OS MCP](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/mcp.html).

## Compact a long Chat

![The Info and compact tab: context 25.7k of 1.1M tokens, 2%; Compact the conversation with Compact now and New chat from a summary; Compact at 80k tokens with Set; Use in this chat: tokens in, tokens out, cache hit, speed, answers, paid by OpenRouter API key](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/img/chat-info-compact.webp)

The model window's **Info & compact** tab.

A model remembers a limited amount of a conversation (its *context window*). The tab shows how much of it this Chat uses (*25.7k of 1.1M tokens*), and:

- **Compact now**: the agent sums up what was said and goes on with less (Hermes uses its `/compress`, Claude Code, Codex and Prime Agent their `/compact`).
- **New chat from a summary**: a new Chat that starts from a summary of this one.
- **Compact at … tokens** › **Set**: compact by itself at that size (default 80k tokens, 50 % of the window, or the agent's own rule).
- **Use in this chat**: tokens in and out, cache hits, speed, answers, and who pays. Claude Code and Codex do not report tokens: for them the numbers are Wazza OS's estimate, marked *estimated*.

## Chat settings

![Chat settings, This chat: Learning in this chat switch on, Learn from this chat now with Learn](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/img/chat-settings-top.webp)

| Option | What it does |
|---|---|
| Learning in this chat (default: on) | What this Chat teaches can become a skill ([How Wazza OS learns](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/skills.html#how-wazza-os-learns)). Turn it off for a private or throwaway Chat. |
| Learn from this chat now | **Learn** reviews this Chat now instead of waiting. |
| Persona | None, or a persona (3D artist (Blender), Film director…): its skills load in this Chat, and the persona learns from it ([Personas](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/skills.html#personas)). |

![What the chat shows: Messages Unfolded, Thinking Folded, Tools Folded, Shell Folded, Previews Unfolded, Text size Default 80 percent, Font Default](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/img/chat-settings-shows.webp)

| What the chat shows | Values (default in bold) |
|---|---|
| Messages | **Unfolded**, Folded, Hidden |
| Thinking | Unfolded, **Folded**, Hidden |
| Tools | Unfolded, **Folded**, Hidden |
| Shell | Unfolded, **Folded**, Hidden |
| Previews | **Unfolded**, Hidden |
| Text size | Small, **Default**, Large, or a percentage |
| Font | **Default**, System, Mono |

![Export .md .html .txt .json, Fork: hover a reply, Delete this chat](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/img/chat-settings-foot.webp)

- **Export**: the whole Chat as Markdown, HTML, plain text or JSON, saved on your computer.
- **Fork**: hold the pointer over a reply and click its fork button: a new Chat starts from there.
- **Delete this chat**: deletes the conversation for good (it asks first).

## What an agent can do

- Work in the VM: read and write its files, run commands, install command-line tools, browse the web with its own tools. A Chat in the VM runs its tools without asking each time (Wazza OS has no ask mode); the VM is its own computer, separate from yours.
- Work in its tab's app: through the app's own tools (GIMP, Blender, ONLYOFFICE, the browser…) or by looking and clicking ([Drive](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/drive.html)).
- Start other agents in other apps' tabs, at the same time ([Several agents at once](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/parallel-tabs.html)).
- Reach your own computer only as you allow: it can find and read your files (below your home folder), copy them into its VM and put its results on your computer ([its file tools](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/files-move.html#a-chat-in-a-vm-tab)). These copies follow your rules in [Settings › Files & sharing](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/settings-files.html#between-this-computer-and-vms) (into the VM: allowed by default; out of it: Wazza OS asks you), and seeing or using your screen needs [Computer Control](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/computer-control.html).

## From the command line

```
$ wazza --gui chat-transcript --tab t5 --last 4
$ wazza --gui chat-model set openrouter/xiaomi/mimo-v2.6-flash
$ wazza --gui chat-queue list --tab t5
```

Reading a Chat, setting the default model, the queued messages: [The command line › Chats](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/cli.html#chats).


---

Page: Several agents at once (Work with agents)
Address: https://os-guide.wazza.ai/parallel-tabs.html

# Several agents at once

One Chat can hand parts of a job to other agents. An agent that works in an app gets its own tab, with that app and its own Chat: a browser for research, GIMP for an image, an editor for code. They work at the same time, in the background, while you watch any of them or keep working in your own tab.

- **What**: Visible agents, each in its own app tab; hidden agents for background work

- **Why**: Every agent has its own window, mouse and keyboard: no one waits for a shared screen

- **Who**: Anyone with a job that spans several apps

- **Limit**: 4 visible agents per Chat at once, fewer when the VM is short of memory

## Why each agent gets its own tab

An agent that works an app by its window needs that window, a pointer and a keyboard. With one shared screen, agents would take turns: while one types in a form, another cannot click in its app. In Wazza OS every app tab has its own picture of its app and its own input, so each agent drives its own app at full speed, and you see each one in its tab exactly as it works. Your own tab stays yours: new tabs open in the background, and nothing an agent does changes what you are looking at.

## Two kinds of helper agents

|  | Visible agent | Hidden agent |
|---|---|---|
| For | Work in an app's window you would want to watch: research in Chromium, an image in GIMP, a document in ONLYOFFICE, code in VSCodium, a scene in Blender | Background work with no window: a web search with its own tools, a calculation, a file conversion, a summary, a check |
| Where | A new tab of that app (or an idle tab of it you already have), with its own Chat | No tab: a Chat of its own behind the scenes |
| What you see | The tab in the strip, grouped with the Chat that started it, with a badge until you look | Its progress in the Chat that started it |
| When it ends | When it answered: its tab closes and its app ends (your Chat tells it to save its file first), unless it was asked to leave the result open | When it answered |

An app that is not installed is installed first, then its agent starts (about a minute more).

## Ask for several agents

1. In any Chat, describe the jobs and say they can run at the same time, one app each. Name the apps when it matters. For example: *Do these two jobs at the same time, each by a visible agent in its own app tab: 1) in Chromium, open en.wikipedia.org and tell me the title of today's featured article; 2) in GIMP, make a 400 x 300 image with a blue circle in the middle and save it as Pictures/circle.png. Tell me when both are done.*
2. The Chat starts one task per app (tool rows *workspace_app_task*), and the new tabs appear in the strip, grouped with your Chat.
3. Click a helper's tab to watch it: its Chat shows the precise instructions your Chat wrote for it, and its app shows the work.
4. Each helper's answer comes back to your Chat by itself (as a message from that tab); your Chat then reports, as you asked.

![The tab strip: the Chat's tab, chromium: today's featured article and gimp: blue circle image, framed together as one group with a badge 3](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/img/parallel-group-tabs.webp)

The Chat's tab and its two helpers' tabs (*chromium: today's featured article*, *gimp: blue circle image*), framed together as one group; the badge counts the group's tabs.

![The helper's Chromium tab: its Chat on the left with the instruction written by the first Chat (Open en.wikipedia.org in the browser, find the Today's featured article section and report the exact title) and its tools chromium_navigate and chromium_read_page; Chromium on the right showing Wikipedia's main page with From today's featured article](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/img/parallel-chromium-agent.webp)

The helper agent's own tab.

1. The instruction your Chat wrote for this helper: precise, self-contained.
2. The helper uses its app's own tools (here Chromium's: open a page, read it).
3. The app, live: Wikipedia's main page with today's featured article.

## Limits

- **4 visible agents per Chat at once.** A fifth is refused until one has answered; the Chat waits, then starts it.
- **Memory comes first.** Past the first helper, no visible agent starts while the VM is short of memory and cannot grow. The Chat is told why, and starts the next helper when one ends. On the 8 GB test computer of these screenshots, the GIMP helper therefore waited for the Chromium one:

![The Chat's tool rows: workspace_app_task(chromium) accepted; workspace_app_task(gimp) refused with visible_agent_limit: this VM is low on memory and cannot grow now, and 1 visible agent(s) of this Chat are at work; a short wait; the same refusal again](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/img/parallel-refusal.webp)

The second helper refused for memory: the Chat waits and starts it once the first one answers.

- To run more agents at once: give the VM more room ([VM resources › Memory](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/settings-resources.html#memory)), close tabs you no longer need, or use a computer with more memory (16 GB or more).
- A helper's tab is a normal tab: you can click in it, stop its Chat, or close it (which ends that helper).
- A helper never closes the tab of the Chat that started it, and never changes the tab you look at.

## More ways to work in parallel

| Ask your Chat to… | What happens |
|---|---|
| keep a helper for follow-ups | The helper stays (its tab too) after its first answer, so your Chat can send it more work, until your Chat ends it. |
| leave the result open | The helper's tab stays open with its result (a video playing, a document) for you to see; its Chat ends. |
| use another tab's Chat | Your Chat writes to the Chat of another tab you opened; each message shows in that Chat with where it came from. |
| repeat something later | Your Chat schedules a message to itself for later, or every N minutes, even after a restart. |
| run a crew | Your Chat plans a team of agents and keeps a record of the plan, the agents and the messages they exchanged. |

From a terminal, the same: `wazza --gui schedule list`, `wazza --gui crew-run --tab t5`, `wazza --gui tool-queue list` ([The command line › Chats](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/cli.html#chats)).


---

Page: Sign in, plans and API keys (Work with agents)
Address: https://os-guide.wazza.ai/signin.html

# Sign in, plans and API keys

An agent needs a model to talk to, and a model needs someone who pays for it. Wazza OS gives your agents models in four ways: your Wazza OS account, a plan you already pay for (log in once), an API key, or any compatible API (a company gateway, a model on your own computer). All of it is on one page: Home › Sign in.

> **The published Wazza OS has no built-in key**
>
> Since alpha 2, Wazza OS ships no shared OpenRouter key. Until you add one of the four, a Chat has no model to answer with. The quickest start: an OpenRouter key (it reaches hundreds of models, several of them free) or a plan login you already have. A Chat on Hermes with none of them answers at once: *Add an OpenRouter key under Sign In › API keys, or sign in to your Wazza account*.

## Which way is for you

| You have… | Use | What your agents get |
|---|---|---|
| A Claude, ChatGPT, Grok or Google AI plan | [Logins](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/signin.html#logins) | The plan's models, at no extra cost, within the plan's limits. |
| An account with an AI provider (OpenRouter, OpenAI, Anthropic, Google AI Studio, DeepSeek, Mistral…) | [API keys](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/signin.html#api-keys) | That provider's models, billed to your account with them. |
| A company AI gateway, or a model running on your computer (Ollama, LM Studio, vLLM…) | [Custom API](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/signin.html#custom-api) | The models that endpoint serves. |
| A Wazza OS account | [Your Wazza OS account](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/signin.html#your-wazza-os-account) | Wazza OS's models (new Chats start on MiMo), Prime Agent's models, and sync of your Chats, skills and settings. |

## Open Sign in

Click **Sign in** in the Home menu (or the account card at the bottom left of Home). The page has your Wazza OS account at the top, then four tabs: **Logins**, **API keys**, **Custom API**, **Web apps**. At the bottom, **Tokens by model** › **Show** lists the tokens each model used.

## Your Wazza OS account

The card at the top: *Keeps your Chats, skills and settings in sync, and adds Wazza OS models to every agent.*

- **Email and password**: the form for an account you have.
- **Log in / Sign up online**: asks where to open the website: **In the VM's browser** (Wazza OS's private sign-in tab; log in or sign up with your email or Google; you are signed in by itself) or **On this computer** (your own browser opens the Google sign-in; paste back the address you land on). The same choices as in [the first start](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/first-start.html#log-in-or-sign-up-online).

Earlier versions signed you in on a test website by default; Wazza OS now uses wazza.ai alone. After an update from one of them it says once, as a notice: *Wazza OS now uses wazza.ai: sign in again*. Sign in with this card.

Once signed in, the account card at the bottom left of Home shows your name instead of *Not signed in*. Sync of your files and Chat history is then turned on in [Settings › Sync & team](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/settings-sync.html).

## Logins

![Sign in page, Logins tab: cards for Claude, ChatGPT, Grok, Google, OpenRouter and Nous Portal, each with its plan, which agents it works in, Not signed in, and a Log in with button](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/img/signin-tab-1.webp)

Home › Sign in › Logins, nothing signed in yet.

1. Open the **Logins** tab.
2. Click **Log in with …** on the plan you have. The provider's own sign-in page opens in Wazza OS's private sign-in tab; sign in there as usual.
3. The card then says *Signed in* with the account. Each card says which agents can use it:

| Login | Plan | Works in |
|---|---|---|
| Claude | Free, Pro or Max plan | Claude Code only |
| ChatGPT | Plus or Pro plan | Codex, Hermes and Prime Agent with their own sign-in; Claude Code and Antigravity through Wazza OS's gateway |
| Grok | SuperGrok or X Premium+ | Every agent |
| Google | Your Google account plan | Antigravity only |
| OpenRouter | Your OpenRouter account | Every agent (the login gives Wazza OS an OpenRouter key of yours) |
| Nous Portal | Your Nous Portal account | Hermes only |

A login can hold **several accounts**: when one runs out (its plan's limit), the next takes over. Each account shows its state: *In use*, *Ready*, *Empty · back at* (with the time it comes back), *Paused* or *Refused*. See [Several keys or accounts](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/signin.html#several-keys-or-accounts).

## API keys

![Sign in page, API keys tab: search 73 providers, and a card per provider (OpenRouter, ChatGPT / OpenAI, Claude / Anthropic, Grok / xAI, Google / Gemini, DeepSeek, Mistral, GitHub Copilot, AI21 and more), each with Add key and Get a key](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/img/signin-tab-2.webp)

Home › Sign in › API keys: 73 providers, the most used first, then A to Z.

1. Find the provider: the most used are first; or type its name in **Search 73 providers**.
2. Click **+ Add key** on its card.
3. No key yet? **Get a key ›** opens the provider's page where you create one.

![The OpenRouter card open for a key: OPENROUTER_API_KEY, a Paste API key field, Check and save, Cancel](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/img/signin-add-key.webp)

1. Paste the key in **Paste API key** (the field names the variable the key is known by, here `OPENROUTER_API_KEY`).
2. Click **Check and save**. Wazza OS checks the key with the provider, then keeps it. The card then shows the key by its last characters only (`sk-or-v1-…` and four characters) with its state, and **+ Add another … key**.

No restart is needed: a Chat that answered *Add an OpenRouter key…* starts again by itself once the key is saved (its agent shows *Setting up your key…* for a few seconds); then send your message again.

A key works in every agent: Wazza OS's gateway gives it to agents that do not support that provider themselves (see [Provider gateway](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/settings-chats.html#network-and-keys)). Keys are kept in Wazza OS's encrypted store on your computer; agents in the VM never see the key itself.

The **GitHub Copilot** card uses your GitHub Copilot plan instead of a key.

### Several keys or accounts

A provider can hold several keys, and a login several accounts: when one runs out of credit or hits its rate limit, the next one takes over, and the first is used again as soon as it can work. On each key or account:

- drag its **⋮⋮** handle to change the order;
- its **⋯** menu: **Use first**, **Move up**, **Move down**, **Rename…**, **Replace key…**, **Sign out** or **Remove**;
- **When one runs out** (per provider): **In order** (the first, until it runs out), **Take turns**, **Least used** or **Random**.

## Custom API

![Sign in page, Custom API tab: Saved endpoints, Endpoint name, API base URL, API, Model ID, Server location, Allow unencrypted HTTP for this host-loopback endpoint, Token handling, Optional API token, Find models, Add](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/img/signin-tab-3.webp)

Home › Sign in › Custom API.

Any OpenAI-compatible or Anthropic-compatible endpoint: your company's gateway, a hosted model, or a model running on your own computer. Every agent can use it: its models appear in each Chat's model list through Wazza OS's gateway.

| Field | What to enter |
|---|---|
| Saved endpoints | **New endpoint**, or one you saved (to change or remove it). |
| Endpoint name | A name for you (it shows in the model lists). |
| API base URL | The address of the API, for example `https://api.example.com/v1`. |
| API | **OpenAI-compatible (chat completions)** or Anthropic-compatible. |
| Model ID (optional) | A model it serves; or leave empty and click **Find models**, which lists the ones it serves. |
| Server location | **Remote HTTPS server**, or a server on this computer (host-local: this computer, not the VM's own localhost). |
| Allow unencrypted HTTP for this host-loopback endpoint | Only for a server on this computer that has no HTTPS (for example `http://127.0.0.1:11434/v1` for Ollama). Use an explicit port (1024–65535, or 443). |
| Token handling | **No token (omit Authorization)**, or how to send a token. |
| Optional API token | The endpoint's token, if it needs one (kept in the encrypted store). |

Click **Add** to save it. Saving does not test the model: open a Chat, pick the model, and ask something to check it.

## Web apps

![Sign in page, Web apps tab: Web apps in vm-1: Google, Microsoft, X, Facebook, TikTok, WhatsApp, OpenStreetMap and Dropbox, each Not signed in with Sign in; Sign out of all web apps; Import a Chrome profile; Company folders](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/img/signin-tab-4.webp)

Home › Sign in › Web apps.

The sign-ins of the VM's web apps (the Google, Microsoft, social network and map apps of [Apps](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/apps.html)), per VM (pick it at the top right). Google's apps share one sign-in (Gmail, Docs, Sheets…), and so do Microsoft's (Outlook, Word…); X, Facebook, TikTok, WhatsApp, OpenStreetMap and Dropbox keep their own.

- **Sign in** on a row opens that site's sign-in in the VM.
- **Sign out of all web apps** ends every web app sign-in of the VM, in every open tab, within seconds.
- **Import a Chrome profile…** copies the Chrome or Chromium profile of your computer (its sign-ins, bookmarks and settings) for the VM's Chromium, and says what was copied, or that no profile was found. Only you can do it; a Chat never can.
- **Company folders ›** opens [Settings › Files & sharing › Company folders](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/settings-files.html#company-folders).

## From the command line

```
$ wazza --gui provider-keys list --credit
$ wazza --gui provider-keys add --stdin < key.json
$ wazza --gui provider-signin status
```

`key.json` holds `{"keys": [{"providerId": "openrouter", "key": "…"}]}`: the key goes in on standard input only, never as a word of the command line (which other users of the computer could see). `list --credit` also says what OpenRouter and DeepSeek keys have left.

Every subcommand and its arguments: [The command line › Keys and sign-ins](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/cli.html#keys-and-sign-ins).


---

Page: Drive: agents on screen (Work with agents)
Address: https://os-guide.wazza.ai/drive.html

# Drive: agents on screen

Drive lets the agent of a tab look at its app as a picture and use it with the mouse and the keyboard, like you would: open menus, fill dialogs, drag, draw, type. Any app becomes something an agent can operate, even one with no tools for agents, and you watch every step happen in the tab.

- **What**: The agent sees its tab's app and clicks, drags, types and presses keys in it

- **When**: Work that only the app's window can do, or when you ask for "Drive only"

- **Who**: Anyone who wants an agent to work an app's buttons and menus

- **Where**: The app of the agent's own tab, in the VM (and your screen with [Computer Control](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/computer-control.html))

## Tools first, Drive for the rest

Many apps give agents their own tools (GIMP, Blender, ONLYOFFICE, the browser…): a tool does one operation exactly and fast, so the agent uses it first. Drive is for what no tool covers (a dialog, a menu, a drawing, an app with no tools), and for when you ask for it: say **"use Drive"** or **"Drive only"** and the agent uses nothing else. The same image of the app also lets the agent check what a tool did.

![An agent in a GIMP tab using GIMP's own tools: gimp_new_image, gimp_text and gimp_run_python, each with its receipt](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/img/gimp-mcp-tools.webp)

Without "Drive only", the agent of a GIMP tab used GIMP's own tools to make an image.

## Ask an agent to use Drive

1. Open the app's tab (Home › Apps › the app) and use its Chat, on the left of the app.
2. Say what to do, as precisely as you would to a person: which menu, which values, which file. Add *Use Drive only* to make it work through the window.
3. Watch: each step shows in the Chat (*drive_look*: it took a picture; *drive_act*: it clicked, typed or pressed keys) and happens in the app on the right.
4. Step in at any time: **Stop** ends the turn; you can click in the app yourself, then tell the agent to go on.

![A GIMP tab: on the left the Chat, where the agent says Starting with Drive, as requested, then drive_look, Step 1 File New (Ctrl+N), drive_act(key), The Create a New Image dialog is open, Step 2 set Size 640 x 480, drive_act(triple_click), The values still read 1920 x 1080: the typing didn't take, let me zoom in on the fields and retry; on the right GIMP's Create a New Image dialog](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/img/drive-in-gimp.webp)

"Use Drive only: in GIMP, create a new image of 640 x 480…": the agent works GIMP through its window.

1. Your request, pinned at the top of the Chat while the agent works.
2. *drive_look*: the agent takes a fresh picture of the app before it acts.
3. *drive_act*: one chunk of work (here a key: `Ctrl`+`N` for File › New).
4. After each act the agent gets the screen as it settled and checks it: here it sees the size did not change, says so, zooms in on the fields and tries again.
5. The app, live: the dialog the agent opened.

## What Drive can do

| Ability | What the agent does with it |
|---|---|
| Look | A picture of the tab's app (the VM's screen). It can zoom on a region, draw a grid on it to aim, take a small fast view, or a short clip of several frames (to follow something that moves). |
| Read the screen | The words on the view (read by text recognition) and the named parts of the app (buttons, fields), each with its place, so it aims at *Save* rather than at guessed pixels. |
| Click and drag | Left, right or double clicks; drags from one point to another; at a place, or at a word or a colour found when the step runs. |
| Type and press keys | Text, and key names or shortcuts (`Return`, `Ctrl`+`S`). |
| Draw | Holds the button along a shape: a circle, an ellipse, an arc, a rectangle, a line, a polygon or any points, at a chosen speed (in a paint, 3D or design app). |
| Chain steps | Up to 11 steps in one act (63 when they draw, wait or repeat), run in order on the live screen: a whole dialog filled in one go, each step aimed when it starts. |
| Wait | Until the screen settles, changes, or a word or colour appears or goes. |
| Listen | The tab's own sound for a few seconds (to check a video or a game plays sound). |
| Record | A recording of the tab while it acts (1 to 8 frames a second, up to 10 minutes; frames are kept only when something changes), with a mark at each action: to show you what it did, as a contact sheet or frame by frame. |
| Recover | When looks keep failing on a tab, it resets what is stuck between Wazza OS and the tab (the picture's stream, the tab's service) without sending any input, then looks again. |

The agent's terminal (a text view) and, with Computer Control, your own computer's windows are Drive "seats" too. Every agent in Wazza OS has Drive, whatever its model, as long as the model takes images.

## What you see, and what stays yours

- **Your view never changes.** Drive works in the agent's own tab, shown or not: it never brings the tab to the front or switches yours. A Drive agent in a background tab works while you use another tab.
- **Your mouse and keys win.** If you click in the app while the agent works, your input goes in; to watch without getting in the way, use [Desktop menu › Lock input](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/window.html#the-desktop-menu).
- **Irreversible steps do not ask.** Agents in Wazza OS work without asking you, including steps that cannot be undone (deleting, sending, paying). When you want to approve such a step, say so in your message: "ask me before you send anything".
- **Several agents, one screen.** Hidden helper agents of a Chat can use Drive on its tab too: their steps take turns with the main agent's, never at the same time.
- **Delivery is not proof.** An act reports what it sent; the agent checks the next picture to know the effect, and an uncertain step is never sent twice.

## Tips for good results

- Name the menus and values: "File › Export As…, PNG, 1920 pixels wide, save in Pictures" works better than "export it".
- Prefer a model that sees images well. A small or fast model takes more tries on dialogs (the screenshot above shows a retry).
- Give the app room: a larger tab (fold the Chat, or a bigger [VM screen size](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/settings-resources.html#screen)) shows more of the app to the agent.
- When an app has tools, let the agent use them: say "Drive only" only when you want to see it done by hand.

## Limits

- Drive works on the app of the agent's own tab. Work in another app is done by an agent in that app's tab ([Several agents at once](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/parallel-tabs.html)).
- It needs a model that takes images (most current models do). With a text-only model, Drive cannot see.
- Each picture is valid for 5 minutes and one action: the agent always acts on a fresh view, so a fast-changing app (a game, a video) is worked with clips and waits.
- Text the agent types goes in as key presses: a field that refuses typing (as in the screenshot above) needs another way (a double-click to select, a spin button, or the app's own tool).


---

Page: Computer Control (Work with agents)
Address: https://os-guide.wazza.ai/computer-control.html

# Computer Control

Computer Control is a Chat whose agent can see and use your own computer (not the VM): its screen, its keyboard and its mouse, in your own apps. It opens only after you allow it with your own click, and it stops as soon as you close its tab.

- **What**: An agent on your real computer's screen, keyboard and mouse

- **Why**: Work outside the VM: an app installed only on your computer, your desktop's settings

- **Who**: Experienced users who understand what they allow

- **Ends**: When you close its tab (Stop halts a turn at once)

> **You do not need it for work in the VM**
>
> Every other Chat works in the VM, a separate computer, where an agent cannot harm your own files. Use Computer Control only for a task that must happen on your own computer, and watch it.

## Open Computer Control

1. Click **+** (Show apps), then **Computer Control** in Main apps (*Screen control*).
2. A card asks: *Open Computer Control?* Read it, then click **Start**. **Cancel**, `Esc` or a click outside the card closes it and nothing opens.

![The card Open Computer Control? This Chat will look at and act on this computer's screen, keyboard and mouse (your own apps, not a VM's) without asking again until you close its tab. Its own shell and file tools run without asking: they change files only in this Chat's folder. Your own mouse and keyboard, and Stop, always win; closing the tab ends the control. Start, Cancel](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/img/cc-consent-card.webp)

The consent card. Only your own real click on Start opens it: an agent, a script or the command line cannot.

The tab then becomes the Computer Control Chat: its name has a red dot, and a red banner over the Chat says what is allowed:

![The Computer Control tab with its red dot, and the banner: Computer Control is active: this Chat can see and use this computer's screen, keyboard and mouse without asking again. Its own shell and file tools run without asking too (Wazza OS has no ask mode) and change files only in this Chat's folder. Stop halts it; closing this tab ends it.](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/img/cc-active-banner.webp)

## What the consent covers

| Allowed, without asking again | Not allowed |
|---|---|
| Looking at your computer's screen (every window you have open). | Anything in another tab: the consent is for this one Chat only. |
| Clicking, typing and pressing keys in your own apps. | Changing files outside this Chat's own folder with its shell and file tools. |
| Running its own shell and file tools, which change files only in this Chat's folder. | Going on after you close the tab, or after Wazza OS restarts. |

- **Your own mouse and keyboard always win**: if you move or type, your input goes first.
- **Stop** halts the agent's current turn at once.
- **Closing the tab ends the control**: the permission is withdrawn before the tab closes.
- After Wazza OS restarts, a restored Computer Control tab says *Computer Control needs your consent again: Wazza OS restarted, so this Chat cannot see or use this computer until you allow it*, with **Allow…** to show the card again.

## Ask it something

Write to it like any Chat. Pick a model that takes images (it works by looking at your screen); the model window is the same as every Chat's ([Choose the agent and the model](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/chats.html#choose-the-agent-and-the-model)).

![A Computer Control Chat asked to look at the screen without clicking: the agent read the Drive tool's description, listed the windows (drive_look, seat host), captured the screen, and analysed the picture](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/img/cc-tools.webp)

"Look at my screen and tell me which apps and windows are open. Do not click or type anything": the agent lists your windows, takes a picture of the screen and reads it, then answers.

Good first requests: "look at my screen and tell me what is open (do not click)", "open the Files app and show me my Downloads folder", "in my desktop settings, turn on the dark style". Say what it must not do as clearly as what it must do. Describing a screen is not always right the first time: in the test above, the agent took the Wazza OS window for a browser; a stronger model sees better.

## How it works, and its limits

- It uses [Drive](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/drive.html) on your computer's windows (the "host" seat) instead of the VM's: it lists your windows, looks at one or at the whole screen, then clicks and types.
- It runs on your computer, inside Wazza OS's sandbox: its shell and file tools are limited to its own folder. It reaches the Internet and Wazza OS; services of your computer (`localhost`) only when [Local services](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/settings-chats.html#network-and-keys) is on.
- Each Computer Control tab has its own permission: opening another one asks again.
- It sees the screen Wazza OS runs on: your desktop session, or, on a server, Wazza OS's own virtual screen ([On a server](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/cli-server.html)).

See also [Privacy and security](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/privacy-security.html).


---

Page: Skills, learning and personas (Work with agents)
Address: https://os-guide.wazza.ai/skills.html

# Skills, learning and personas

A skill is written know-how an agent loads before it works: how to use GIMP, how to rig a character in Blender, how to write release notes. Wazza OS ships hundreds of them, finds the right ones for each task, and keeps improving them from what happens in your Chats.

- **What**: Text files of procedures, checks and lessons that agents read

- **Why**: Agents do app work right the first time, and do not repeat yesterday's mistakes

- **Who**: Everyone (learning is on by default); power users who tune or write skills

- **Where to look**: Settings › Skills & learning

## Where skills come from

| Kind | What it is | Where you see it |
|---|---|---|
| Basic Chat skills | Shipped with Wazza OS; every Chat may load them (for example GitHub, Google Workspace, Word documents, architecture diagrams, arXiv papers, Airtable, Apple Notes) | [Settings › Skills & learning › Skills](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/settings-skills.html#skills) |
| App skills | One per app: how its agent uses that app (its tools, its menus, its pitfalls) | The app's **Edit app…** (right-click it in Apps) |
| The skill library | 310 specialist skills in 41 domains: 3D, film, video editing, motion, audio, design, game design and game engines, CAD and simulation, writing, office documents, spreadsheets, presentations, software (front end, back end, mobile, testing, security, DevOps, cloud), data and machine learning, growth… | Agents search it when a task needs it; personas group them |
| Learned skills and lessons | What Wazza OS learned from your Chats: new skills, and lessons added to existing ones | [Learned changes](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/settings-skills.html#learned-changes) |

You never have to pick skills: when a task needs an app, a tool or a domain the agent has no skill for in its context, it searches all of them first (best matches, with what each costs in context), reads the ones that fit, and follows them.

## How Wazza OS learns

At set moments, Wazza OS reviews a Chat's recent turns and keeps **one small lesson or skill**, with the evidence from the turns (what worked, what failed and its fix), never from the same turns twice. Every agent finds it afterwards, whatever its harness.

- **When**: by default every 10 turns, every 30 minutes of agent work, after a Chat has been idle 10 minutes, when a Chat ends, and when it is compacted ([How often](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/settings-skills.html#how-often)).
- **With which model**: each Chat's own, if it is at least *Standard*; or the learning model you set ([Learning](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/settings-skills.html#learning)). The tokens it uses are counted in *Spent today*.
- **Where it applies**: to one app (found only from that app's tabs), to everything (General), or to one project.
- **Kept where**: on this computer, or also with your account (the default *This computer and your account*).
- **Per Chat**: **Learning in this chat** off leaves a Chat out; **Learn from this chat now** reviews it at once (the Chat's model window › Chat settings).

Wazza OS also learns from **how you use apps**: the app journal notes the menus, clicks and keys you use in the VM's apps (never a password) and turns them into how-to lessons. It is yours only: pause it or delete its notes in [App journal](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/settings-skills.html#app-journal).

## Review and undo what was learned

1. Open Settings › Skills & learning › **Learned changes**.
2. Each change says what it is (a lesson, a new skill, a removal, a move), where it applies, and which Chat it came from (**Open its Chat**). Open its details for the evidence and the exact change.
3. **Undo** takes it back (a lesson's line goes; a learned skill goes or gets its earlier text back; a removed skill returns). **Move to General** (or to an app) changes where it applies.

An app's own lessons also show in its **Edit app…** under *Lessons noted by Chats*, with the same Undo.

## Edit or add a skill

- **A basic skill**: Settings › Skills & learning › Skills › **Edit** on its card. A shipped skill opens as your own copy, which replaces it on this computer.
- **An app's skill**: right-click the app in Apps › **Edit app…** › its skill files ([Edit an app's skill](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/custom-apps.html#edit-an-apps-skill)). **Revert to shipped** brings the original back.
- **A new skill**: the easiest way is to ask a Chat: "write a skill for our release-notes style, from this conversation", or turn on learning and let it come. For your own app, the skill is a field of its recipe ([Add your own apps](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/custom-apps.html)).

## Personas

A persona is an agent role: a description of how it works and a group of skills it loads, for one kind of task. It learns from its own Chats: procedures and tool sequences that worked, pitfalls and their fixes, worked examples.

- **Starter personas**: 3D artist (Blender), video editor, image and vector designer, film director, sound designer, motion designer, writer, game designer. They are yours to change.
- **Use one**: in a Chat's model window › **Chat settings** › **Persona**; or ask a Chat to start an agent "as the film director".
- **Make one**: Settings › Skills & learning › **Personas** › New persona: a name (its role), a description, when to use it, its skills ([every field](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/settings-skills.html#personas)).

## From the command line

```
$ wazza --gui invoke modules_call packages skill_learned '{"action":"list"}'
$ wazza --gui invoke modules_call packages persona '{"action":"list"}'
```
