Page: Apps and tabs (Apps and files)
Address: https://os-guide.wazza.ai/apps.html

# Apps and tabs

The apps live in the VM. Home › Apps lists every app you can use, about 70 of them; one click installs an app and opens it in a tab, with a Chat beside it whose agent knows that app.

## The Apps page

![Home, Apps page: search, Add app, category filters Main apps, Installed, Office, Internet, Communication, Creative, Video and audio, 3D and games, Developer, System, Your apps; the Main apps Chat, Computer Control and Wazza Pro; the Office apps with download badges](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/img/home-apps-full.webp)

Home › Apps right after the first start.

1. **Search apps**: type part of a name or of what it does (*photo*, *pdf*, *3d*).
2. **Add app**: add an app that is not in the list ([Add your own apps](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/custom-apps.html)).
3. The filters: **Main apps**, **Installed**, then the categories (Office, Internet, Communication, Creative, Video & audio, 3D & games, Developer, System) and **Your apps** (the ones you added). Each shows how many apps it holds.
4. An **installed** app: no badge. A click opens it.
5. A **not installed** app: a download badge at its top right. A click installs it, then opens it.
6. Each section says how many of its apps are installed and how many are left to install.

### The main apps

| App | What it is |
|---|---|
| Chat | *Ask any agent*: a tab that is all Chat ([Chats, agents and models](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/chats.html)). |
| Computer Control | *Screen control*: a Chat that can use your own computer, after your consent ([Computer Control](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/computer-control.html)). |
| Wazza Pro | *AI media creation*: Wazza's image, video, audio and voice tools, with a Wazza account and its credits. |

### What is in the catalog

| Category | Apps |
|---|---|
| Office | ONLYOFFICE Documents, Spreadsheets, Presentations and PDF editor; Calendar; Sticky Notes; the web versions of Google Docs, Sheets, Slides, Forms, Keep and Calendar, and of Microsoft Word, Excel, PowerPoint, OneNote and Outlook Calendar |
| Internet | Chromium, Chromium Incognito, Brave, Opera, Proton VPN, OpenStreetMap, Google Maps, Google Drive, OneDrive, Dropbox; tools: OSM places and routes, Search |
| Communication | Gmail, Outlook, Proton Mail, Google Meet, Teams, Telegram, Signal, WhatsApp, Discord, X, Facebook, Postiz (post scheduler) |
| Creative | GIMP, Inkscape, Glaxnimate (2D animation), Motion Studio (motion graphics), Trelby (screenwriting) |
| Video & audio | VLC, Kdenlive, OBS Studio, Voice Studio (text to speech), YouTube, TikTok, Spotify; tool: Video Toolkit (FFmpeg video tools and yt-dlp) |
| 3D & games | Blender, FreeCAD, Godot, Web Game Studio, Tiled (game maps), Free Texture Packer (sprite sheets), BREP (parametric CAD), Unity Hub |
| Developer | VSCodium, Zed, Wave Terminal, Postgres; tool: Git |
| System | Files, Desktop, Settings, Calculator, KeePassXC, OTPClient (2FA codes); tools: GPU for apps, Sound card drivers |

The *tools* have no window: they give the VM and its agents a capability (Git, the graphics libraries, sound, web search, maps and routes, video processing). They install like apps; Git, GPU for apps, Sound card drivers, Search and OSM places and routes are installed on the first start.

Web apps (Gmail, Google Docs, Word, Teams…) open in the VM's browser as their own tab; their sign-ins are on [Sign in › Web apps](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/signin.html#web-apps).

## Install an app

![Apps page with gimp typed in the search: the Creative section shows GIMP, Photo editing, with its download badge](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/img/apps-search.webp)

Searching *gimp*: one result, not installed yet (the badge at its top right).

1. Find the app (filter or search).
2. Click it (its tooltip says *Install and open*). A new tab opens and shows the installation:

![The new GIMP tab, Starting: Installing GIMP, The app will open once installation and verification finish. You can use another tab while this runs. Elapsed time, Running, Cancel installation](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/img/apps-installing.webp)

1. The tab says *Installing …* with the time elapsed. You can use other tabs meanwhile; **Cancel installation** stops it.
2. When it is installed and checked, the app opens in the tab, with its Chat on the left. A notification says it is done.

Installing takes from under a minute (small apps) to several minutes (Blender, ONLYOFFICE), depending on your connection. Apps install inside the VM, so they never change your computer. When an installation fails, the tab says why with **Retry installation** and **Show log**; Wazza OS already retried once by itself.

> An agent can install apps for you too: ask "install Inkscape and open it", or give it a job in an app that is not installed: it installs it first.

## Open and use an app

- Click an installed app: it opens in a new tab ([Tabs](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/window.html#tabs)). Open the same app twice and you get two tabs, each with its own window and its own Chat.
- Use it as on any computer: click, type, use its menus. Its files are in the VM ([Files and sharing](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/files.html)).
- Ask its Chat to work in it for you: the agent knows the app (its skill) and uses its tools or [Drive](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/drive.html).

![A GIMP tab after its agent's work: the Chat's answer Done, the image is open in GIMP, 800 x 600 canvas with a dark teal background, Hello from Wazza OS in white, centered; and GIMP showing the image with Hello from Wazza OS](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/img/drive-gimp-result.webp)

"Create a new 800 x 600 image with a dark teal background and write Hello from Wazza OS in large white letters in the middle": the agent of a GIMP tab did it with GIMP's own tools.

### The app menu

![The menu of the GIMP card: GIMP, Photo editing; Open in vm-1; Open in a new VM; Edit app; Uninstall from vm-1](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/img/apps-card-menu.webp)

Right-click an app on the Apps page:

| Item | What it does |
|---|---|
| Open in vm-1 | Opens it in that VM (one item per VM where it is installed). |
| Open in a new VM | Makes a new VM and opens the app there ([several VMs](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/settings-vms.html#add-a-vm)). |
| Edit app… | The app's recipe and its skill files: how it installs and starts, and what its agent knows ([Edit an app's skill](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/custom-apps.html#edit-an-apps-skill)). |
| Uninstall from vm-1… | Removes the app from that VM (below). |
| Remove from catalog… | (an app you added) Takes your app out of the catalog, once it is uninstalled everywhere. |

## Uninstall an app

1. Right-click the app on the Apps page › **Uninstall from vm-1…**.
2. A box shows the exact plan before anything happens:

![Uninstall GIMP from vm-1? Cannot uninstall yet: the app is open in tab vm-1.t2; Removes files: the GIMP AppImage and its commands and 2 more; Open in tabs: vm-1.t2; APT GIMP 2.10 was removed at install and is not restored; Plan e553f5f406e4; Show every file, package and folder; Close its open tabs first; Uninstall (grey); Cancel](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/img/apps-uninstall.webp)

Uninstalling GIMP while a GIMP tab is open.

1. What will be removed (files, commands, packages), the tabs where the app is open, and what is not restored (here, an older GIMP that its install had replaced).
2. **Show every file, package and folder**: the complete list.
3. **Close its open tabs first**: needed when the app is open (otherwise the box says *Cannot uninstall yet* and **Uninstall** stays grey).
4. **Uninstall** removes exactly that plan; **Cancel** changes nothing. The card follows it (*Uninstalling…*) and a notification says when it is done.

Your files made with the app (in the VM's folders) stay. Apps that Wazza OS itself needs (Files, Desktop, the default tools) cannot be uninstalled.

## From the command line

```
$ wazza --gui app list
$ wazza --gui app status gimp
$ wazza --gui app uninstall gimp --vm vm-1 --follow
```

Every `app` subcommand: [The command line › Apps](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/cli.html#apps).


---

Page: Desktop apps and the GPU (Apps and files)
Address: https://os-guide.wazza.ai/gpu-apps.html

# Desktop apps and the GPU

The apps of the VM are real Linux desktop apps. The ones that draw a lot (3D, video, large images) draw on your computer's graphics card, which the VM shares with your computer. You do not need to set anything: this page explains what happens, how to check it, and the two other ways for special cases.

- **What**: The VM's apps drawing and computing on your graphics card

- **Why**: Blender, FreeCAD or OBS stay smooth; renders and effects run at the card's speed

- **Who**: Everyone with 3D, video or design work; Native GPU for power users with a spare card

- **Where**: Settings › VM resources › Graphics

## Three ways to use your card

| GPU setting | What the VM's apps get | For |
|---|---|---|
| **Virtualized GPU** (default) | Your card, shared with your computer: OpenGL, Vulkan and OpenCL, each through the fastest path your computer offers. | Everyone. Your own apps keep the card too. |
| Native GPU (experimental) | One of your cards, lent to the running VM: its apps use it with its own driver, at full speed, including CUDA (NVIDIA) and HIP (AMD). Your computer cannot use that card while it is lent. | Computers with a second graphics card that does not drive your screen, for heavy compute (GPU rendering, AI models). |
| None (CPU only) | Software graphics on the VM's processors: everything works, 3D is much slower. | Computers without a usable graphics card, or to rule the card out while looking for a problem. |

Change it in [Settings › VM resources › Graphics › GPU](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/settings-resources.html#graphics); it applies at the VM's next start (Native GPU lends the card to the running VM). The graphics libraries the apps need are the *GPU for apps* tool, installed on the first start.

## Which apps use it

| App | On your card | Good to know |
|---|---|---|
| Blender | The 3D view, and EEVEE renders | Cycles renders on the VM's processors with the Virtualized GPU; with Native GPU it can use the card's CUDA or HIP. Agents test a render small first, then render the full size. |
| FreeCAD, Godot, BREP, Unity Hub | The 3D view (OpenGL, Vulkan) |  |
| Kdenlive, OBS Studio | The preview and effects (OpenGL) | Encoding a video mostly uses the VM's processors. |
| GIMP, Inkscape, Glaxnimate, Motion Studio | Drawing the canvas |  |
| Chromium, web apps, Web Game Studio | WebGL pages: 3D in the browser, maps, the web games Web Game Studio's Chat makes (three.js, Babylon.js…) |  |

The VM's processors and memory matter as much: a render or an encode uses the processors you allow in [VM resources](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/settings-resources.html#memory-and-cpu). Before heavy work (a render, a build, an encode), an agent reads what the VM has now and plans with it.

## Check that apps use your card

![The VM card: vm-1 running, CPU 18%, RAM 2.1 of 5.8 GB, Auto: 75% of the memory free now, then OpenGL 4.2 · virgl (virgl (Radeon RX 7900 XTX (radeonsi, navi31, LLVM 20…)](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/img/vm-card-graphics.webp)

The VM card at the bottom left of Home: its last line names the card the VM draws on (here an AMD Radeon RX 7900 XTX, through virtualization).

- **The VM card** (Home, bottom left): the last line names your card. *llvmpipe* there means software graphics: the VM is not using your card.
- **Settings › VM resources › Graphics › In the VM**: the path Vulkan, OpenGL and OpenCL each take now, on your card or on the VM's processors, in plain words.
- **GPU use** (same page): how busy each running VM keeps your card.
- **In the VM's terminal**: `glxinfo -B` (OpenGL), `vulkaninfo --summary` (Vulkan), `clinfo -l` (OpenCL).
- **Smoothness**: the tab's Desktop menu › **FPS** shows the frame rate of the app's picture ([The Desktop menu](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/window.html#the-desktop-menu)).

## Lend a card (Native GPU)

> Experimental. While a card is lent, your computer cannot use it; Wazza OS never lends the card your screen is plugged into.

1. Settings › VM resources › Graphics › GPU › **Native GPU (passthrough, experimental)**, and pick the **Card**.
2. Read the **Native GPU** line: it says whether this computer can lend that card, and what to do first: close the programs that use it, move your screen's cable to another port, or the one-time setup **Allow lending a card** (it asks for your administrator password). Then **Check again**.
3. Apply. Wazza OS installs the card's driver in the VM first (AMD, Intel or NVIDIA), then lends the card to the running VM as a second graphics card: the VM's picture stays, and its apps use the card for their work.

Turning Native GPU off, or stopping the VM, gives the card back to your computer. Nothing is changed for good: a restart of your computer always gives every card back. Your computer needs IOMMU turned on in its firmware; the line says when it is not.

**One card only?** **Lend-ready mode** makes your computer draw its desktop with the processor from its next restart, so its only card can be lent. Turn it off to get the card back for your desktop (again from the next restart).

## Graphics memory

A VM may hold at most 50 % of the graphics memory free (Auto), where Linux can bound it (6.14 or newer); set another share or a fixed size in [Graphics › GPU memory](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/settings-resources.html#graphics). Raise it for very large scenes; lower it to keep more for your own apps.

## When 3D is slow

- The VM card says *llvmpipe*: your card is not used. Run `wazza --check` on your computer: its *Graphics driver* line says what to fix (driver, permissions; NVIDIA needs its driver 495 or newer).
- Close other tabs with 3D apps: they share the same card and the VM's processors.
- Give the VM more processors ([VM resources › vCPUs](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/settings-resources.html#vcpus)).
- Lower the VM's screen size ([Screen](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/settings-resources.html#screen)): fewer pixels to draw and send.
- More fixes: [Troubleshooting](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/troubleshooting.html#an-app-tab-stays-black-or-frozen).

## From the command line

```
$ wazza --gui gpu status
$ wazza --gui gpu mode virtualized
$ wazza --gui vm-gpu status
```

`gpu mode` takes `virtualized`, `native` or `none`; `vm-gpu auto PERCENT` or `vm-gpu set MIB` sets the graphics memory.


---

Page: Add your own apps (Apps and files)
Address: https://os-guide.wazza.ai/custom-apps.html

# Add your own apps

Any Linux app that runs on Ubuntu can become a Wazza OS app. Its *recipe* says how to install it in the VM once and how to start it. It then gets a card in Apps, opens in tabs with its own Chat, and can bring its own tools for agents and its own skill.

- **What**: A recipe: install script, start script, and optionally tools (MCP) and a skill

- **Why**: Your tools are not in the catalog; your agents should know them as well as GIMP

- **Who**: Anyone (a Chat writes the recipe); developers and admins (the form)

- **Where**: Apps › Add app; any app's right-click › Edit app…

## Two ways to add an app

![The Add app menu: Add an app: Your own app… (any Linux app), Ask a Chat to add one… (it writes the recipe)](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/img/apps-add-menu.webp)

Home › Apps › **Add app**.

| Way | For |
|---|---|
| **Ask a Chat to add one…** | Everyone: say which app; the agent finds how to install it, writes and checks the recipe, and installs it. |
| **Your own app…** | When you know the commands: a form with every field of the recipe. |

## Ask a Chat to add an app

1. Home › Apps › **Add app** › **Ask a Chat to add one…**. A new Chat tab opens with this already in its send box: *Add this app to Wazza OS's Apps (write its recipe, save it, then install it):*
2. Finish the sentence with the app, and anything that matters to you, then send. For example: *Krita, the painting app, from the Ubuntu packages*.
3. The agent writes the recipe, checks it, saves it and installs the app in the VM, telling you what it does in the Chat. Like everything an agent does in the VM, this runs without asking you; say in your message if you want to read the recipe before it installs.
4. When it is installed, its card is in Apps (filter **Your apps**), and the agent can open it.

A Chat can also change a recipe later ("make Krita open files", "add this skill to Krita"). If the app has its own tools (an MCP server) that work without its window, the agent can make them available to every Chat of the VM; otherwise only the Chat of a tab where the app is open gets them.

## Fill the form

![The Add your own app form: Application name, Description, Executable name, Install script, Launch script, Opens a file, Uninstall script, Skill for the app's Chat, Optional MCP stdio server, MCP install script, MCP executable, MCP arguments, and the help text](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/img/custom-app-form.webp)

Apps › Add app › **Your own app…**. Its buttons (**Load XTerm example**, **Cancel**, **Add app**) are below the help text.

1. What the card shows, and how Wazza OS knows the app is installed.
2. How it installs and how it starts.
3. What its Chat knows about it (its skill).
4. Its own tools for agents (optional).

| Field | Rules | What it is |
|---|---|---|
| Application name | Required; up to 80 characters | The card's name. |
| Description | Optional; up to 320 characters | The card's short words (empty: "User-added application"). |
| Executable name (in the guest) | Required; a plain program name: letters, digits, `_` and `-`, up to 64 | The program Wazza OS looks for to know the app is installed, for example `krita`. |
| Install script | Required; up to 8192 characters | Shell commands that install the app. They run as the administrator (root) inside the VM, never on your computer, and only after your approval. |
| Launch script | Required; up to 4096 characters | Starts the app, as the VM's user. Keep the app in the foreground: start it with `exec`, do not send it to the background. It gets the variables `WAZZA_APP_OWNER` and `WAZZA_APP_ID`. |
| Opens a file | Off by default | On: the app can open files (double-click in the Explorer, "open this in Krita"); the launch script gets the file as `$1`. |
| Uninstall script | Optional; up to 8192 characters | Runs as root before the app's files are removed, when you uninstall it. |
| Skill for the app's Chat | Optional; no length limit | Becomes the app's `SKILL.md`: what the agent of this app's tabs reads first (its menus, its shortcuts, what to avoid). You can add more skill files later in Edit app. |
| Optional MCP stdio server | Off by default | Turns on the three fields below: the app's own tools for agents (see [below](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/custom-apps.html#give-your-app-tools)). |
| MCP install script | Optional; up to 8192 bytes | Installs the tools' server (root, in the VM, after approval). |
| MCP executable | Required with MCP; a full path in the VM starting with `/`, up to 512 bytes | The server's program. |
| MCP arguments | A JSON list of up to 32 strings; default `[]` | The words given to the server. |

> The scripts run with full rights inside the VM: add only scripts and servers you trust. Never put a password or an API key in these fields.

Then **Add app**. Saving only adds the recipe: *"<name> saved. Select its card to approve installation and open it."* Click the card (in **Your apps**): your click approves the installation, which runs in a new tab like any app's ([Install an app](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/apps.html#install-an-app)).

### Example: XTerm

**Load XTerm example** fills the form with a small working app, a terminal:

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Application name | XTerm |
| Description | A guest X11 terminal |
| Executable name | `xterm` |
| Launch script | `exec /usr/bin/xterm` |

Install script:

```
set -eu
apt-get -o Acquire::ForceIPv4=true update
DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive apt-get install -y xterm
```

The same pattern works for any app of Ubuntu's packages: change the name, the program and the package.

## Give your app tools

An app's tools let its agent do exact operations (GIMP's agent has 40, from "new image" to "export"). They come from an MCP server: a program in the VM that speaks the Model Context Protocol over its standard input and output. Turn on **Optional MCP stdio server**, then give how to install it, its full path and its arguments. The server gets `WAZZA_APP_OWNER` and `WAZZA_APP_ID`, so it knows which app and tab it serves. Its tools reach the Chat of a tab where the app is open.

## Edit an app

Right-click an app's card in Apps › **Edit app…**. A tab named *Edit App — <name>* opens; it works for the apps of the catalog too.

![Edit App, GIMP: Built-in app MCP: 40 tools a Chat of this app gets, gimp.status, gimp.activate, gimp.adjust_brightness_contrast and the others; they act on the app open in that Chat's tab](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/img/edit-app-mcp.webp)

The top of Edit App for GIMP: the tools a Chat of this app gets.

- **The app's tools**: the list of tools its Chat gets, by name.
- **Six sections**, each folded: 1 App installation script, 2 App execution script, 3 MCP installation script, 4 MCP execution command, 5 MCP execution arguments, 6 App skill. For an app that comes with Wazza OS, a note at the top says which parts you can change: for GIMP, its installation script (as your own version), while how it starts stays read-only.
- **Apply** saves your changes as a new version of the recipe. It does not install, open or restart the app: a changed installation script takes effect when you install the app again.
- **Discard unsaved edits** forgets your changes; **Close editor tab** closes it.

## Edit an app's skill

An app's skill is what its agent knows about it. It can be several files: GIMP's are `SKILL.md` (the main one), and topics such as errors, filters, recipes and its Python scripting.

![Associated skill files: Skill files; SKILL.md, errors.md, filters.md, library.md, pdb-python.md and recipes.md, each marked shipped; the file name SKILL.md; its text; Add skill file, Save skill file, Stage for Apply; SKILL.md loaded (8087 bytes); 6 skill files a Chat of this app gets: 6 shipped with Wazza OS (read-only)](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/img/edit-app-skill-files.webp)

At the bottom of Edit App: *Associated skill files*.

1. Click **Skill files**, then a file. *(shipped)* marks a file that comes with Wazza OS; the line at the bottom says how many files the app's Chat gets, and whose they are.
2. Change its text.
3. **Save skill file**: your copy is saved for this app and replaces the shipped file for its Chats. Or **Stage for Apply**: the change is saved with the recipe's next **Apply**.

- **Revert to shipped** (shown on a file you saved over a shipped one) removes your copy: the shipped file is used again.
- **Add skill file**: a new topic for the app: type a new name ending in `.md` and its text, then save or stage it.

![The six sections of Edit App, 6 App skill open: Own app instructions, not executable code; the SKILL.md text; then Lessons noted by Chats: what Chats learned while using this app, noted beside its skill; No lesson noted by Chats on this app's skills yet](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/img/edit-app-sections.webp)

Section *6 · App skill* open: the skill's text, then *Lessons noted by Chats*.

**Lessons noted by Chats**: what Chats learned while using this app ([How Wazza OS learns](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/skills.html#how-wazza-os-learns)). Every Chat of the app reads them with its skill; the skill file itself is not changed. Change a lesson's words, or remove it; Settings › Skills & learning › [Learned changes](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/settings-skills.html#learned-changes) lists every change with its Undo.

## Remove an app you added

1. Uninstall it from every VM that has it: right-click its card › **Uninstall from vm-1…** ([Uninstall an app](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/apps.html#uninstall-an-app)).
2. Right-click its card › **Remove from catalog…**: its recipe goes, with its card.

Only an app you added can be removed from the catalog; while it is installed, the menu says *Uninstall it from vm-1 first*.

## From the command line

A recipe is a JSON file (the `wazza.app.v1` format). Start from a template, edit it, check it, save it:

```
$ wazza --gui app template apt --skill > myapp.json
$ wazza --gui app validate --stdin < myapp.json
$ wazza --gui app save --stdin --install --vm vm-1 < myapp.json
$ wazza --gui app list
$ wazza --gui app remove APP_ID
```

Templates: `apt` (Ubuntu packages) or `script` (your own install script), with `--mcp` and `--skill` to include those parts. More: [The command line › Apps](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/cli.html#apps).


---

Page: Files and sharing (Apps and files)
Address: https://os-guide.wazza.ai/files.html

# Files and sharing

Your computer and the VM have separate files. Agents and apps work on the VM's files; your own files go into the VM only when you put them there, and results come back to your computer as new files, never over yours.

## Where files live

| Place | What is there |
|---|---|
| The VM's home folder (`/home/ubuntu` in the VM) | Everything apps and agents make: Documents, Pictures, Downloads, Desktop… The VM's own Files app and the Explorer show it. |
| `~/wazza_os` in the VM | A folder Wazza OS shares with the VM for its own work: files attached to Chats, previews, each Chat's working folder. Leave it to Wazza OS. |
| `~/Company/<Name>` in the VM | Company folders, read-only ([below](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/files.html#company-folders)). |
| Your computer's `Downloads/From the VM` | Files copied out of the VM land here, as new files. |
| Your computer's `Downloads` | VM backups (zip files), exported Chats. |

Wazza OS never changes your own files: what it writes on your computer is always a new file (with `_copy1`-style names when a name is taken).

## The Explorer

![The Explorer: VM 1 selector, view buttons, reload and close; Home; New file, New folder, Paste here; the home folder's files with name, date modified, type and size](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/img/window-explorer.webp)

Click the button at the far left of the tab strip. The Explorer opens over the Chat of the current tab.

1. The VM whose files you see (pick another running VM).
2. Views (list, grid, pictures, details), reload, close.
3. **New file**, **New folder**, **Paste here**.
4. The folder's content: click a folder's arrow to open it; double-click a file to open it in its app (a new tab); right-click a file for its menu (open with, rename, move, copy, permissions, delete, download to your computer).

Deleting in the Explorer is permanent: the VM has no trash. Wazza OS refuses to overwrite: renaming or moving onto an existing name is refused.

## Bring your files into the VM

- **Drag and drop** files from your file manager onto a folder of the Explorer, onto a Chat (attached to your message) or onto an app's window (copied into the VM's `Downloads` and opened by the app).
- **Copy and paste**: copy files in your file manager, then **Paste here** in the Explorer, or paste in the VM's Files app.
- **Ask an agent**: "copy my Documents/report.pdf into the VM".

Every way, step by step, with where the files land and how they are named: [Move files](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/files-move.html).

## Get files out of the VM

- **The Explorer**: right-click › **Copy**, then paste in your file manager; or › **Download to this computer** (your `Downloads`), or **Download zip**.
- **Drag out** of an app of the VM (its Files app, for instance) onto your file manager.
- **Copy and paste** from the VM's Files app: by default Wazza OS asks first; the files land in `Downloads/From the VM` and on your clipboard.
- **Ask an agent**: "put circle.png on my computer" (into `Downloads/From the VM`, after your Allow).

Details: [Move files](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/files-move.html#out-of-a-vm-onto-your-computer). Copied **text** goes both ways between your computer and the VM, always: copy on one side, paste on the other.

## Versions and undo

- **File versions**: when something overwrites, replaces or deletes one of your files in the VM, Wazza OS keeps the version before. Ask a Chat "show me the versions of Documents/report.odt" and "restore the version of 10:42": the current file is kept as a version first.
- **A Chat's own edits**: Wazza OS keeps a checkpoint of every file a Chat changes. Ask that Chat "what did you change?" (each change with its lines), "show me the diff of report.md", or "put my files back as they were before your last turn": it restores only when you ask, and a restore can itself be undone.

## Company folders

Your company's file servers (SFTP, FTPS or SMB), mounted read-only in every VM at `~/Company/<Name>`, so agents can read company documents without changing them. Set them up in [Settings › Files & sharing › Company folders](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/settings-files.html#company-folders); a team's admins can add them for every member.

## Sync with your account

With a Wazza OS account, your skills, files and Chat history sync with your account's vault, so your other computers have them: [Settings › Sync & team](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/settings-sync.html).

## From the command line

```
$ wazza --gui explorer list Documents
$ wazza --gui explorer transfer --from host --to vm-1 --folder Documents ~/report.pdf
$ wazza --gui clipboard files --to-computer allow
```

Every subcommand: [The command line › Files](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/cli.html#files).


---

Page: Move files (Apps and files)
Address: https://os-guide.wazza.ai/files-move.html

# Move files between your computer, the VMs and Chats

Your computer and each VM have their own files. You move them by hand (drag and drop, copy and paste, the Explorer) or you ask an agent. Wazza OS only reads your files, and on your computer it only ever adds new files: it never writes over one of yours.

- **What**: Every way between your computer, the VMs and Chats, and where the files land

- **Why**: Give an app or an agent your files; get the results back

- **Who**: Everyone

- **Where**: The Explorer, any tab, your own file manager

Where files live (the VM's home, its `wazza_os` folder, company folders) and the Explorer itself: [Files and sharing](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/files.html).

## Which way

| You want to… | Do this | It lands in |
|---|---|---|
| put files of your computer into a VM | drag them onto a folder of the [Explorer](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/files-move.html#onto-a-folder-of-the-explorer), or copy them in your file manager and **Paste here** in the Explorer | that folder |
| give a file of your computer to an agent | [drop it on the Chat](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/files-move.html#onto-a-chat), or **+** › **From this computer…** | your message, as an attachment |
| give a VM file to an agent | type `@` in the message box and pick it; from the next release, also drag it from the [Explorer onto the Chat](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/files-move.html#from-the-explorer-onto-a-chat) | your message, by its path in the VM (nothing is copied) |
| open a file of your computer in an app of the VM | [drop it on the app's window](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/files-move.html#onto-an-apps-window) | the VM's `Downloads`, and the app opens it |
| get a VM file on your computer | in the Explorer, right-click it › **Copy**, then paste in your file manager; or › **Download to this computer**; or drag it out of the app's window | where you paste or drop; your `Downloads` |
| copy between two VMs | the Explorer's **Copy**, then **Paste here** in the other VM's Explorer | the folder you paste in |
| let an agent do it | ask a VM tab's Chat: "copy Documents/report.pdf from my computer into the VM", "put render.png on my computer" | the VM's `Downloads` or the folder you name; your `Downloads/From the VM` or the folder you name |

## Drag and drop

### Onto a folder of the Explorer

![The Wazza OS window with the Explorer open on the left and GIMP in its tab; the computer's own Files window at the bottom right shows report.txt selected, and its icon is being dragged onto the Explorer's Documents folder, which is outlined](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/img/move-drop-explorer.webp)

report.txt dragged from the computer's Files (bottom right) onto the VM's Documents folder in the Explorer (left).

1. Open the Explorer: the button at the far left of the tab strip. It shows the VM of the tab you are on.
2. Drag files or folders from your file manager onto a folder of the Explorer: the folder lights up.
3. Let go. The line under the list follows the copy, with **Cancel**, then says where the files went: *Dropped into /home/ubuntu/Documents: report.txt*.

![The Explorer's list with the Videos folder's details (VM path /home/ubuntu/Videos) and, at the bottom, the line Copying video-master.mov… 13% · 0 of 1 files · 223.3 MB of 1.60 GB, with Cancel](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/img/move-drop-progress.webp)

A 1.6 GB video dropped on the VM's Videos folder, on its way.

- **A name already there**: the new file is `report (2).txt`, then `report (3).txt`… Nothing in the VM is overwritten.
- **Size**: no limit; only the free space of the VM's disk counts. Folders come with everything in them.
- **No question**: your own drop is your consent, whatever the [file-copy settings](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/files-move.html#what-the-file-copy-settings-cover) say. Your files are only read.

### Onto a Chat

![Two moments of the Chat's message box: first the line Copying and verifying 1 file(s)… with Cancel attachment, then photo.png attached above an empty message](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/img/move-drop-chat.webp)

photo.png dropped on a VM tab's Chat: copied and checked, then attached to the next message.

Drop files from your file manager onto a Chat. The message box says *Copying and verifying 1 file(s)…* (with **Cancel attachment**), then shows each file above your text. They go with your next message. **+** › **From this computer…** does the same with your computer's file chooser.

- The agent gets its own copy in the VM (in the VM's `wazza_os/chat` folder). Your file is only read.
- **8 files at a time**: the message box names the others; drop them again.
- **A folder** is not attached: it is copied into the VM's `Downloads`, and the message box says where. Ask the agent to look there.
- **Size**: no limit but the VM's free disk (Wazza OS keeps 256 MB of it free).
- The [Computer Control](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/computer-control.html) Chat takes no files: it reads your files where they are.

### Onto an app's window

![Left: photo.png dragged from the computer's Files over GIMP's canvas in its tab. Right: GIMP shows photo.png, opened from the drop](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/img/move-drop-app.webp)

photo.png dragged from the computer's Files onto GIMP's window (left): GIMP opened it (right).

Drag files from your file manager onto an app in a tab and let go where the app should take them. Wazza OS copies them into the VM, then drops them into the app at that spot, as a drop inside the VM would: GIMP opens a picture, a text editor opens a text. A notice follows the copy (*Copying the dropped files into vm-1: 37%*), then says *Dropped into vm-1: photo.png. The app received them (they are in vm-1's Downloads).*

- **Where they are**: in the VM's `Downloads`. Dropped on the VM's desktop: on its `Desktop`. Dropped on a folder of the VM's own Files app: in that folder.
- When the window under the pointer takes no drop, the files stay in the VM's `Downloads` and the notice says so.

### From the Explorer onto a Chat

> Known issue in the published build (0.2.0, build 44c5d0ea07c1): a VM file dragged from the Explorer onto its Chat, or copied in the Explorer and pasted in the message box, is not attached (the message box says *Not attached: …*). Type `@` in the message box and pick the file instead ([Mention a file or an app](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/chats.html#mention-a-file-or-an-app)). The next release attaches it as this section shows.

![The Explorer over the Chat: the Pictures folder is open and its file hello-poster.png selected; below, the message box says Attached from vm-1 by its path (nothing copied): hello-poster.png and holds @file:///home/ubuntu/Pictures/hello-poster.png](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/img/move-explorer-chat.webp)

The next release: hello-poster.png, a file of the VM's open Pictures folder, dropped on the Chat of a tab on that VM, attached by its path.

Drag files or folders of a VM from the Explorer onto the Chat of a tab on that same VM, or copy them in the Explorer (right-click › **Copy**) and paste them in the message box. They are attached by their path in the VM: the message box gets `@file:///home/ubuntu/Documents/report.txt` (a folder's path ends with `/`) and says *Attached from vm-1 by its path (nothing copied): report.txt*. Nothing is copied: the agent reads the file where it is. **+** › **From the VM's files…** opens the Explorer on the Chat's VM for this, and typing `@` picks a file the same way ([Mention a file or an app](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/chats.html#mention-a-file-or-an-app)).

- **8 at a time**, like a drop of your own files.
- A file of **another VM** is not attached: the message box says so. Copy it into this Chat's VM first (the Explorer's **Copy**, then **Paste here** in one of its folders).
- On the **Computer Control** Chat, a VM's files are not on your computer: download them or copy them to *This computer* in the Explorer first.
- Files of *This computer* in the Explorer drop on a VM's Chat as your own files do (above).

### Out of a VM, onto your computer

![Left: poster-brief.txt dragged from the VM's Files app (in its tab, right) over the computer's own Files window (top left). Right: the file is in the computer's Documents folder, and a notice at the bottom right says Dropped on this computer from vm-1: poster-brief.txt](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/img/move-drag-out.webp)

poster-brief.txt dragged out of the VM's Files (left) and dropped in the computer's Documents (right).

Drag files in an app of the VM (its Files app, for instance) out of the VM's picture, and let go on a folder of your file manager or on your desktop. Wazza OS copies them out of the VM while you drag (*Copying the dragged files from vm-1: 40%*), and the app you let go on takes them (*Dropped on this computer from vm-1: …*).

- Let go where nothing takes files: they are put on your clipboard (*On the clipboard: … Nothing took the drop there. Paste with Ctrl+V in Files.*). Paste them in any folder.
- Back on the same VM's picture, the drop is refused: the files are already there.
- With **From a VM to this computer** set to **Off**, drags out are refused.
- From the Explorer, use [Copy and paste](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/files-move.html#with-the-explorer) or [Download](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/files-move.html#the-explorers-download): on Ubuntu 24.04's desktop (GNOME on Wayland), a row of the Explorer dragged onto your file manager does not land in this version.

## Copy and paste

### With the Explorer

![The Explorer's line at the bottom left says Copied poster-brief.txt: paste with Ctrl+V here, in another folder or VM, or in this computer's file manager; the computer's Files window at the bottom right shows poster-brief.txt pasted in its folder](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/img/move-copy-paste.webp)

A VM file copied in the Explorer (its line, bottom left), then pasted with Ctrl+V in the computer's Files (bottom right).

1. Right-click a file or folder in the Explorer › **Copy**. A VM file is first saved on your computer (*Copying poster-brief.txt… saving 1 files*), then the line says *Copied poster-brief.txt: paste with Ctrl+V here, in another folder or VM, or in this computer's file manager*.
2. Paste: `Ctrl`+`V` in a folder of your file manager (the file lands where you paste), or **Paste here** in the Explorer, in another folder, another VM or *This computer*. From the next release, a paste in the message box of a Chat on the same VM attaches it by its path ([above](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/files-move.html#from-the-explorer-onto-a-chat)).

The other way works too: copy files in your file manager, then **Paste here** in the Explorer (into the selected folder, else the folder shown). These are your own copies: no question, no size limit, new names only.

### With the VM's Files app

![Left: the computer's own Files window in Downloads, with poster-brief.txt just pasted and selected. Right: the VM's Files app in its tab, its Home folder with poster-brief.txt selected, the file that was copied there](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/img/move-vm-copy.webp)

poster-brief.txt copied in the VM's Files (right, in its tab) and pasted in the computer's Files (left).

- **Out of the VM**: copy files in the VM's Files (`Ctrl`+`C`). Wazza OS copies them out at once and puts them on your computer's clipboard: *Ready to paste on this computer: poster-brief.txt*. Paste them (`Ctrl`+`V`) in any folder of your file manager: they land where you paste. Your own copy asks nothing; with **From a VM to this computer** set to **Off**, nothing is copied.
- **Into the VM**: copy files in your file manager, then paste them in a folder of the VM's Files. They are copied when you paste: *Pasted in vm-1: 1 file (28 KB)*. This follows **From this computer to a VM**: Allow (the default) copies at once, Ask shows a question at the paste (*Paste 1 item from this computer in vm-1?*, with **Allow**), Off copies no files.
- No limit of size or number: only the free disk where the files land counts.
- Copied **text** goes both ways in every case.

## The Explorer's Download

Right-click a VM file or folder in the Explorer › **Download to this computer** (in an opened folder's list the item reads **Download**):

- It is copied into your `Downloads` folder, whatever its size; a folder stays a folder. The line says *Downloading hello-poster.png to Downloads…*, then *Downloaded to Downloads: hello-poster.png*. A second download of it is `hello-poster_copy1.png`.
- A file of 16 KB or less opens your computer's Save dialog instead: you choose its name and folder. Known issue in this version: the line may say *not_ready*, or the dialog may close without saving. Use **Download zip**, or the Explorer's **Copy** and paste it in your file manager.
- **Download zip** makes one `.zip` in your `Downloads`: a folder's zip (`Pictures.zip`) holds the folder with everything in it.

## Names, sizes and progress

- **Into a VM**, a name already taken gives `report (2).txt`, `report (3).txt`…
- **On your computer**, it gives `report_copy1.txt`, `report_copy2.txt`… Wazza OS never writes over, deletes or renames a file of yours.
- **Size**: your own copies (drops, drags out, the Explorer, copy and paste with the VM's apps) have no limit but the free disk where the files land, checked before the copy starts. An agent's copy takes 1 to 64 files or folders at a time, up to 4 GB, 4,096 files and folders and 32 levels of folders.
- **Progress**: the Explorer's line (with **Cancel**), a notice for drops on an app's window, drags out and copies through the clipboard, and the message box for a Chat's attachments.
- **Your files** are only read. Links are never followed, and agents leave hidden files (names starting with a dot) out.

## What the file-copy settings cover

[Settings › Files & sharing › Between this computer and VMs](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/settings-files.html#between-this-computer-and-vms) has one setting each way: **Ask**, **Allow** or **Off**. *From this computer to a VM* is Allow by default, *From a VM to this computer* is Ask.

| How the files move | What the setting does |
|---|---|
| Your own drag and drop; the Explorer's Copy, Paste and Download | Nothing to allow: your gesture is the consent. Off (from a VM) still stops drags out of a VM's window. |
| Copy in the VM's apps, paste on your computer | No question (your own copy). Off: nothing is copied. |
| Copy on your computer, paste in the VM's apps | Allow: copied at the paste. Ask: a question at the paste, with **Allow**. Off: no files (text still is). |
| An agent's copy, either way | Allow: at once. Ask: a question with **Allow**; after 2 minutes without it, nothing is copied. Off: refused, and the agent tells you. With the defaults: into a VM at once, to your computer after your Allow. |

A question appears as a notice at the bottom right of the window and waits in Home › [Notifications](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/window.html#notifications) (*Needs you*), with its **Allow**, until it expires.

## Agents

### A Chat in a VM tab

The agent of a tab's Chat works in its VM's files directly: its commands and apps read and write them. For your computer's files (below your home folder) it has these tools:

| Tool | What it does |
|---|---|
| `computer.files.search` | Finds files of your computer by name, below your home (hidden ones only when asked, never keys, keyrings or browser profiles). |
| `computer.files.read` | Reads one file below your home, up to 256 KB per read. |
| `computer.files.copy` | Copies 1 to 64 files or folders of your computer into its VM (its `~/Downloads`, or the folder named). A taken name becomes `report (2).txt`. |
| `computer.files.upload` | Copies 1 to 64 VM files or folders to your computer (your `Downloads/From the VM`, or a folder below your home), as new files only. |
| `computer.files.replace` | Replaces a file on your computer with a VM file, only a file Wazza OS itself made there (an upload) that nobody changed since; never one of yours. |
| `computer.files.transfer` | How far a copy, upload or replace went: waiting for your Allow, running, done or failed. |

An example, on a VM tab's Chat with MiMo: *"Copy Documents/route-tests/report.txt from my computer into this VM's Documents folder. Then make report-checked.txt from it in the VM, with a last line: Checked in the VM. Then put report-checked.txt on my computer."*

![The Chat's steps: computer_files_read of the computer's report.txt, computer_files_copy into /home/ubuntu/Documents, read_file of report (3).txt, Write of report-checked.txt, computer_files_upload to Documents/route-tests, then the agent waiting for the user's Allow](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/img/move-agent-steps.webp)

The agent's steps: the copy landed as report (3).txt (two report files were already there); its upload waits for your Allow.

![Home, Notifications: vm-1's Chat asks to copy 1 item to this computer? report-checked.txt. Allow adds them to the computer's Documents/route-tests folder as new files; nothing on this computer is changed otherwise. Allow button. Below: vm-1's Chat copied 1 file (69 B) from this computer into /home/ubuntu/Documents](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/img/move-agent-allow.webp)

The upload's question (also shown as a notice at the bottom right), and the copy before it.

The copy into the VM ran at once (*vm-1's Chat copied 1 file (69 B) from this computer into /home/ubuntu/Documents*); the upload waited for **Allow**, then `report-checked.txt` was in the folder on the computer, and the agent read it back.

### The Computer Control Chat

The [Computer Control](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/computer-control.html) Chat runs on your computer, not in a VM: it lists, searches, reads and opens your files (below your home). It copies nothing into a VM.

### Agents outside Wazza OS

An agent connected through [`wazza-os mcp`](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/mcp.html#connect-an-agent-from-outside) moves files with the [`explorer`](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/mcp-tools.html#tool-explorer) tool, the same commands as the command line below:

| Verb | What it does |
|---|---|
| `copy_to_vm` | Files of your computer into a VM (default `~/Downloads`), by the file-copy setting: `{"verb":"copy_to_vm","paths":["~/report.pdf"],"vm":"vm-1","folder":"~/Documents"}` |
| `upload` | VM files to your computer, as new files (default `Downloads/From the VM`), by the file-copy setting: `{"verb":"upload","vm_paths":["~/Pictures/poster.png"]}` |
| `copies` | How far a `copy_to_vm` or `upload` went: `{"verb":"copies","id":"…"}` |
| `transfer` | A copy as your own Paste (any size) between your computer and a VM, or two VMs, into a folder: `{"verb":"transfer","from":"host","to":"vm-1","folder":"~/Documents","paths":["~/a.pdf"]}` |
| `clipboard_copy`, `clipboard_paste` | Files put on, and pasted from, the file clipboard, as a file manager's Copy and Paste |
| `import`, `stage` | One file of your computer into the VM's `~/Downloads`; one VM file copied into Wazza OS's share to read it on your computer |

## From the command line

```
$ wazza --gui explorer copy-to-vm ~/Documents/brief.txt --vm vm-1 --folder /home/ubuntu
$ wazza --gui explorer upload Pictures/hello-poster.png --vm vm-1
$ wazza --gui explorer transfer --from vm-1 --to host --folder ~/Documents Pictures/hello-poster.png
$ wazza --gui clipboard files
```

`clipboard files` prints the two file-copy settings and the copies waiting for your Allow. Every subcommand: [The command line › Files](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/cli.html#files).


---

Page: The Wazza OS MCP (Connect and automate)
Address: https://os-guide.wazza.ai/mcp.html

# The Wazza OS MCP

MCP (the Model Context Protocol) is the standard way an AI agent gets tools. Wazza OS gives the agent of every Chat its own tools through its MCP server, whatever the agent and the model: that is how an agent opens apps, works in them, handles files and starts other agents. You have nothing to set up. Agents that run outside Wazza OS get the same reach through `wazza-os mcp`.

- **What**: Wazza OS's tools for agents: apps, tabs, Drive, files, other agents, skills

- **Why**: Every agent, in every harness, can do real work in Wazza OS, the same way

- **Who**: Everyone (automatic in every Chat); developers who connect their own agents

- **Where**: Every Chat; outside agents: `wazza-os mcp`

## How it works

An MCP server lists tools: each with a name, what it does and its arguments. The agent's model reads the list, picks the tools a task needs and calls them; each answer comes back to the model. In Wazza OS, every Chat, whether its agent is Hermes, Prime Agent, Claude Code, Codex or Antigravity, is connected to Wazza OS's server (named `wazzastu` in agents' tool lists) when it starts. Each call shows in the Chat as a step you can open ([Follow the agent's work](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/chats.html#follow-the-agents-work)).

## The tools a Chat gets

| Family | What the agent can do | Ask, for example |
|---|---|---|
| Tabs and apps | Open apps in new tabs, read the tabs, close the tabs it opened; install and uninstall apps; add apps with a recipe ([Add your own apps](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/custom-apps.html)) | "Open Inkscape and draw a logo" |
| The app's own tools | In a tab where an app is open, that app's tools: GIMP has 40 (new image, layers, filters, text, export…), and Blender, ONLYOFFICE, Chromium and others have theirs | "Make the image 1920 pixels wide" |
| Drive | Look at any tab's screen and act on it with the mouse and keyboard ([Drive](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/drive.html)) | "Click Export in that dialog" |
| Files | The VM's files (list, open in an app, rename, move, delete); your computer's files below your home folder (search, read, copy into the VM, upload results to `Downloads/From the VM`, by your [Files & sharing](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/settings-files.html) rules: [Move files › Agents](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/files-move.html#agents)); company folders (read only) | "Find my latest invoice PDF and copy it into the VM" |
| Other agents | Start helper agents, visible in their own tabs or hidden; write to the Chat of another tab you opened and read its answer ([Several agents at once](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/parallel-tabs.html)) | "Have a Chromium agent collect the prices while you write the table" |
| Skills | Search and read skills, learn from this Chat, list and undo what was learned, use personas ([Skills](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/skills.html)) | "Learn from this chat now" |
| Wazza OS itself | Notifications, the VM's memory and what it has for heavy work, the computer check, the setup state, Wazza OS account tools | "How much memory can the VM use now?" |

## The rules the tools follow

- **Your view never changes.** A tab an agent opens opens in the background, with a badge; the tab you are looking at is never closed or moved.
- **Inside the VM, agents do not ask.** Commands, installs and steps in apps run at once ([Where Wazza OS asks you](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/privacy-security.html#where-wazza-os-asks-you)).
- **Some things only you can do.** Starting [Computer Control](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/computer-control.html), **Let this Chat edit my files**, turning on Local services, importing your Chrome profile and loosening the file-copy rules need your own click: an agent asking for them is refused, and tells you.
- **Each Chat works in its VM.** A Chat acts on the tabs of its own VM (it opens an app in another VM only when asked to); only the Computer Control Chat can look at your computer's screen.

## Connect an agent from outside Wazza OS

Agents that run outside Wazza OS, on your computer or on a server (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, VS Code, Gemini CLI and others), connect to `wazza-os mcp`: an MCP server that comes with Wazza OS. Its tools are the commands of [the command line](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/cli.html) (`vm`, `app`, `explorer`: its file copies are in [Move files](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/files-move.html#agents-outside-wazza-os), `drive`, `chat_transcript`, `timeouts`…), plus `ui` for the window's actions (open an app, send to a Chat…), `check` and `version`. Each call runs the same `wazza --gui …` command your terminal would, with your rights.

Add the server to your agent, once. Wazza OS can be closed while you do: it is only a line in your agent's settings. For Claude Code:

```
$ claude mcp add --scope user wazza-os -- wazza-os mcp
```

1. For another agent, `wazza-os mcp --print-config CLIENT` prints what to add (table below). Wazza OS never edits your agents' settings itself.
2. Start Wazza OS before you ask (on a server: [Wazza OS on a server](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/cli-server.html)).
3. Ask your agent, for example: *In Wazza OS, open Files in the background, ask its Chat what is in my Documents folder, and tell me.*

### Good to know

- **The tools need Wazza OS running.** With it closed, `status` and the other tools answer that the Wazza OS app is not running for this user; `check` (what this computer lacks) and `version` work anyway.
- **Who starts Wazza OS.** In the published build (0.2.0, build 44c5d0ea07c1) no tool starts it: the agent asks you to, and you start it from your app menu, with `wazzaos` in a terminal, or on a server with `wazza --virtual-screen=always`. From the next release, the `start` tool starts it.
- **Pictures of Wazza OS and input into it.** In the published build, `screenshot` and `native_input` work only with Wazza OS's own screen on a server ([the virtual screen](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/cli-server.html#the-virtual-screen)). From the next release they also work on a desktop, on Wazza OS's own window only: while an agent holds the input, a mark on the window says so.
- **Apps open in the background.** The agent opens an app inside Wazza OS with `ui` `open_app`: it gets a tab of its own in the background, and your screen stays as it is.

| Agent | `--print-config` | What to add |
|---|---|---|
| Claude Code | `claude` | `claude mcp add --scope user wazza-os -- wazza-os mcp` |
| Codex | `codex` | `codex mcp add wazza-os -- wazza-os mcp`, or in `~/.codex/config.toml`: `[mcp_servers.wazza-os]`, `command = "wazza-os"`, `args = ["mcp"]` |
| Cursor | `cursor` | `~/.cursor/mcp.json`: `{"mcpServers": {"wazza-os": {"command": "wazza-os", "args": ["mcp"]}}}` |
| VS Code | `vscode` | `.vscode/mcp.json`: `{"servers": {"wazza-os": {"type": "stdio", "command": "wazza-os", "args": ["mcp"]}}}` |
| Gemini CLI | `gemini` | `~/.gemini/settings.json`: `{"mcpServers": {"wazza-os": {"command": "wazza-os", "args": ["mcp"]}}}` |
| Hermes | `hermes` (coming in the next release) | In `~/.hermes/config.yaml`: see [below](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/mcp.html#hermes-and-prime-agent) |
| Prime Agent | `prime` (coming in the next release) | One `prime-agent mcp add` command: see [below](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/mcp.html#hermes-and-prime-agent) |
| Any other | `json` | `{"command": "wazza-os", "args": ["mcp"], "type": "stdio"}` |

### Hermes and Prime Agent

The two agents of Wazza OS's own Chats can also run on their own, outside Wazza OS. These lines work with the published build (0.2.0, build 44c5d0ea07c1; tested with the Hermes and Prime Agent versions Wazza OS ships: 40 tools, a `status` call answered). `--print-config hermes` and `--print-config prime`, which print exactly these lines, come in the next release.

**Prime Agent**: one command, which writes the server into `~/.prime/agent/settings.json`:

```
$ prime-agent mcp add wazza-os --env XDG_RUNTIME_DIR=XDG_RUNTIME_DIR --env DISPLAY=DISPLAY --env WAYLAND_DISPLAY=WAYLAND_DISPLAY -- wazza-os mcp
```

Prime Agent gives a server only `HOME`, `PATH` and `TMPDIR`. The `--env` parts pass on `XDG_RUNTIME_DIR`, without which `wazza-os mcp` cannot find the running Wazza OS (every call would say it is not running), and your display, for the next release's `start` tool. A variable your session does not have is passed on empty, which does no harm.

**Hermes**: add this to `~/.hermes/config.yaml`, under `mcp_servers`:

```
mcp_servers:
  wazza-os:
    command: wazza-os
    args: ["mcp"]
    enabled: true
    timeout: 600
    env:
      DISPLAY: ${DISPLAY}
      WAYLAND_DISPLAY: ${WAYLAND_DISPLAY}
```

`timeout: 600` lets one call run up to 10 minutes (Hermes stops a call after 5 by default, and a Drive step can take longer). Hermes gives a server only a few environment variables (`XDG_RUNTIME_DIR` among them, which `wazza-os mcp` needs): `env` passes your display on, so that the next release's `start` tool can open Wazza OS's window on your desktop. To let the next release's `provider_keys` read an API key from the environment (`add_from_env`), list that variable under `env` too.

### What the agent does

1. `status`: is Wazza OS running? If not, every tool answers that the Wazza OS app is not running for this user, and the agent asks you to start it.
2. `vm` (list, start): the VMs.
3. `ui` `open_app`: the app opens in a background tab; your screen stays as it is. `vm_tabs_read` gives its tab.
4. `ui` `chat_send` to that tab's Chat (a Chat never shown starts in the background), then `chat_transcript` reads its answer.
5. `drive` look and act, for work in the app itself.

### What stays yours

- Computer Control starts only with your own click; the tools are refused it.
- Deleting or resetting a VM, removing data and similar commands need the command line's own confirmations (the `yes` argument, or the typed words *REMOVE ALL DATA*), and are marked as destructive, so agents ask you before calling them.
- The `pro` and `wazza_tools` tools spend Wazza Pro credits: they run only with `confirm_spend`, and only when you asked for that run.
- Passwords and keys travel only as the command's standard input, never in a command line.
- Nothing runs while it is idle: the server lives only while your agent runs it.

Every tool with what it does, its arguments and an example: [Every Wazza OS MCP tool](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/mcp-tools.html) (the same text as `wazza-os mcp --print-docs`). An agent without MCP runs the same commands in its shell ([The command line](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/cli.html)).


---

Page: Every MCP tool (Connect and automate)
Address: https://os-guide.wazza.ai/mcp-tools.html

# Every Wazza OS MCP tool

The tools `wazza-os mcp` gives an agent that runs outside Wazza OS: each one is a command of [the command line](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/cli.html). Below: how an agent uses them, then every tool with what it does, its arguments and an example.

- **What**: The reference of every tool of `wazza-os mcp`

- **Why**: To know what an outside agent can do in Wazza OS, and how to ask

- **Who**: Anyone connecting Claude Code, Codex, Cursor or another agent

- **Where**: Set up on [The Wazza OS MCP](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/mcp.html#connect-an-agent-from-outside)

## Find the tool for a task

| To… | The agent uses |
|---|---|
| see whether Wazza OS runs, and what this computer lacks | [`status`](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/mcp-tools.html#tool-status), [`check`](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/mcp-tools.html#tool-check) |
| open an app in a tab, read the tabs, send to a tab's Chat | [`ui`](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/mcp-tools.html#tool-ui) (actions `open_app`, `vm_tabs_read`, `chat_send`) |
| read a Chat's conversation | [`chat_transcript`](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/mcp-tools.html#tool-chat_transcript) |
| list the apps, check whether one is installed, uninstall it, add your own | [`app`](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/mcp-tools.html#tool-app) |
| put files into a VM, or bring them out | [`explorer`](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/mcp-tools.html#tool-explorer) (`copy_to_vm`, `upload`) |
| see and use an app's screen | [`drive`](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/mcp-tools.html#tool-drive) (look, act) |
| start, stop or back up VMs; their memory, disk and graphics | [`vm`](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/mcp-tools.html#tool-vm), [`vm_memory`](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/mcp-tools.html#tool-vm_memory), [`vm_disk`](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/mcp-tools.html#tool-vm_disk), [`vm_gpu`](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/mcp-tools.html#tool-vm_gpu), [`gpu`](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/mcp-tools.html#tool-gpu) |
| API keys and sign-ins | [`provider_keys`](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/mcp-tools.html#tool-provider_keys), [`provider_signin`](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/mcp-tools.html#tool-provider_signin), [`wazza_account`](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/mcp-tools.html#tool-wazza_account) |
| settings of new Chats and their limits | [`chat_model`](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/mcp-tools.html#tool-chat_model), [`timeouts`](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/mcp-tools.html#tool-timeouts), [`local_services`](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/mcp-tools.html#tool-local_services) |
| a picture of Wazza OS itself (published build: on a server only; from the next release also on a desktop, its own window) | [`screenshot`](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/mcp-tools.html#tool-screenshot) |
| a recording of Wazza OS's own screen on a server | [`record`](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/mcp-tools.html#tool-record) |

Each tool's table: the *verb* (what the tool does this time), its *arguments*, what it does, and an example: the tool's arguments, then `→` the command it runs. This page is made from the same text that `wazza-os mcp --print-docs` prints for the next release. The published build (0.2.0, build 44c5d0ea07c1) has 40 of these tools; new in the next release: the [`start`](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/mcp-tools.html#tool-start) tool; [`provider_keys`](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/mcp-tools.html#tool-provider_keys)' `add_from_env` and `add_from_file`; [`ui`](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/mcp-tools.html#tool-ui)'s `outcome` verb and `timeout_ms`; [`screenshot`](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/mcp-tools.html#tool-screenshot) and [`native_input`](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/mcp-tools.html#tool-native_input) on a desktop, and `native_input`'s `scroll`. In both builds, `explorer`'s `upload` without a folder puts the files in `Downloads/From the VM` (its description below still says `Downloads`).

## How an agent uses them

Wazza OS runs apps in virtual machines (VMs vm-1 to vm-8) on this computer; each app opens in a tab, and each tab has its own Chat (an AI agent). These tools are Wazza OS's own command line (`wazza --gui ...`): each one runs that CLI and answers its output and exit status (exit 2: the CLI refused the arguments, its usage text says how; nothing was done).

### The typical flow

1. status: is the Wazza OS app running? If not: start it with start (unless the user said not to start it); it waits until the app answers and returns its window state (check says what this computer lacks when it cannot start).
2. vm {verb: "list"}: the VMs; vm {verb: "start", vm: "vm-2"} starts a stopped one (minutes; list again).
3. ui {verb: "do", action: "open_app", args: {appId: "files", vmId: "vm-1"}}: the app opens in a background tab (the user's screen stays as it is); ui {verb: "do", action: "vm_tabs_read", args: {vm: "vm-1"}} names its tab id. app {verb: "list"} lists the apps, app {verb: "status", app_id} whether one is installed.
4. Chat: ui {verb: "do", action: "chat_send", args: {vmId, tabId, childId: "", text}} (childId "": the tab's own Chat, always named; a tab's Chat that never started starts behind the view); then chat_transcript {tab, vm, last: 5} reads its answer.
5. Drive (GUI work in a tab's app): drive {verb: "look", vm, tab} returns an image and a snapshot_id; drive {verb: "act", vm, tab, args: {snapshot_id, action: "left_click", x, y}} runs one action and returns the next view: check it, then the next act.
6. Files: explorer (a VM's files; this computer's with computer: true; copy_to_vm, upload). Settings: vm_memory, vm_disk, vm_gpu, gpu, chat_model, timeouts, local_services, clipboard. Updates: ui {verb: "do", action: "update_read"} and "update_check" (installing an update is the user's own). Everything else: invoke.
7. Sign the app's Chats in (the user's own accounts; a token is never copied from one program to another): provider_signin {verb: "status"} lists the providers, their methods and what is signed in. A login: provider_signin {verb: "start", provider, method: "oauth"} answers its attempt and auth ids; {verb: "open", attempt, auth, browser: "external"} opens its page in the user's own browser, where the user approves once; {verb: "poll", attempt, auth} until it is done; {verb: "commit", attempt, auth} keeps it; status then shows it verified (it is signed in only once verified). On a server (no browser here): open answers the link instead; give it to the user, who approves on any device and gives you the code it shows; {verb: "submit", attempt, auth, prompt, secret: <the code>} (sent on stdin). Claude's plan login (Claude Code's own, as setup run's logins): invoke {verb: "modules_call", module: "agent", method: "claude_code_signin", args: {op: "start"}} answers its attemptId; {op: "status", attemptId} names its authUrl: the user opens it, signs in and is shown a code; {op: "submit", attemptId, code}; {op: "status", attemptId} until state done, its account named. An API key: provider_keys {verb: "add_from_env", provider, from_env: <variable>} reads it from your own environment (the user exports it, e.g. OPENROUTER_API_KEY): it never passes through your model; add_from_file reads a 0600 file.
8. Screens: screenshot answers the Wazza OS window's own picture (its virtual screen, or on a desktop the app's own window); native_input begin, then focus/pointer/click/key/text/scroll, then end, acts in that window only. Look before you click: screenshot, one action, screenshot again.

### The rules

these tools act with the user's own CLI rights: keep the user's screen as it is unless the user asked to see something (no focus, no Settings page opened on its own). A refusal names its code and why (user_only_app: Computer Control opens only by the user's own click); busy or not ready: call again in a few seconds; ui_outcome_pending (a window action still running after the CLI followed it for 5 minutes): read it with ui {verb: "outcome", outcome: <its id>}, never send the action again. Destructive verbs (delete, reset, remove_all, quit...) only when the user asked for exactly that. pro and wazza_tools runs spend Wazza Pro credits.
