### `status`

Whether the Wazza OS app is running on this computer and its main window's state (visible, focused, its virtual screen). Call it first: an error means the Wazza OS app is not running (start starts it, unless the user said not to).

| verb | arguments | what it does | example |
|---|---|---|---|
| - | - | the running app's window state | `{}` → `wazza --gui status` |

### `start`

Start the Wazza OS app when it is not running (CLI `wazza start`): on a desktop as the user's own start (its window on the user's screen), with no display (a server, SSH) on its own virtual screen, the manual's server mode. Already running: it says so and starts nothing. It waits until the app answers (timeout, default 120 s) and answers its window state as status does. Call it when status says the app is not running, unless the user said not to start it.

| verb | arguments | what it does | example |
|---|---|---|---|
| - | `timeout` (optional): how long to wait for the app to answer, in seconds (5 to 600; default 120) | start the Wazza OS app (or say it already runs) and answer its window state | `{}` → `wazza start` |

### `check`

What this computer gives Wazza OS (KVM, a systemd user session, X11, the Chat sandbox, the GPU) and how to fix what is missing; works with the Wazza OS app stopped. Exit status 1 when something is missing.

| verb | arguments | what it does | example |
|---|---|---|---|
| - | `json` (optional): answer in JSON instead of words | the computer check | `{"json":true}` → `wazza --check --json` |

### `version`

The installed Wazza OS version (works with the Wazza OS app stopped). The running build and the installed package, side by side: ui {action: "version_read"}.

| verb | arguments | what it does | example |
|---|---|---|---|
| - | - | the version | `{}` → `wazza --version` |

### `ui`

The Wazza OS app's window actions (the CLI's `wazza --gui invoke modules_call ui do`): open apps in tabs, read tabs and what the user sees, send to a tab's Chat, read Chats, settings, updates and 200 more. They run as the user's own CLI: keep the user's view as it is unless the user asked to see something (open_app opens in a background tab unless focus: true; focus_tab, open_settings and the like change the screen). Most used actions (args): open_app {appId, vmId?, url?, file?}; app_open_in_vm {appId, vm}; vm_tabs_read {vm}; tabs_read {vmId?}; view_read {}; close_tab {tabId, vmId}; tab_rename {tabId, title}; tab_open_with {vmId, path}; chat_send {vmId, tabId, childId: "", text} (childId is required: "" is the tab's own Chat, a subagent's id comes from chat_subagent_list; a tab whose Chat never started starts it behind the view); chat_stop {vmId, tabId}; chat_set_model {vmId, tabId, modelId}; chat_list_threads {vmId, tabId}; chat_conversation_read {vmId, tabId, last?}; chat_default_read {}; chat_default_set {harnessId, modelId}; vm_list {}; vm_start {vm}; start_sandbox {}; settings_get {}; skills_native_read {}; version_read {}; update_read {}; update_check {}. Every action with its arguments: verb catalog. A refusal names its code (user_only_app: Computer Control opens only by the user's own click). A slow action (open_app while its VM is busy) is followed until the window reports it, up to 5 minutes; an answer that still says ui_outcome_pending names its outcome id: read it with verb outcome {outcome: <that id>} (again until it is no longer pending), never by sending the action again.

| verb | arguments | what it does | example |
|---|---|---|---|
| do | `action`: the action's id (verb catalog lists them); `args` (optional): the action's arguments (its catalog schema); `timeout_ms` (optional): how long the window's answer is awaited before it is followed (ms, at most 25000; default the action's own) | run one window action (its answer is followed until the window reports it) | `{"verb":"do","action":"open_app","args":{"appId":"files","vmId":"vm-1"}}` → `wazza --gui invoke modules_call ui do -` |
| outcome | `outcome`: the outcome id a ui_outcome_pending answer names; `timeout_ms` (optional): how long to wait for it now (ms, at most 25000) | what a window action that answered ui_outcome_pending did, once the window reports it | `{"verb":"outcome","outcome":"fc674edf422d2a11937349f7ff8c108d","timeout_ms":20000}` → `wazza --gui invoke modules_call ui outcome -` |
| catalog | - | every action with its summary, view class and argument schema | `{"verb":"catalog"}` → `wazza --gui invoke modules_call ui catalog -` |

### `vm`

Wazza OS's virtual machines by number: vm-1 starts with the Wazza OS app, vm-2 to vm-8 are extra ones (CLI `wazza --gui vm`). A cold start takes minutes: watch verb list. Use delete, reset and restore with into only when the user asked for exactly that: they remove a disk for good.

| verb | arguments | what it does | example |
|---|---|---|---|
| list | - | every VM: running, starting or stopped, its disk | `{"verb":"list"}` → `wazza --gui vm list` |
| create | - | a new VM, stopped, with the lowest free number | `{"verb":"create"}` → `wazza --gui vm create` |
| start | `vm`: the VM by number: vm-1 to vm-8 | start a stopped VM (vm-2 to vm-8; vm-1 starts with the Wazza OS app, or ui {action: "start_sandbox"}) | `{"verb":"start","vm":"vm-2"}` → `wazza --gui vm start vm-2` |
| stop | `vm`: the VM by number: vm-1 to vm-8 | stop a running VM (its apps end; its disk is kept) (removes or ends something) | `{"verb":"stop","vm":"vm-2"}` → `wazza --gui vm stop vm-2` |
| delete | `vm`: the VM by number: vm-1 to vm-8; `yes`: true: you mean it (the disk goes for good) | remove a stopped VM and its disk for good (removes or ends something) | `{"verb":"delete","vm":"vm-3","yes":true}` → `wazza --gui vm delete vm-3 --yes` |
| reset | `vm`: the VM by number: vm-1 to vm-8; `yes`: true: you mean it (the disk goes for good) | make a stopped VM new: its disk removed for good, its number kept (removes or ends something) | `{"verb":"reset","vm":"vm-3","yes":true}` → `wazza --gui vm reset vm-3 --yes` |
| backup | `vm`: the VM by number: vm-1 to vm-8 | a backup zip of a VM in Downloads | `{"verb":"backup","vm":"vm-2"}` → `wazza --gui vm backup vm-2` |
| backups | - | the backups and the backup job that runs | `{"verb":"backups"}` → `wazza --gui vm backups` |
| restore | `backup`: a backup's id (verb backups) or the path of its .zip; `into` (optional): a stopped VM whose disk the backup replaces for good; `yes` (optional): true with into: you mean it | a new VM from a backup; with into and yes, replace a stopped VM's disk (removes or ends something) | `{"verb":"restore","backup":"bk-1"}` → `wazza --gui vm restore bk-1` |

### `vm_memory`

A VM's RAM (CLI `wazza --gui vm-memory`): read it, set it, or let Wazza OS scale it automatically.

| verb | arguments | what it does | example |
|---|---|---|---|
| status | `vm` (optional): the VM by number: vm-1 (the default) to vm-8 | the VM's RAM now, its bounds and the policy | `{"verb":"status"}` → `wazza --gui vm-memory status` |
| set | `mib`: the RAM in MiB; `vm` (optional): the VM by number: vm-1 (the default) to vm-8 | give the VM this much RAM now (live) | `{"verb":"set","mib":8192,"vm":"vm-1"}` → `wazza --gui vm-memory set 8192 --vm vm-1` |
| auto | `percent`: the share of this computer's RAM auto-scale may give (10-100); `min` (optional): the least RAM in MiB | let Wazza OS scale the RAM to what the VM needs | `{"verb":"auto","percent":50}` → `wazza --gui vm-memory auto 50` |
| min | `mib`: the least RAM in MiB | the least RAM auto-scale keeps | `{"verb":"min","mib":4096}` → `wazza --gui vm-memory min 4096` |

### `vm_disk`

A VM's root disk (CLI `wazza --gui vm-disk`): its size and free room; grow it (it never shrinks back).

| verb | arguments | what it does | example |
|---|---|---|---|
| status | `vm` (optional): the VM by number: vm-1 (the default) to vm-8 | the disk's size, use and target | `{"verb":"status"}` → `wazza --gui vm-disk status` |
| set | `gib`: the new size in GiB; `vm` (optional): the VM by number: vm-1 (the default) to vm-8 | grow the disk to this size (uses this computer's disk; it never shrinks back) | `{"verb":"set","gib":80}` → `wazza --gui vm-disk set 80` |

### `vm_gpu`

The GPU memory Wazza OS's VMs may use (CLI `wazza --gui vm-gpu`).

| verb | arguments | what it does | example |
|---|---|---|---|
| status | - | each VM's GPU memory and the bound | `{"verb":"status"}` → `wazza --gui vm-gpu status` |
| auto | `percent`: the share of the GPU's memory | scale it automatically | `{"verb":"auto","percent":50}` → `wazza --gui vm-gpu auto 50` |
| set | `mib`: the GPU memory in MiB | a fixed GPU memory | `{"verb":"set","mib":2048}` → `wazza --gui vm-gpu set 2048` |

### `gpu`

How the VMs use this computer's graphics cards (CLI `wazza --gui gpu`; Settings › Graphics): virtualized, a native card lent to a VM, or none.

| verb | arguments | what it does | example |
|---|---|---|---|
| status | - | the mode, the cards and each VM's paths | `{"verb":"status"}` → `wazza --gui gpu status` |
| mode | `mode`: the GPU mode | set the GPU mode | `{"verb":"mode","mode":"virtualized"}` → `wazza --gui gpu mode virtualized` |
| card | `card`: auto, auto:N[:API], or PCI addresses PCI[,PCI...] | which card native mode lends | `{"verb":"card","card":"auto"}` → `wazza --gui gpu card auto` |

### `vm_resources`

What a VM has now and the most auto-scale gives it (vCPUs, RAM, GPU, disk) and this computer's CPUs, load, RAM, GPUs and free disk (CLI `wazza --gui vm-resources`). Read it before a render, a build or a large install.

| verb | arguments | what it does | example |
|---|---|---|---|
| - | `vm` (optional): the VM by number: vm-1 (the default) to vm-8 | the resources | `{"vm":"vm-1"}` → `wazza --gui vm-resources --vm vm-1` |

### `data`

Wazza OS's own data on this computer (CLI `wazza --gui data`). remove_all removes ALL of it (VMs, settings, sign-ins, Chats, logs, caches) for good at the next start: only when the user asked for exactly that, with the typed words.

| verb | arguments | what it does | example |
|---|---|---|---|
| status | - | Wazza OS's folders, their sizes, a waiting removal | `{"verb":"status"}` → `wazza --gui data status` |
| remove_all | `confirm`: exactly REMOVE ALL DATA | remove all of Wazza OS's data (the Wazza OS app closes) (removes or ends something) | `{"verb":"remove_all","confirm":"REMOVE ALL DATA"}` → `wazza --gui data remove-all --confirm 'REMOVE ALL DATA'` |
| cancel | - | cancel a removal still waiting for the next start | `{"verb":"cancel"}` → `wazza --gui data cancel` |

### `app`

Apps of Wazza OS's catalog and the user's own (CLI `wazza --gui app`): list, read and check manifests, install state, save a custom app, uninstall, follow and cancel jobs, an app's MCP, templates. Open an app in a tab: ui {action: "open_app"}. Install a catalog app on the VM shown: ui {action: "open_app"} opens and installs it, or invoke {verb: "modules_call", module: "packages", method: "install_request", args: {appId, vmId}}.

| verb | arguments | what it does | example |
|---|---|---|---|
| list | - | the app catalog | `{"verb":"list"}` → `wazza --gui app list` |
| get | `app_id`: the app's id (app {verb: "list"} lists them: gimp, vscodium...) | an app's manifest | `{"verb":"get","app_id":"gimp"}` → `wazza --gui app get gimp` |
| validate | `manifest`: the manifest (with its skill files) to check | check a manifest; its errors by cause | `{"verb":"validate","manifest":{"manifest":{"name":"Hello"}}}` → `wazza --gui app validate --stdin` |
| status | `app_id`: the app's id (app {verb: "list"} lists them: gimp, vscodium...); `vm` (optional): the VM by number: vm-1 (the default) to vm-8; `refresh` (optional): check it again in the VM now | whether an app is installed in a VM, installing, or why not | `{"verb":"status","app_id":"gimp","vm":"vm-1"}` → `wazza --gui app status gimp --vm vm-1` |
| save | `manifest`: {manifest, skills, expectedRevision?}; `install` (optional): install it once saved; `vm` (optional): the VM by number: vm-1 (the default) to vm-8; `focus` (optional): show it on the user's screen (changes what the user sees: only when the user asked) | save a custom app (new, or a new revision) | `{"verb":"save","manifest":{"manifest":{"name":"Hello"}},"install":true}` → `wazza --gui app save --stdin --install` |
| uninstall | `app_id`: the app's id (app {verb: "list"} lists them: gimp, vscodium...); `vm` (optional): the VM by number: vm-1 (the default) to vm-8; `close_tabs` (optional): close its open tabs first; `purge_data` (optional): remove its user data too; `focus` (optional): show it on the user's screen (changes what the user sees: only when the user asked); `follow` (optional): wait and print the job's output until it ends (minutes for an install) | uninstall an app from a VM (removes or ends something) | `{"verb":"uninstall","app_id":"gimp","vm":"vm-1"}` → `wazza --gui app uninstall gimp --vm vm-1` |
| uninstall_plan | `app_id`: the app's id (app {verb: "list"} lists them: gimp, vscodium...); `vm` (optional): the VM by number: vm-1 (the default) to vm-8; `close_tabs` (optional): with closing its open tabs; `purge_data` (optional): with removing its user data | what an uninstall would remove | `{"verb":"uninstall_plan","app_id":"gimp"}` → `wazza --gui app uninstall-plan gimp` |
| remove | `app_id`: the app's id (app {verb: "list"} lists them: gimp, vscodium...); `forget_vm` (optional): VMs whose record of it goes too | remove a custom app from Wazza OS (removes or ends something) | `{"verb":"remove","app_id":"custom-0123abcd"}` → `wazza --gui app remove custom-0123abcd` |
| observe | `job_id`: the job's id an install, uninstall or MCP request answered; `since` (optional): the output offset to read from (the last answer's next); `follow` (optional): wait and print the job's output until it ends (minutes for an install) | a job's state and output | `{"verb":"observe","job_id":"job-1","since":0}` → `wazza --gui app observe job-1 --since 0` |
| cancel | `job_id`: the job's id an install, uninstall or MCP request answered; `focus` (optional): show it on the user's screen (changes what the user sees: only when the user asked) | cancel an app job | `{"verb":"cancel","job_id":"job-1"}` → `wazza --gui app cancel job-1` |
| mcp_install | `app_id`: the app's id (app {verb: "list"} lists them: gimp, vscodium...); `vm` (optional): the VM by number: vm-1 (the default) to vm-8; `follow` (optional): wait and print the job's output until it ends (minutes for an install) | install an app's MCP in a VM (its Chats list its tools again) | `{"verb":"mcp_install","app_id":"gimp"}` → `wazza --gui app mcp-install gimp` |
| mcp_uninstall | `app_id`: the app's id (app {verb: "list"} lists them: gimp, vscodium...); `vm` (optional): the VM by number: vm-1 (the default) to vm-8; `follow` (optional): wait and print the job's output until it ends (minutes for an install) | remove an app's MCP from a VM | `{"verb":"mcp_uninstall","app_id":"gimp"}` → `wazza --gui app mcp-uninstall gimp` |
| template | `kind`: an apt package app or a script app; `mcp` (optional): with a headless MCP server; `skill` (optional): with a SKILL.md | a manifest template to fill | `{"verb":"template","kind":"apt","skill":true}` → `wazza --gui app template apt --skill` |

### `explorer`

Files (CLI `wazza --gui explorer`): a VM's files (list, rename, move, delete, permissions, stage one for reading on this computer, its default app), this computer's home (list, details, open, search, read with computer: true), and copies between this computer and the VMs. Changes act only on the item a fresh list named (expect); delete is permanent (yes).

| verb | arguments | what it does | example |
|---|---|---|---|
| list | `path` (optional): a folder (default the home); `vm` (optional): the VM by number: vm-1 (the default) to vm-8; `computer` (optional): this computer's home instead of a VM | a folder's entries with their ids | `{"verb":"list","path":"~/Documents"}` → `wazza --gui explorer list ~/Documents` |
| rename | `path`: a path in the VM: ~/... (the VM's home), absolute, or relative to the Chat folder; vm-N:/... names the VM; `new_name`: the new name; `expect` (optional): the item's id from a fresh explorer list: the change acts only on that very item; `vm` (optional): the VM by number: vm-1 (the default) to vm-8 | rename one item | `{"verb":"rename","path":"~/a.txt","new_name":"b.txt"}` → `wazza --gui explorer rename ~/a.txt b.txt` |
| move | `path`: a path in the VM: ~/... (the VM's home), absolute, or relative to the Chat folder; vm-N:/... names the VM; `target_folder`: the folder it moves into; `name` (optional): a new name there; `expect` (optional): the item's id from a fresh explorer list: the change acts only on that very item; `vm` (optional): the VM by number: vm-1 (the default) to vm-8 | move one item | `{"verb":"move","path":"~/a.txt","target_folder":"~/Documents"}` → `wazza --gui explorer move ~/a.txt ~/Documents` |
| delete | `path`: a path in the VM: ~/... (the VM's home), absolute, or relative to the Chat folder; vm-N:/... names the VM; `yes`: true: you mean it (there is no trash); `expect` (optional): the item's id from a fresh explorer list: the change acts only on that very item; `vm` (optional): the VM by number: vm-1 (the default) to vm-8 | delete one item for good (a folder only when empty) (removes or ends something) | `{"verb":"delete","path":"~/old.txt","yes":true}` → `wazza --gui explorer delete ~/old.txt --yes` |
| permissions | `path`: a path in the VM: ~/... (the VM's home), absolute, or relative to the Chat folder; vm-N:/... names the VM; `mode`: chmod's three octal digits (644, 755); `recursive` (optional): a folder's items too; `expect` (optional): the item's id from a fresh explorer list: the change acts only on that very item; `vm` (optional): the VM by number: vm-1 (the default) to vm-8 | change an item's permissions | `{"verb":"permissions","path":"~/run.sh","mode":"755"}` → `wazza --gui explorer permissions ~/run.sh 755` |
| stage | `path`: a path in the VM: ~/... (the VM's home), absolute, or relative to the Chat folder; vm-N:/... names the VM; `vm` (optional): the VM by number: vm-1 (the default) to vm-8 | copy one VM file into Wazza's share and print its path on this computer (to read or preview it) | `{"verb":"stage","path":"~/Pictures/a.png"}` → `wazza --gui explorer stage ~/Pictures/a.png` |
| default_app | `path`: a path in the VM: ~/... (the VM's home), absolute, or relative to the Chat folder; vm-N:/... names the VM; `vm` (optional): the VM by number: vm-1 (the default) to vm-8 | the Wazza OS app the VM opens that file with | `{"verb":"default_app","path":"~/a.svg"}` → `wazza --gui explorer default-app ~/a.svg` |
| details | `path`: a path in this computer's home (~/..., computer:~/...); `computer` (optional): true: this computer's home | one entry of this computer's home | `{"verb":"details","path":"~/a.txt","computer":true}` → `wazza --gui explorer details ~/a.txt --computer` |
| open | `path`: a path in this computer's home; `computer` (optional): true: this computer's home | open a file of this computer with its default app (on the user's screen: only when asked) | `{"verb":"open","path":"~/a.pdf","computer":true}` → `wazza --gui explorer open ~/a.pdf --computer` |
| import | `path`: a file or folder of this computer's home; `vm` (optional): the VM by number: vm-1 (the default) to vm-8 | copy a file of this computer into the VM's ~/Downloads (run again to see how far it went) | `{"verb":"import","path":"~/a.pdf"}` → `wazza --gui explorer import ~/a.pdf` |
| transfer | `from` (optional): host or vm-N (default host); `to` (optional): host or vm-N (default host); `folder` (optional): the folder it pastes into; `id` (optional): a transfer's id: its progress (or cancel it); `cancel` (optional): with id: stop that transfer; `paths` (optional): the files and folders to copy | copy files between this computer and a VM, or between VMs; with id, its progress | `{"verb":"transfer","to":"vm-1","folder":"~/Downloads","paths":["~/a.pdf"]}` → `wazza --gui explorer transfer --to vm-1 --folder ~/Downloads ~/a.pdf` |
| clipboard_copy | `from` (optional): host or vm-N (default host); `id` (optional): a copy's id: its state; `paths` (optional): the files to put on Wazza OS's file clipboard | copy files onto Wazza OS's file clipboard | `{"verb":"clipboard_copy","paths":["~/a.pdf"]}` → `wazza --gui explorer clipboard-copy ~/a.pdf` |
| clipboard_paste | `to` (optional): host or vm-N (default host); `folder` (optional): the folder it pastes into; `id` (optional): a paste's id: its state | paste the file clipboard into a folder | `{"verb":"clipboard_paste","to":"vm-1","folder":"~/Downloads"}` → `wazza --gui explorer clipboard-paste --to vm-1 --folder ~/Downloads` |
| search | `words`: the words to find in file names; `computer`: true: this computer's home; `in` (optional): a folder to search in; `limit` (optional): the most results | find files of this computer's home by name | `{"verb":"search","words":["invoice"],"computer":true}` → `wazza --gui explorer search invoice --computer` |
| read | `path`: a file of this computer's home; `computer`: true: this computer's home; `offset` (optional): the byte to start at; `length` (optional): how many bytes | read a file of this computer's home | `{"verb":"read","path":"~/notes.txt","computer":true}` → `wazza --gui explorer read ~/notes.txt --computer` |
| copy_to_vm | `paths`: files of this computer; `vm` (optional): the VM by number: vm-1 (the default) to vm-8; `folder` (optional): the VM folder (default ~/Downloads) | copy files of this computer into a VM (the user's file copy permission applies) | `{"verb":"copy_to_vm","paths":["~/a.pdf"],"vm":"vm-1"}` → `wazza --gui explorer copy-to-vm ~/a.pdf --vm vm-1` |
| upload | `vm_paths`: files of the VM; `vm` (optional): the VM by number: vm-1 (the default) to vm-8; `folder` (optional): the folder of this computer (default Downloads) | copy VM files to this computer (never overwrites: a new name when taken) | `{"verb":"upload","vm_paths":["~/render.png"]}` → `wazza --gui explorer upload ~/render.png` |
| replace | `vm_path`: the VM file; `target`: the file of this computer it replaces (one Wazza OS made); `vm` (optional): the VM by number: vm-1 (the default) to vm-8 | replace a file of this computer that Wazza OS made with a VM file | `{"verb":"replace","vm_path":"~/a.png","target":"~/Downloads/a.png"}` → `wazza --gui explorer replace ~/a.png ~/Downloads/a.png` |
| copies | `id`: a copy's id (copy_to_vm or upload answered it) | how far a copy went | `{"verb":"copies","id":"cp-1"}` → `wazza --gui explorer copies --id cp-1` |

### `drive`

Drive: see and use an app's window in a tab like a person does (CLI `wazza --gui drive` and `wazza --gui invoke modules_call drive`). look returns one image of the tab and a snapshot_id; act runs ONE action on it (x, y are pixels of that image) and returns the next view: check it before the next act. Actions (args.action): left_click, double_click, right_click, left_click_drag (x2, y2), scroll, type_text (text, ASCII), paste_utf8 (text), key (keys: ["ctrl+s"]), key_chord, hold_key, wait (until: "changed"). Refusals: stale_snapshot (look again), user_input_active (the user types: wait, look again), input_locked_by_user (ask the user to unlock the tab). context lists what the tab offers; recover restarts a stuck tab's Drive.

| verb | arguments | what it does | example |
|---|---|---|---|
| look | `vm`: the tab's VM (vm-1...); `tab`: the tab's id; `args` (optional): Drive's look fields: mode ("lean"), zoom [x, y, w, h], ... | one image of the tab and its snapshot_id (single use, 300 s) | `{"verb":"look","vm":"vm-1","tab":"t2","args":{"mode":"lean"}}` → `wazza --gui invoke modules_call drive look - --image-out '<images>'` |
| act | `vm`: the tab's VM; `tab`: the tab's id; `args`: Drive's act fields: snapshot_id, action, x, y, text, keys, ... | one action on the last look, then the next view | `{"verb":"act","vm":"vm-1","tab":"t2","args":{"snapshot_id":"s1","action":"left_click","x":40,"y":60}}` → `wazza --gui invoke modules_call drive act - --image-out '<images>'` |
| context | `vm`: the tab's VM; `tab`: the tab's id | what Drive can do on the tab now (its seats, whether it is in view) | `{"verb":"context","vm":"vm-1","tab":"t2"}` → `wazza --gui invoke modules_call drive context -` |
| record | `vm`: the tab's VM; `tab`: the tab's id; `args`: op: start \| stop \| status \| release, recording_id | record the tab (start, then stop with its recording_id) | `{"verb":"record","vm":"vm-1","tab":"t2","args":{"op":"start"}}` → `wazza --gui invoke modules_call drive record - --image-out '<images>'` |
| evidence | `vm`: the tab's VM; `tab`: the tab's id; `args`: op: status \| export \| keep \| retire | the before/after images Drive kept of a tab's Chat | `{"verb":"evidence","vm":"vm-1","tab":"t2","args":{"op":"status"}}` → `wazza --gui invoke modules_call drive evidence -` |
| recover | `tab`: the tab's id (t1, t2...: ui {action: "vm_tabs_read"} lists a VM's tabs); `vm` (optional): the VM by number: vm-1 (the default) to vm-8 | restart a tab's stuck Drive (no input, no view change) | `{"verb":"recover","tab":"t2"}` → `wazza --gui drive recover --tab t2` |

### `chat_transcript`

Read one tab's Chat conversation whole (CLI `wazza --gui chat-transcript`): the user's messages and each answer's message, thinking, tool and bash entries, oldest first. Send to a Chat with ui {action: "chat_send"}, then read its answer here (last: 5).

| verb | arguments | what it does | example |
|---|---|---|---|
| - | `tab`: the tab's id (t1, t2...: ui {action: "vm_tabs_read"} lists a VM's tabs); `vm` (optional): the VM by number: vm-1 (the default) to vm-8; `thread` (optional): one of the Chat's threads (default the selected one); `kinds` (optional): comma list of user,message,thinking,tool,bash,error; `roles` (optional): comma list of user,assistant; `contains` (optional): only entries with this text (any case); `from` (optional): entries from this number on; `last` (optional): only the newest N entries | the conversation | `{"tab":"t2","vm":"vm-1","last":5}` → `wazza --gui chat-transcript --tab t2 --vm vm-1 --last 5` |

### `chat_queue`

The messages queued while a tab's Chat answers (CLI `wazza --gui chat-queue`): list, edit, discard.

| verb | arguments | what it does | example |
|---|---|---|---|
| list | `tab`: the tab's id (t1, t2...: ui {action: "vm_tabs_read"} lists a VM's tabs); `vm` (optional): the VM by number: vm-1 (the default) to vm-8 | the queued messages with their ids | `{"verb":"list","tab":"t2"}` → `wazza --gui chat-queue list --tab t2` |
| edit | `id`: the item's id from list (key:revision); `text`: the new text; `tab`: the tab's id (t1, t2...: ui {action: "vm_tabs_read"} lists a VM's tabs); `vm` (optional): the VM by number: vm-1 (the default) to vm-8 | replace a queued message's text | `{"verb":"edit","id":"q1:2","text":"hello","tab":"t2"}` → `wazza --gui chat-queue edit q1:2 --stdin --tab t2` |
| discard | `id`: the item's id from list; `tab`: the tab's id (t1, t2...: ui {action: "vm_tabs_read"} lists a VM's tabs); `vm` (optional): the VM by number: vm-1 (the default) to vm-8 | drop a queued message | `{"verb":"discard","id":"q1:2","tab":"t2"}` → `wazza --gui chat-queue discard q1:2 --tab t2` |

| cancel | `id`: its id (sch-...) | cancel one | `{"verb":"cancel","id":"sch-01ab"}` → `wazza --gui schedule cancel sch-01ab` |

### `tool_queue`

The Chats' tool call queues (CLI `wazza --gui tool-queue`): list, status, graph, move items, cancel.

| verb | arguments | what it does | example |
|---|---|---|---|
| list | `vm` (optional): the VM by number: vm-1 (the default) to vm-8; `tab` (optional): the tab's id (t1, t2...: ui {action: "vm_tabs_read"} lists a VM's tabs) | every queue | `{"verb":"list"}` → `wazza --gui tool-queue list` |
| status | `queue`: the queue's id (q1, q2...: list names them) | one queue's items | `{"verb":"status","queue":"q1"}` → `wazza --gui tool-queue status q1` |
| graph | `queue`: the queue's id (q1, q2...: list names them) | its items' order and links | `{"verb":"graph","queue":"q1"}` → `wazza --gui tool-queue graph q1` |
| transfer | `queue`: the queue's id (q1, q2...: list names them); `items`: rest, or item ids a,b,c (status lists them); `to` (optional): the queue they move into | move items to another queue | `{"verb":"transfer","queue":"q1","items":"rest","to":"q2"}` → `wazza --gui tool-queue transfer q1 rest --to q2` |
| cancel | `queue`: the queue's id (q1, q2...: list names them); `items` (optional): item ids a,b,c (default the whole queue) | cancel a queue or some of its items | `{"verb":"cancel","queue":"q1"}` → `wazza --gui tool-queue cancel q1` |

### `timeouts`

How long one tool call and one command of a Chat may run before Wazza OS stops it (CLI `wazza --gui timeouts`; Settings › Agent).

| verb | arguments | what it does | example |
|---|---|---|---|
| status | - | both timeouts | `{"verb":"status"}` → `wazza --gui timeouts status` |
| set | `tool` (optional): seconds for one tool call (10-1800); `command` (optional): seconds for one command (10-7200) | change them | `{"verb":"set","tool":120}` → `wazza --gui timeouts set --tool 120` |

| off | `tab` (optional): the tab's id (t1, t2...: ui {action: "vm_tabs_read"} lists a VM's tabs); `vm` (optional): the VM by number: vm-1 (the default) to vm-8 | keep them off | `{"verb":"off"}` → `wazza --gui local-services off` |

### `provider_keys`

API keys of Wazza OS's providers (CLI `wazza --gui provider-keys`): list, add (usable in every Chat at once), remove, rename. Add a key with add_from_env (recommended): the CLI reads it from an environment variable of this MCP server (the agent's own environment, e.g. OPENROUTER_API_KEY set by the user), so the key never passes through your model; add_from_file reads it from the user's file of mode 0600. add takes keys you were given as text (they pass through your model: only when the user gave them to you). Keys travel only on stdin or from those sources, never argv, and are never shown back.

| verb | arguments | what it does | example |
|---|---|---|---|
| list | `credit` (optional): with each key's credit | the providers and their keys (never the key itself) | `{"verb":"list"}` → `wazza --gui provider-keys list` |
| add_from_env | `provider`: the provider's id (list names them: openrouter...); `from_env`: the name of the environment variable that holds the key (this MCP server's environment); `name` (optional): the key's name on the Sign in page (0 to 40 characters) | add one key, read by the CLI from an environment variable (recommended: never through your model) | `{"verb":"add_from_env","provider":"openrouter","from_env":"OPENROUTER_API_KEY"}` → `wazza --gui provider-keys add --provider openrouter --from-env OPENROUTER_API_KEY` |
| add_from_file | `provider`: the provider's id (list names them: openrouter...); `from_file`: the path of the user's file that holds the key: one line, mode 0600, owned by the user; `name` (optional): the key's name on the Sign in page (0 to 40 characters) | add one key, read by the CLI from a 0600 file (never through your model) | `{"verb":"add_from_file","provider":"openrouter","from_file":"keys/openrouter.key"}` → `wazza --gui provider-keys add --provider openrouter --from-file keys/openrouter.key` |
| add | `keys`: {"keys": [{"providerId", "key", "name"?}]} | add keys given as text (they pass through your model: prefer add_from_env) | `{"verb":"add","keys":{"keys":[{"providerId":"openrouter","key":"(the key)"}]}}` → `wazza --gui provider-keys add --stdin` |
| remove | `providers`: the providers whose keys go | remove every key of these providers (removes or ends something) | `{"verb":"remove","providers":["openrouter"]}` → `wazza --gui provider-keys remove openrouter` |
| remove_key | `provider`: the provider; `key_id`: the key's id from list | remove one key (removes or ends something) | `{"verb":"remove_key","provider":"openrouter","key_id":"k1"}` → `wazza --gui provider-keys remove-key --provider openrouter --key k1` |
| rename | `provider`: the provider; `key_id`: the key's id from list; `name`: its new name (0 to 40 characters) | name a key | `{"verb":"rename","provider":"openrouter","key_id":"k1","name":"work"}` → `wazza --gui provider-keys rename --provider openrouter --key k1 --name work` |

### `provider_signin`

Sign-ins of Wazza OS's providers and logins (CLI `wazza --gui provider-signin`): status, start an OAuth or key sign-in, poll it, open its page, submit a code (stdin), commit, cancel, sign out; the order of a provider's keys or a login's accounts and when one runs out (rotation). Every op takes the same optional flags (vm, provider, method, attempt, auth, browser, prompt, validation_model, account); start names provider and method, the next steps the attempt and auth ids start answered.

| verb | arguments | what it does | example |
|---|---|---|---|
| status | `vm` (optional): the VM by number: vm-1 (the default) to vm-8; `provider` (optional): the provider's id (openrouter...); `method` (optional): the sign-in method's id (oauth, key...); `attempt` (optional): the attempt id start answered; `auth` (optional): the auth id start answered; `browser` (optional): where a sign-in page opens (external and chrome are on the user's screen); `prompt` (optional): the prompt id a submit answers; `validation_model` (optional): the model a key's check uses; `account` (optional): one account of a login; `refresh` (optional): read them again now | every sign-in's state | `{"verb":"status"}` → `wazza --gui provider-signin status` |
| custom_apis | - | the saved custom APIs | `{"verb":"custom_apis"}` → `wazza --gui provider-signin custom-apis` |
| start | `vm` (optional): the VM by number: vm-1 (the default) to vm-8; `provider` (optional): the provider's id (openrouter...); `method` (optional): the sign-in method's id (oauth, key...); `attempt` (optional): the attempt id start answered; `auth` (optional): the auth id start answered; `browser` (optional): where a sign-in page opens (external and chrome are on the user's screen); `prompt` (optional): the prompt id a submit answers; `validation_model` (optional): the model a key's check uses; `account` (optional): one account of a login | start a sign-in (provider, method): its attempt and auth ids | `{"verb":"start","provider":"openrouter","method":"oauth"}` → `wazza --gui provider-signin start --provider openrouter --method oauth` |
| poll | `vm` (optional): the VM by number: vm-1 (the default) to vm-8; `provider` (optional): the provider's id (openrouter...); `method` (optional): the sign-in method's id (oauth, key...); `attempt` (optional): the attempt id start answered; `auth` (optional): the auth id start answered; `browser` (optional): where a sign-in page opens (external and chrome are on the user's screen); `prompt` (optional): the prompt id a submit answers; `validation_model` (optional): the model a key's check uses; `account` (optional): one account of a login | how a sign-in goes (attempt, auth) | `{"verb":"poll","attempt":"a1","auth":"u1"}` → `wazza --gui provider-signin poll --attempt a1 --auth u1` |
| open | `vm` (optional): the VM by number: vm-1 (the default) to vm-8; `provider` (optional): the provider's id (openrouter...); `method` (optional): the sign-in method's id (oauth, key...); `attempt` (optional): the attempt id start answered; `auth` (optional): the auth id start answered; `browser` (optional): where a sign-in page opens (external and chrome are on the user's screen); `prompt` (optional): the prompt id a submit answers; `validation_model` (optional): the model a key's check uses; `account` (optional): one account of a login; `focus` (optional): show it on the user's screen (changes what the user sees: only when the user asked) | open a sign-in's page (attempt, auth; browser external and chrome are on the user's screen) | `{"verb":"open","attempt":"a1","auth":"u1","browser":"in-app"}` → `wazza --gui provider-signin open --attempt a1 --auth u1 --browser in-app` |
| submit | `vm` (optional): the VM by number: vm-1 (the default) to vm-8; `provider` (optional): the provider's id (openrouter...); `method` (optional): the sign-in method's id (oauth, key...); `attempt` (optional): the attempt id start answered; `auth` (optional): the auth id start answered; `browser` (optional): where a sign-in page opens (external and chrome are on the user's screen); `prompt` (optional): the prompt id a submit answers; `validation_model` (optional): the model a key's check uses; `account` (optional): one account of a login; `secret`: the code or key (one line) | answer a sign-in's prompt (attempt, auth, prompt) with a code or key | `{"verb":"submit","attempt":"a1","auth":"u1","prompt":"p1","secret":"(the code)"}` → `wazza --gui provider-signin submit --attempt a1 --auth u1 --prompt p1 --secret-stdin` |
| commit | `vm` (optional): the VM by number: vm-1 (the default) to vm-8; `provider` (optional): the provider's id (openrouter...); `method` (optional): the sign-in method's id (oauth, key...); `attempt` (optional): the attempt id start answered; `auth` (optional): the auth id start answered; `browser` (optional): where a sign-in page opens (external and chrome are on the user's screen); `prompt` (optional): the prompt id a submit answers; `validation_model` (optional): the model a key's check uses; `account` (optional): one account of a login | keep a finished sign-in (attempt, auth) | `{"verb":"commit","attempt":"a1","auth":"u1"}` → `wazza --gui provider-signin commit --attempt a1 --auth u1` |
| cancel | `vm` (optional): the VM by number: vm-1 (the default) to vm-8; `provider` (optional): the provider's id (openrouter...); `method` (optional): the sign-in method's id (oauth, key...); `attempt` (optional): the attempt id start answered; `auth` (optional): the auth id start answered; `browser` (optional): where a sign-in page opens (external and chrome are on the user's screen); `prompt` (optional): the prompt id a submit answers; `validation_model` (optional): the model a key's check uses; `account` (optional): one account of a login | cancel a sign-in (attempt, auth) | `{"verb":"cancel","attempt":"a1","auth":"u1"}` → `wazza --gui provider-signin cancel --attempt a1 --auth u1` |
| sign_out | `vm` (optional): the VM by number: vm-1 (the default) to vm-8; `provider` (optional): the provider's id (openrouter...); `method` (optional): the sign-in method's id (oauth, key...); `attempt` (optional): the attempt id start answered; `auth` (optional): the auth id start answered; `browser` (optional): where a sign-in page opens (external and chrome are on the user's screen); `prompt` (optional): the prompt id a submit answers; `validation_model` (optional): the model a key's check uses; `account` (optional): one account of a login | sign a provider out (provider; method or account for one of them) (removes or ends something) | `{"verb":"sign_out","provider":"openrouter"}` → `wazza --gui provider-signin sign-out --provider openrouter` |
| order | `provider`: a provider, or the login claude or chatgpt; `ids`: its keys' or accounts' ids, comma separated, first first | the order its keys or accounts are used in | `{"verb":"order","provider":"openrouter","ids":"k2,k1"}` → `wazza --gui provider-signin order --provider openrouter --ids k2,k1` |
| rotation | `provider`: a provider, or the login claude or chatgpt; `mode`: which key or account is used next | when one runs out, which is next | `{"verb":"rotation","provider":"openrouter","mode":"take_turns"}` → `wazza --gui provider-signin rotation --provider openrouter --mode take_turns` |

### `wazza_account`

The user's Wazza account in Wazza OS (CLI `wazza --gui wazza-account`): its state, sign in and out, the website connection, and the website's MCP. Passwords and URLs travel only on stdin.

| verb | arguments | what it does | example |
|---|---|---|---|
| status | - | signed in or not, the account | `{"verb":"status"}` → `wazza --gui wazza-account status` |
| start | - | start a browser sign-in | `{"verb":"start"}` → `wazza --gui wazza-account start` |
| logout | - | sign out (removes or ends something) | `{"verb":"logout"}` → `wazza --gui wazza-account logout` |
| login | `email`: the account's email; `password`: the password | sign in with email and password | `{"verb":"login","email":"me@example.com","password":"(the password)"}` → `wazza --gui wazza-account login --email me@example.com --password-stdin` |
| complete | `url`: the sign-in's return URL | finish a browser sign-in | `{"verb":"complete","url":"(the URL)"}` → `wazza --gui wazza-account complete --url-stdin` |
| connect_start | - | start the website connection | `{"verb":"connect_start"}` → `wazza --gui wazza-account connect-start` |
| connect_status | - | the connection's state | `{"verb":"connect_status"}` → `wazza --gui wazza-account connect-status` |
| connect_logout | - | end the connection (removes or ends something) | `{"verb":"connect_logout"}` → `wazza --gui wazza-account connect-logout` |
| connect_complete | `url`: the connection's return URL | finish the connection | `{"verb":"connect_complete","url":"(the URL)"}` → `wazza --gui wazza-account connect-complete --url-stdin` |
| mcp | `method`: the website MCP's method (tools/list, tools/call...); `params` (optional): its params | call the Wazza website's MCP | `{"verb":"mcp","method":"tools/list"}` → `wazza --gui wazza-account mcp tools/list` |

### `wazza_tools`

The user's Wazza AI tools (images, video, audio, voice, text) from the Wazza website (CLI `wazza --gui wazza-tools`): catalog, describe, estimate, run, read, runs, cancel, balance. RUN SPENDS WAZZA PRO CREDITS: estimate first and run only what the user asked for. The op's fields (query, model, workflow, inputs, waitSeconds...) go in fields; read and cancel name the run's call id.

| verb | arguments | what it does | example |
|---|---|---|---|
| catalog | `fields` (optional): the op's fields as one object (query, model, workflow, inputs, waitSeconds...); `call` (optional): a run's call id (32 hex), for read and cancel | the tools and models (fields: {query?}) | `{"verb":"catalog","fields":{"query":"image"}}` → `wazza --gui wazza-tools catalog --args-stdin` |
| describe | `fields` (optional): the op's fields as one object (query, model, workflow, inputs, waitSeconds...); `call` (optional): a run's call id (32 hex), for read and cancel | one model's inputs (fields: {model}) | `{"verb":"describe","fields":{"model":"m1"}}` → `wazza --gui wazza-tools describe --args-stdin` |
| estimate | `fields` (optional): the op's fields as one object (query, model, workflow, inputs, waitSeconds...); `call` (optional): a run's call id (32 hex), for read and cancel | what a run would cost (fields: {model, inputs}) | `{"verb":"estimate","fields":{"model":"m1","inputs":{}}}` → `wazza --gui wazza-tools estimate --args-stdin` |
| run | `fields` (optional): the op's fields as one object (query, model, workflow, inputs, waitSeconds...); `call` (optional): a run's call id (32 hex), for read and cancel | run a tool: SPENDS WAZZA PRO CREDITS (fields: {model or workflow, inputs, waitSeconds?}) | `{"verb":"run","fields":{"model":"m1","inputs":{"prompt":"a cat"}}}` → `wazza --gui wazza-tools run --args-stdin` |
| read | `fields` (optional): the op's fields as one object (query, model, workflow, inputs, waitSeconds...); `call` (optional): a run's call id (32 hex), for read and cancel | a run's state and files (call) | `{"verb":"read","call":"0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef"}` → `wazza --gui wazza-tools read --call 0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef` |
| runs | `fields` (optional): the op's fields as one object (query, model, workflow, inputs, waitSeconds...); `call` (optional): a run's call id (32 hex), for read and cancel | recent runs | `{"verb":"runs"}` → `wazza --gui wazza-tools runs` |
| cancel | `fields` (optional): the op's fields as one object (query, model, workflow, inputs, waitSeconds...); `call` (optional): a run's call id (32 hex), for read and cancel | cancel a run (call) | `{"verb":"cancel","call":"0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef"}` → `wazza --gui wazza-tools cancel --call 0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef` |
| balance | `fields` (optional): the op's fields as one object (query, model, workflow, inputs, waitSeconds...); `call` (optional): a run's call id (32 hex), for read and cancel | the credits left | `{"verb":"balance"}` → `wazza --gui wazza-tools balance` |

### `pro`

A Wazza Pro tab's own app tools through that tab's Chat (CLI `wazza --gui pro`). A run that costs SPENDS WAZZA PRO CREDITS and needs confirm_spend: true: use it only when the user asked for that run.

| verb | arguments | what it does | example |
|---|---|---|---|
| run | `tool`: the Pro tool's name (verb list); `tab`: the tab's id (t1, t2...: ui {action: "vm_tabs_read"} lists a VM's tabs); `vm` (optional): the VM by number: vm-1 (the default) to vm-8; `harness` (optional): the host harness of the Pro tab's Chat that runs it (claude-code, codex...); default its own; `confirm_spend` (optional): true: the user agreed to spend credits on this run; `arguments` (optional): the tool's arguments | run one Pro tool | `{"verb":"run","tool":"generate_image","tab":"t3","arguments":{"prompt":"a cat"}}` → `wazza --gui pro generate_image --tab t3 --args-stdin` |
| observe | `request_id`: the run's request id (a pending answer named it); `tab`: the tab's id (t1, t2...: ui {action: "vm_tabs_read"} lists a VM's tabs); `vm` (optional): the VM by number: vm-1 (the default) to vm-8; `harness` (optional): the host harness of the Pro tab's Chat that runs it (claude-code, codex...); default its own | a pending run's state | `{"verb":"observe","request_id":"r1","tab":"t3"}` → `wazza --gui pro --observe r1 --tab t3` |
| list | `tab`: the tab's id (t1, t2...: ui {action: "vm_tabs_read"} lists a VM's tabs); `vm` (optional): the VM by number: vm-1 (the default) to vm-8; `harness` (optional): the host harness of the Pro tab's Chat that runs it (claude-code, codex...); default its own | the Pro tab's tools | `{"verb":"list","tab":"t3"}` → `wazza --gui pro --list --tab t3` |

### `pro_input`

### `invoke`

Any control-plane command of the running Wazza OS app (CLI `wazza --gui invoke`): its modules, their methods and jobs. modules_call reaches every module method (sandbox, packages, agent, ui, drive, updater...): modules_list and modules_status say what each offers. The other tools cover the usual work; use this one for what they do not.

| verb | arguments | what it does | example |

| modules_call | `module`: the module's id; `method`: the method; `args` (optional): the method's arguments | call one module method | `{"verb":"modules_call","module":"sandbox","method":"status","args":{}}` → `wazza --gui invoke modules_call sandbox status -` |
| jobs_list | - | the jobs | `{"verb":"jobs_list"}` → `wazza --gui invoke jobs_list` |

| jobs_cancel | `job_id`: the job's id | cancel a job | `{"verb":"jobs_cancel","job_id":"job-1"}` → `wazza --gui invoke jobs_cancel job-1` |
| jobs_output | `job_id`: the job's id; `since` (optional): the output offset to read from | a job's output | `{"verb":"jobs_output","job_id":"job-1","since":0}` → `wazza --gui invoke jobs_output job-1 0` |
| events_poll | `since` (optional): the event number to read from | the app's events | `{"verb":"events_poll","since":0}` → `wazza --gui invoke events_poll 0` |
| session_get | - | the session | `{"verb":"session_get"}` → `wazza --gui invoke session_get` |
| claims | - | the claims | `{"verb":"claims"}` → `wazza --gui invoke claims` |
| claims_report | - | the claims report | `{"verb":"claims_report"}` → `wazza --gui invoke claims_report` |
| gnome | `words`: help \| stream-status \| frame \| app-launch ID \| app-focus ID \| terminal-open \| terminal-focus \| hermes \| pointer X Y \| click X Y [B] \| key KEY | a GNOME desktop action in the VM shown | `{"verb":"gnome","words":["stream-status"]}` → `wazza --gui invoke gnome stream-status` |

### `native_input`

Pointer and keyboard input into the Wazza OS app's own window (CLI `wazza --gui native-input`), on a desktop or its virtual screen: begin a lease, then focus, pointer, click, scroll, key, text, end. X,Y are the screenshot's pixels; never the user's pointer or another window.

| click | `id`: the lease id begin answered (64 hex); `x`: x; `y`: y; `button` (optional): 1, 2 or 3 (default 1) | click | `{"verb":"click","id":"0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef","x":10,"y":20}` → `wazza --gui native-input click 0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef 10 20` |
| scroll | `id`: the lease id begin answered (64 hex); `x`: x; `y`: y; `direction`: the wheel's direction; `steps` (optional): 1 to 20 wheel notches (default 1) | scroll | `{"verb":"scroll","id":"0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef","x":10,"y":20,"direction":"down"}` → `wazza --gui native-input scroll 0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef 10 20 down` |
| key | `id`: the lease id begin answered (64 hex); `key`: a printable key, Tab, Return, Escape, BackSpace, arrows, Ctrl+a, Ctrl+l... | press a key | `{"verb":"key","id":"0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef","key":"Return"}` → `wazza --gui native-input key 0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef Return` |
| text | `id`: the lease id begin answered (64 hex); `text`: 1 to 512 printable ASCII characters | type text | `{"verb":"text","id":"0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef","text":"hello"}` → `wazza --gui native-input text 0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef --stdin` |
| end | `id`: the lease id begin answered (64 hex) | end the lease | `{"verb":"end","id":"0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef"}` → `wazza --gui native-input end 0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef` |
