---

Page: The command line (Connect and automate)
Address: https://os-guide.wazza.ai/cli.html

# The command line

Everything you click in Wazza OS, a terminal can do too. `wazza --gui …` commands talk to the Wazza OS that is running for you, in the background, and answer in JSON: for scripts, for a server with no screen, and for agents outside Wazza OS.

- **What**: `wazza --gui` commands for the running Wazza OS, and `wazza --check`

- **Why**: Repeatable setups, scripts, servers, other agents

- **Who**: Developers, admins, power users

- **Where**: Any terminal of the same user as the running Wazza OS

## Before you start

- `wazza`, `wazzaos` and `wazza-os` are the same program; this manual writes `wazza`.
- Wazza OS must be running for the same user: `wazza --gui status` says so. The commands never open a second window, and only change what you see when you ask (the `--focus` options).
- Answers are JSON on standard output. Exit codes: **0** done; **1** refused, failed, or Wazza OS not reachable; **2** the command was wrong and nothing was sent (the usage is printed).
- Passwords, keys and tokens are read only from standard input (`--stdin`, `--password-stdin`, `--key-stdin`), never as a word of the command: they stay out of your shell history and the process list.
- `wazza --version` prints the program's version and the installed package's (version, build and date).
- For agents that take MCP servers rather than a shell, `wazza-os mcp` offers these same commands as MCP tools ([Connect an agent from outside](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/mcp.html#connect-an-agent-from-outside); every tool: [Every Wazza OS MCP tool](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/mcp-tools.html)).

```
$ wazza --gui status
$ wazza --version
```

## Check this computer

`wazza --check` runs the same checks as the first start, without starting Wazza OS and without a screen: KVM, the systemd user session, the X11 display, the Chat sandbox, the graphics driver and the VM display buffers. Each line says what was found, what it means, and the commands that fix it.

```
$ wazza --check
$ wazza --check --json
```

Exit 0: nothing missing; 1: something is missing (VMs or the window would not start). A *limited* item (for example software graphics) does not fail the check. What each item means: [First start › What is checked](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/first-start.html#what-is-checked).

## Set up without clicks

A setup file does the first start's steps: your Wazza OS account, plan logins, API keys, apps, and appearance. Write it once and run it on every computer:

```
{
  "account": {"email": "me@example.com", "passwordFile": "~/secrets/wazza-password"},
  "logins": ["claude", "chatgpt"],
  "keys": [{"provider": "openrouter", "name": "work", "keyFile": "~/secrets/openrouter.key"}],
  "whenOneRunsOut": {"openrouter": "take turns"},
  "apps": ["gimp", "blender"],
  "vm": {"memory": "auto", "cpus": "auto"},
  "appearance": {"theme": "dark", "glass": "reduced", "reduceMotion": false},
  "tabs": {"limit": 0}
}
```

```
$ wazza --gui setup run --file ~/wazza-setup.json
$ wazza --gui setup status
$ wazza --gui setup reset-first-run
```

| Field | What it takes |
|---|---|
| `account` | `email`, and `passwordFile` (a file holding the password) or `passwordStdin: true`; never the password itself |
| `logins` | Plan logins: `claude`, `chatgpt`, `grok`, `google`, `openrouter`, `nous` |
| `keys` | API keys: `provider`, an optional `name`, `keyFile`; never the key itself |
| `whenOneRunsOut` | Per provider: `in order`, `take turns`, `least used`, `random` |
| `apps` | App ids to install (`wazza --gui app list` shows them) |
| `vm` | Only `"auto"` (numbers are set in Settings or with the commands below) |
| `appearance` | `theme` dark, light or system; `glass` on, reduced or off; `reduceMotion` |
| `tabs.limit` | Tabs before they fold: 0 = Auto, up to 99 |

It runs only the steps not done yet, so running it twice changes nothing. Each step prints one line as it ends: `✓` done, `→` waiting for you (a login prints its link and reads the code you paste in the terminal), `✗` failed. Exit 0: all done; 1: a step needs you or failed; 2: the file is malformed (nothing ran). `--file -` reads the file from standard input; `--json` prints one JSON line per step.

## VMs

```
$ wazza --gui vm list
$ wazza --gui vm create
$ wazza --gui vm start vm-2
$ wazza --gui vm stop vm-2
$ wazza --gui vm backup vm-2
$ wazza --gui vm backups
$ wazza --gui vm restore BACKUP_ID
```

| Command | Does |
|---|---|
| `vm list` | Every VM by number, running or stopped, with its disk |
| `vm create` | A new stopped VM with the lowest free number |
| `vm start VM`, `vm stop VM` | Start or stop one |
| `vm backup VM`, `vm backups` | A zip of the VM in your Downloads (in the background); the list of backups |
| `vm restore BACKUP_ID` or `PATH.zip` | A new VM from a backup; with `--into VM --yes`, replaces a stopped VM's disk for good |
| `vm reset VM --yes` | Makes a stopped VM (not vm-1) new at its next start: its disk is removed |
| `vm delete VM --yes` | Removes a stopped VM (not vm-1) and its disk, for good |

## Memory, disk and graphics

```
$ wazza --gui vm-resources
$ wazza --gui vm-memory status
$ wazza --gui vm-memory auto 50
$ wazza --gui vm-disk set 64
$ wazza --gui gpu status
```

| Command | Does |
|---|---|
| `vm-resources [--vm VM]` | What the VM has now and the most it may get, its graphics and disk, and your computer's processors, load, memory, graphics cards and free disk |
| `vm-memory status [--vm VM]` | The memory rule and each VM's memory and limit |
| `vm-memory auto PERCENT [--min MIB]` | Auto: PERCENT (10 to 100) of the memory free now, for every VM |
| `vm-memory set MIB [--vm VM]` | A fixed amount, in MiB, added to the running VM at once |
| `vm-disk status`, `vm-disk set GIB [--vm VM]` | The disk's size; grow it (only grows: a running VM grows at once) |
| `vm-gpu status`, `vm-gpu auto PERCENT`, `vm-gpu set MIB` | The graphics memory a VM may hold |
| `gpu status`, `gpu mode virtualized\|native\|none`, `gpu card …` | The GPU setting ([Desktop apps and the GPU](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/gpu-apps.html)) |

The same settings, explained: [Settings › VM resources](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/settings-resources.html).

## Keys and sign-ins

```
$ wazza --gui wazza-account login --email me@example.com --password-stdin < ~/secrets/wazza-password
$ wazza --gui provider-keys add --stdin < ~/secrets/keys.json
$ wazza --gui provider-keys list --credit
$ wazza --gui provider-signin status
```

`keys.json` holds `{"keys": [{"providerId": "openrouter", "key": "…"}]}`; keep it readable only by you, or pipe it from your password manager. Also: `provider-keys remove PROVIDER`, `wazza-account status` and `logout`, `copilot key-from-gh` (GitHub Copilot from your `gh` sign-in). Plan logins that open a browser are easiest with the setup file above. Details: [Sign in › From the command line](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/signin.html#from-the-command-line).

## Chats

```
$ wazza --gui chat-model set openrouter/xiaomi/mimo-v2.6-flash
$ wazza --gui chat-transcript --tab t5 --last 4
$ wazza --gui chat-transcript --tab t5 --kinds tool,bash > t5-tools.json
$ wazza --gui timeouts set --command 1800
```

| Command | Does |
|---|---|
| `chat-model status`, `chat-model set MODEL` | The model new Chats start on (a Chat keeps its own) |
| `chat-transcript --tab TAB [--vm VM]` | A tab's whole conversation as one JSON document, oldest first: `--kinds user,message,thinking,tool,bash,error`, `--roles user,assistant`, `--contains TEXT`, `--from N`, `--last N` |
| `chat-queue list\|edit\|discard … --tab TAB` | The messages waiting while a Chat answers |
| `schedule list`, `schedule cancel ID` | Messages the Chats scheduled for later |
| `timeouts`, `timeouts set [--tool S] [--command S]` | The time limits: a tool call 10 to 1800 s (default 60), a command 10 to 7200 s (default 600) |
| `local-services status\|on\|off` | Whether Chats on your computer may reach its local services |

Tab ids (`t5`) come from the window's `tabs_read` action (below). To send a message to a Chat: the window action `chat_send`.

## Apps

```
$ wazza --gui app list
$ wazza --gui invoke modules_call packages install_request '{"appId":"gimp","vmId":"vm-1"}'
$ wazza --gui app status gimp --vm vm-1 --refresh
$ wazza --gui app uninstall gimp --vm vm-1 --focus
```

| Command | Does |
|---|---|
| `app list`, `app get APP_ID` | Every app, and one app's recipe |
| `install_request` (above) | Installs an app, in the background (a failed install is tried once more) |
| `app status APP_ID [--vm VM] [--refresh]` | Installed or not; `--refresh` checks the VM itself |
| `app uninstall APP_ID [--vm VM] [--focus] [--follow]` | Shows the uninstall's confirmation in Wazza OS (only your click there uninstalls); `--follow` waits for the result |
| `app observe JOB_ID --follow` | An install's or uninstall's live output |
| `app template`, `validate`, `save`, `remove` | Your own apps ([Add your own apps](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/custom-apps.html#from-the-command-line)) |

## Files

```
$ wazza --gui explorer list Documents --vm vm-1
$ wazza --gui explorer copy-to-vm ~/report.pdf --vm vm-1 --folder Documents
$ wazza --gui explorer upload Pictures/circle.png --vm vm-1
$ wazza --gui clipboard files --to-computer allow
```

| Command | Does |
|---|---|
| `explorer list [PATH] [--vm VM]` | A folder of the VM's home (works for a VM in the background) |
| `explorer rename`, `move`, `delete PATH --yes`, `permissions` | As in the Explorer; never overwrites; delete is permanent |
| `explorer copy-to-vm PATH… [--vm VM] [--folder F]` | Your files into the VM (default `~/Downloads`), by your copy rule |
| `explorer upload VM_PATH… [--vm VM]` | The VM's files to your computer, as new files (default `Downloads/From the VM`), by your copy rule |
| `explorer list\|details\|open\|search\|read … --computer` | Your own files, below your home |
| `clipboard copy --stdin [--guest-only]` | Puts text on the VM's clipboard (and yours) |
| `clipboard files [--to-vm R] [--to-computer R]` | The file-copy rules: `ask`, `allow`, `off` |

## The window, and everything else

Every action of the window has a name, and `ui do` runs it with its arguments; `ui catalog` lists them all (about 200: open an app, read the tabs, send to a Chat, read what you see, start a VM, read the settings…).

```
$ wazza --gui invoke modules_call ui catalog '{}'
$ wazza --gui invoke modules_call ui do '{"action":"tabs_read","args":{}}'
$ wazza --gui invoke modules_call ui do '{"action":"open_app","args":{"appId":"inkscape"}}'
$ wazza --gui invoke modules_call drive look '{"vmId":"vm-1","tabId":"t3"}' --image-out ./t3
```

Arguments larger than a command line holds: `-` reads them from standard input, `@file.json` from a file. Also: `data status` (Wazza OS's folders on your computer and their sizes), `data remove-all --confirm "REMOVE ALL DATA"` ([Remove all data](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/settings-computer.html#remove-all-data)), `quit`. On a server, `screenshot` and `record` capture Wazza OS's own screen ([Wazza OS on a server](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/cli-server.html)).

## When an agent runs these commands

A command run by the agent of a Chat (from its shell) is that Chat's: it may not change your view (focus, quit), reach another tab's Chat, copy files for another VM, or do what only you can do (Let this Chat edit my files, loosening the file-copy rules, Local services on). An agent outside Wazza OS that you started yourself runs the commands as you, in its shell or through `wazza-os mcp` ([Connect an agent from outside](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/mcp.html#connect-an-agent-from-outside)).


---

Page: On a server (virtual screen) (Connect and automate)
Address: https://os-guide.wazza.ai/cli-server.html

# Wazza OS on a server

Wazza OS is a desktop app, but it does not need a screen: on a server, a cloud machine or over SSH it brings its own *virtual screen*, and you drive it with [the command line](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/cli.html). Its VM, apps and Chats work exactly as on a desktop.

- **What**: Wazza OS with its own invisible screen, driven from a terminal

- **Why**: Agents and apps on a powerful machine, in CI, or for a whole team

- **Who**: Admins, developers, automation

- **Where**: `wazza --virtual-screen=…` and `wazza --gui …`

## What the server needs

| Need | Why | How |
|---|---|---|
| Hardware virtualization (KVM): `/dev/kvm` readable and writable | The VM runs on it | Bare metal, or a cloud machine with nested virtualization; your user in the `kvm` group |
| A systemd user session | Each VM runs in a memory-capped scope of it | Log in over SSH (a session that starts it), or keep it running without a login: `loginctl enable-linger "$USER"` |
| The virtual-screen tools: Xvfb, xauth, openbox, dbus, ffmpeg, Python 3 | The virtual screen, its window manager, recordings | Every package installs them (the tarball's installer checks them) |
| A graphics card (optional) | 3D apps draw on it | Without one, the VM uses software graphics |

`wazza --check` tells what is missing, with the commands that fix it ([Check this computer](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/cli.html#check)). Install Wazza OS as on a desktop ([Install](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/install.html)).

## Start, set up, use, stop

Check the machine:

```
$ wazza --check
```

Start Wazza OS in the background, with its own screen:

```
$ nohup wazza --virtual-screen=always >/dev/null 2>&1 &
```

Wait until it answers:

```
$ until wazza --gui status >/dev/null 2>&1; do sleep 2; done
```

Set it up without clicks: account, logins, keys, apps ([the setup file](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/cli.html#set-up-without-clicks)):

```
$ wazza --gui setup run --file ~/wazza-setup.json
```

Use it: every command of [the command line](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/cli.html), and pictures of its screen:

```
$ wazza --gui vm list
$ wazza --gui screenshot ~/wazza.png
```

Stop it:

```
$ wazza --gui quit
```

A login that opens a browser (a plan login such as Claude or ChatGPT) prints its link in the terminal instead: open it on any computer, sign in, and paste the code it gives back into the terminal. API keys need no browser.

## The virtual screen

`--virtual-screen=auto|always|never` (default `auto`) decides where the window goes:

| Value | Wazza OS… |
|---|---|
| `auto` (default) | uses your display when there is one, and starts its own screen when there is none |
| `always` | always starts its own screen, even on a desktop (it then runs out of sight) |
| `never` | never starts one: without a display, the start fails |

Its own screen is private to your user (1280 × 800, with a simple window manager) and stops when Wazza OS stops. It is the only screen Wazza OS captures: `--gui screenshot FILE.png`, `--gui record start FILE.mp4` and `--gui record stop ID` work with it, and refuse on a normal desktop (Wazza OS never captures your own desktop). To see what a tab of the VM shows, on any screen, use Drive:

```
$ wazza --gui invoke modules_call drive look '{"vmId":"vm-1","tabId":"t3"}' --image-out ./t3
```

`--gui host-app launch chromium` (or `vlc`, `xmessage`) opens that app of the server on Wazza OS's own screen, and only there; `host-app list` and `host-app stop ID` follow and close it.

## Over SSH, and for other agents

- The commands work over SSH, as the user who started Wazza OS. The SSH session must have that user's runtime folder (`XDG_RUNTIME_DIR`), as a normal login does.
- An agent on another machine can use the same commands through SSH; an agent on the server itself runs them in its shell ([Connect an agent from outside](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/mcp.html#connect-an-agent-from-outside)).
- One Wazza OS runs per user: a second start for the same user goes to the one already running.

## On your own computer

Start Wazza OS from your desktop as usual, then use `wazza --gui …` from any terminal of your user: the commands work in the background and change what you see only when you ask (`--focus`). A tab a command opens appears in the background, with a badge.


---

Page: General (Settings)
Address: https://os-guide.wazza.ai/settings-general.html

# Settings › General

How Wazza OS looks (theme, glass, motion), where each tab's Chat sits, how many tabs show before they fold, the frame rate of app tabs, and which version runs.

## Open Settings and find an option

1. Click **Settings** in the Home menu on the left (open Home with the **+** at the end of the tab strip if it is not shown). Settings opens in the Home tab.
2. Pick a page in the list on the left: General, Virtual machines, VM resources, Chats & agents, Skills & learning, Files & sharing, Sync & team, This computer. In a narrow window the list becomes a drop-down next to the title.
3. Each page has tabs (here Appearance, Tabs & layout, Display, About); one tab shows at a time.
4. Or type in **Search settings** (top right): every row of every page that matches your words shows, whatever its page and tab.

### Apply and Discard

On most tabs a change is **held**, not applied: the control shows your new value, its row is marked *Not applied*, and the bar at the bottom of the tab counts the changes. **Apply** applies every held change of the tab together and says what it applied; **Discard** puts them back. If you leave a tab or a page with held changes, Wazza OS asks **Apply**, **Discard** or **Stay** first. With nothing held, the bar says *No changes to apply*.

A few sections have their own button instead (VM resources' **Save and apply**, New Chats' **Use for new Chats**, Time limits' **Save**, the VM list), and text fields have their own button next to them. A change made by an agent or by the command line is never held: it applies at once.

## Appearance

![Settings, General page, Appearance tab: Theme Dark Light Match system, Glass On Reduced Off, Reduce motion switch, and the bar No changes to apply with Discard and Apply](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/img/settings-general-1.webp)

Settings › General › Appearance, with the defaults.

| Option | Values | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| Theme | **Dark** (default), Light, Match system | Dark is Wazza OS's dark petrol. Light uses the Solarized palette (cream background, dark blue text). Match system follows your desktop's light or dark preference and changes with it. The whole window switches in one step. |
| Glass | **On** (default), Reduced, Off | On: a glass lens follows what you hover (menu items, tabs, app cards) and a button squishes slightly when you press it. Reduced: the lens without its blur, and the selected item drawn flat (lighter on a slow graphics card). Off: plain darker highlights, no lens. |
| Reduce motion | Off (default) / On | On: no squish, no springs, no moving highlights anywhere in Wazza OS. Use it if motion bothers you or on a slow computer. When your desktop itself asks for reduced motion, Wazza OS follows it too. |

## Tabs & layout

![Tabs and layout tab: Chat side Left of the app or Right of the app; Tabs shown before they fold, Auto with minus and plus buttons](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/img/settings-general-2.webp)

Settings › General › Tabs & layout.

| Option | Values | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| Chat side | **Left of the app** (default), Right of the app | Where each tab's Chat sits next to its app, in every VM. The divider between them can still be dragged in each tab. |
| Tabs shown before they fold | **Auto** (default), or a number from 1 to 99 | Auto: tabs shrink to their icons when the strip is full, then group once even the icons no longer fit; the others are in the count square's menu. A number (for example 6): when you open one tab more, all tabs fold into one square that shows how many there are; click it to see and pick any tab. Use **−** and **+** or type the number. |

## Display

![Display tab: Max frame rate set to 240, and the line 240 frames a second in every app tab](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/img/settings-general-3.webp)

Settings › General › Display on a new installation.

| Option | Values | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| Max frame rate | Auto, 60, 75, 90, 120, 144, 165, **240** (a new installation's value) | The most frames a second every app tab is drawn at (the VM's picture in the Wazza OS window). Auto follows the refresh rate of the screen the Wazza OS window is on (and is read again when you move the window to another screen). A choice applies at once to every app tab and is kept for the next start. The line under it says the rate in effect. A lower rate uses less CPU and GPU on your computer; it does not change how fast apps run in the VM. |

When an app tab's desktop cannot start, a recovery card for that tab appears in this section (*Guest desktop startup failed*, with **Retry desktop startup**). It is only there while the problem lasts; see [Troubleshooting](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/troubleshooting.html#an-app-tab-stays-black-or-frozen).

## About

![About tab: three tiles, Running 0.2.0+git.z1793589620.e97d03637c1d, Installed the same version, Checked just now with a Check again button](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/img/settings-general-4.webp)

Settings › General › About (here on alpha 2: your computer shows its own version).

| Tile | What it shows |
|---|---|
| Running | The version of Wazza OS that runs now, its build (the 12-character code) and its date. |
| Installed | The version installed on your computer. It differs from Running after an update was installed but Wazza OS was not restarted yet: quit and start Wazza OS to run the new one. |
| Checked | When Wazza OS last read both. **Check again** reads them now. |

The same two versions in a terminal: `wazza --version` (see [The command line](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/cli.html#check)). To look for a newer version, use [the Update page](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/update.html).


---

Page: Virtual machines (Settings)
Address: https://os-guide.wazza.ai/settings-vms.html

# Settings › Virtual machines

Your VMs: which one this window shows, start, stop and restart, add another VM, back one up to a zip and bring it back, remove or reset one.

> Most people only ever use **vm-1**, the VM the first start makes. More VMs are for keeping work apart (a client's project, a test setup), each with its own apps, files and Chats. You can have up to 8 VMs, and 4 can run at the same time.

## VMs

![VMs tab: This window shows vm-1 ready with Start, Stop and Restart; the row vm-1 (primary) shown, running, disk 2.1 GB, RAM up to 5.8 GB (Auto 75%), 9 vCPUs (Auto 75%) with Back up; New VM; 1 VM (0 stopped); at most 8, 4 running at once](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/img/settings-vms-1.webp)

Settings › Virtual machines › VMs, with one VM.

### This window shows

The drop-down names the VM whose tabs, desktop and Chats this Wazza OS window shows, with its state (*vm-1 · ready*). Pick another running VM to switch the window to it. Next to it:

| Button | What it does |
|---|---|
| Start | Starts the VM shown (when it is stopped). A cold start takes about a minute. |
| Stop | Shuts the VM down: its apps end (unsaved work in them is lost), its disk and files are kept. |
| Restart | Stops and starts the VM. Use it when the VM's desktop or apps stop answering, or so that a setting that "applies at the next start" (disk, graphics, screen size) takes effect now. |

### The VM list

Each VM of this computer has a row: its number (`vm-1` to `vm-8`), *(primary)* for vm-1, *shown* for the one this window shows, a green dot while it runs, and a line with its state, its disk size, its memory limit and its processors (with the Auto profile they come from: see [VM resources](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/settings-resources.html)). The list refreshes by itself.

| Row button | When it shows | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| Start | A stopped VM other than vm-1 | Starts it with its own disk. A first start makes its disk and takes a few minutes; the row follows it and says why if it fails. One VM starts at a time: while another one is starting, the row offers **Start when vm-N is ready** (with **Cancel**). The other VMs run beside vm-1: when vm-1 is stopped, the row offers **Start vm-1, then vm-N**. |
| Stop | A running or starting VM other than vm-1 | Shuts it down; its apps end, its disk is kept. (vm-1 stops with **Stop** next to **This window shows**.) |
| Back up | A VM that has a disk, running or stopped (vm-1 too) | Copies its disk, compressed, into a zip saved as a new file in your Downloads folder, in the background. A running VM keeps running (a live copy). The row follows the job (phase and percent). |
| Remove… | A stopped VM, vm-2 to vm-8 | Removes the VM and its disk for good. A second click on **Remove for good** confirms; anything else cancels. |
| Reset… | A stopped VM, vm-2 to vm-8, that has a disk | Deletes its disk and everything in it for good, keeps its number; its next start makes a fresh disk (like a new VM). Confirm with **Reset for good**. |

### Add a VM

1. Click **New VM**. A new VM is added, stopped, with the lowest free number (vm-2 if you have only vm-1). Its disk is made the first time it starts.
2. Click **Start** on its row. The first start takes a few minutes.
3. To work in it, pick it in **This window shows**. Its tabs, desktop and Chats are its own.

At most 4 VMs run at once; with 4 running, stop one before you start another. Every running VM takes memory and processors within the limits of [VM resources](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/settings-resources.html), which are shared out between the running VMs.

## Backups

![Backups tab: A backup is a zip in Downloads. It becomes a new VM, stopped, or replaces a stopped VM's disk. No backups yet: Back up on a stopped VM makes one.](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/img/settings-vms-2.webp)

Settings › Virtual machines › Backups, before the first backup.

A backup is a zip file in your computer's Downloads folder holding one VM's disk, compressed. The tab lists the backups Wazza OS made, each with two buttons:

| Button | What it does |
|---|---|
| Make a VM from it | Makes a new VM, stopped, with that disk (the lowest free number). Your other VMs are not touched. |
| Move into a VM… | Replaces the disk of a stopped VM other than vm-1 with the backup. Everything that was in that VM is lost; confirm with **Replace for good**. |

One backup or restore runs at a time, and while it holds a VM's disk, that VM's row offers nothing. Back up before a risky change; copy the zip elsewhere (a USB disk, another computer) to keep it safe. From a terminal: `wazza --gui vm backup vm-2`, `wazza --gui vm backups`, `wazza --gui vm restore BACKUP_ID` (see [The command line](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/cli.html#vms)).

## Remove or reset a VM

![Remove or reset a VM tab: Remove a VM, Remove on a VM's row above (vm-2 to vm-8); Reset a VM, Reset on a stopped VM's row above, its disk goes, its number stays, vm-1 cannot be reset yet](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/img/settings-vms-3.webp)

This tab explains the two buttons of the VM rows (above): **Remove…** takes a VM away with its disk; **Reset…** keeps the VM but replaces its disk with a fresh one. Both work on vm-2 to vm-8 only, and only when the VM is stopped.

> **vm-1 cannot be removed or reset here**
>
> Its disk holds Wazza OS's own state. To start vm-1 again from nothing, use [Settings › This computer › Remove all data](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/settings-computer.html#remove-data), which erases everything of Wazza OS on this computer (every VM, Chat, sign-in and setting).


---

Page: VM resources (Settings)
Address: https://os-guide.wazza.ai/settings-resources.html

# Settings › VM resources

How much of your computer a VM may use (memory, processors, disk, graphics card) and the size of its screen. Every value here is a limit, not a reservation: a VM starts small, grows up to the limit when its apps need it, and gives back what it does not use.

> The defaults suit almost every computer: memory up to 75 % of what is free (never below 8 GB when your computer has it), processors up to 75 % of your computer's, a disk that grows into half of your free disk space, your graphics card shared with the VM. Change them only for a reason (a laptop that must stay responsive, a large render). [Memory, CPU and disk](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/memory-cpu.html) explains the behaviour behind them.

## How this page saves

This page does not use the Apply bar of the other pages. Its own footer, under every tab:

| Control | What it does |
|---|---|
| Apply to | The VM whose memory and processors are changed while it runs (vm-1, or another running VM). |
| Save and apply | Saves every value of this page. Memory and vCPUs apply at once to the VM chosen in **Apply to**, while it runs; disks, graphics and the screen size apply at the VM's next start. Save never restarts a VM by itself. |
| Restart the VM now | Shows after a save that has something waiting for the next start: restarts the VM so it applies now. Apps running in the VM end; save your work first. |
| Status | What happened last: *Native defaults loaded; no saved Settings file exists yet* on a new installation, then what was saved and applied, or why a value was refused (shown in red). |
| Reset to defaults | Memory, vCPUs and disks back to Auto, graphics and the launch options back to their defaults. Only these settings: your VMs, Chats and keys are not touched. |

## Memory & CPU

![Memory and CPU tab: Memory Auto 75 percent, minimum 5.8 GB, equals 5.8 GB; vCPUs Auto More 75 percent equals 9; then the Apply footer](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/img/settings-resources-1.webp)

Settings › VM resources › Memory & CPU on the test computer (a VM itself with 8 GB of memory and 12 threads, so the minimum shows 5.8 GB there instead of 8 GB).

### Memory

The most memory (RAM) one VM may take. The VM starts with what its desktop needs, takes more when its apps need it (the line under the row says how much it may take now), and gives it back when idle, so a high limit costs your computer nothing until it is used.

| Choice | Fields | What it means |
|---|---|---|
| **Auto** (default) | A percentage: pick 25, 35, 50 or 75 in the list, or type any whole number from 10 to 100. Default **75 %**.; **min**: a minimum in GB, default **8 GB**. | The limit is that percentage of the memory free on your computer now (counting the memory Wazza OS's own VMs already hold), split between the running VMs. It follows your computer: when other programs take memory, the limit goes down. It is never below the minimum when your computer has that much memory in total (minus 2 GB kept for your computer itself). The **= … GB** on the right is the result now. |
| Manual | A fixed value, picked from the list. | The limit is that value whatever is free. Pick it when you want a predictable size. |

> Wazza OS also keeps 10 % of your computer's memory free at all times: when your computer runs short, the VM stops growing and a notice says so (for example *Wazza OS keeps 10% of this computer's memory free; the VM stays at 3 GB*). See [Memory, CPU and disk](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/memory-cpu.html#when-memory-is-short).

### vCPUs

The most processors (threads) one VM may use. A VM boots with 2 and gets more while its programs wait for CPU.

| Choice | Fields | What it means |
|---|---|---|
| **Auto** (default) | Less · 25 %, Half · 50 %, **More · 75 %** (default) | That share of your computer's hardware threads (the row says how many: "75 % of this computer's 12 threads, so 9 now"). |
| Manual | A number, picked from the list | Exactly that many at most. |

## Disks

![Disks tab: System disk Auto Half 50 percent equals 48 GB, grows as it fills, never shrinks; Data disk Unchanged](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/img/settings-resources-2.webp)

Settings › VM resources › Disks.

| Option | Values | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| System disk | **Auto**: Less · 25 %, **Half · 50 %** (default), More · 75 % of the free space on the drive that holds the VMs' disks.; Manual: a size in GB (at least 8). | The size the VM's main disk (its system, apps and files) may grow to. It takes space on your drive only as it fills, and never shrinks: deleting files in the VM does not give the space back to your computer. A larger value applies at the VM's next start; a smaller one never cuts an existing disk. |
| Data disk | **Unchanged** (default: no data disk), or a size to add or grow to (up to 1024 GB) | An extra disk for the VM, added or grown while the VM runs (for large projects, media libraries, datasets). |

To see how much space a VM's disk takes now: the VM's row in [Virtual machines](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/settings-vms.html#the-vm-list) (*disk 2.1 GB*), or [This computer › Usage](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/settings-computer.html#usage).

## Graphics

![Graphics tab: GPU memory, GPU use, GPU Virtualized GPU, Card Auto, Lend-ready mode with Turn on, In the VM lines for Vulkan, OpenGL and OpenCL, then the Apply footer](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/img/settings-resources-3.webp)

Settings › VM resources › Graphics on the test computer. On your computer the rows name your own graphics card.

| Option | Values | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| GPU | **Virtualized GPU** (default); Native GPU (passthrough, experimental); None (CPU only) | **Virtualized**: the VM's apps draw on your graphics card through virtualization, shared with your computer: Vulkan, OpenCL and OpenGL each take the fastest path they have here, translated only where there is no other. **Native GPU**: one of your graphics cards is lent to the running VM: its apps use it directly (CUDA, HIP, Vulkan, OpenCL, OpenGL at full speed), and your computer cannot use that card while it is lent; only on computers that pass its check (see *Native GPU* below). **None**: the VM draws with its processors only (slower; for computers without a usable graphics card). Applies at the VM's next start. |
| Card | **Auto** (default: your computer's choice), or one of your cards by name and address | The card the VM draws on. Each card shows its role (*drives your screen*, *can drive your screen*). With two identical cards, their addresses tell them apart. Under Native GPU, a card that cannot be lent says why. |
| More cards | (Native GPU, computers with several cards) one switch per card | Lend these cards to the VM too (up to 8). A card that cannot be lent says why. |
| Native GPU | (shown with Native GPU) **Allow lending a card**, **Check again** | The line says whether this computer can lend the chosen card and what to do first: the programs to close that use it, a one-time setup that **Allow lending a card** makes (it asks for your administrator password), and, when your screen's cable is plugged into a port of the card that will be lent, where to move it so your screen keeps working. **Check again** reads it again. |
| Lend-ready mode | Off (default) / **Turn on** | Only for a computer with one graphics card that also draws its desktop: from your computer's next restart, its desktop is drawn by the processor, so Native GPU can lend your only card to the VM. Turn it off again to get your card back for your desktop (again from the next restart). |
| GPU memory | Auto: a percentage (default 50 %) of the graphics memory free now, per VM; Manual: a value in GB | The most graphics memory one VM may hold. Shown only where your computer can bound it (Linux 6.14 or newer, with its GPU memory controller); elsewhere the row says it cannot be bounded and shows what each VM holds now. |
| GPU use | A reading (live) | How busy each running VM keeps the graphics card (its busiest engine), as a reading: your computer has no way to cap a VM's share of GPU work. |
| In the VM | A reading | The path each graphics programming interface takes in the VM now, in plain words: Vulkan, OpenGL and OpenCL, each on your card or on the VM's processors. Shown once the VM runs. |

Which apps need what, and how to check that an app uses your card: [Desktop apps and the GPU](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/gpu-apps.html).

## Screen

![Screen tab: Screen size 1400 x 1050 (4:3); Custom size 1400 by 1050 with minus and plus buttons](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/img/settings-resources-4.webp)

Settings › VM resources › Screen, with the default size.

| Option | Values | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| Screen size | 1024 × 768 (4:3), 1280 × 720 (16:9), 1280 × 800 (16:10), 1366 × 768 (16:9), **1400 × 1050 (4:3)** (default), 1440 × 900 (16:10), 1600 × 900 (16:9), 1900 × 1080, 1920 × 1080 (16:9), Custom | The size of the VM's own screen, shared by every tab of the VM (each tab shows the app on it, scaled to the space the tab gives it). A larger screen gives apps more room and takes more memory and bandwidth to draw. |
| Custom size | Width 640–3840, height 480–2160 | Any size in that range (pick **Custom** above, or type: the list follows). |

## Developer options

A hidden section for developers (shown only in developer mode): video memory, the virtualization accelerator (auto, kvm, tcg), the VM's VNC display number, user networking, the API provider, the Pro app account line, and a folder of your computer shared into the VM. You never need them; the command line and the MCP reach them.

## From the command line

The same values, for scripts (see [The command line](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/cli.html#vm-resources)):

```
$ wazza --gui vm-resources
$ wazza --gui vm-memory auto 50 --min 8192
$ wazza --gui vm-disk set 80
$ wazza --gui gpu mode virtualized
```

Page: Chats & agents (Settings)
Address: https://os-guide.wazza.ai/settings-chats.html

# Settings › Chats & agents

The agent and model every new Chat starts with, how long an agent's command or tool call may run, and what Chats may reach on the network.

## New Chats

![New Chats tab: Agent and model Choose; Agent Hermes; Model xiaomi/mimo-v2.6-flash; Provider Auto (Wazza OS's routing); Use for new Chats; and the line New Chats start on Hermes, MiMo-V2.6-Flash, OpenRouter (your choice)](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/img/settings-chats-1.webp)

Settings › Chats & agents › New Chats after choosing MiMo-V2.6-Flash (through an OpenRouter key added in Sign in) as the default.

One default for every new Chat, and for the agents Chats start (unless a Chat picks another). It never changes a Chat that already exists: a Chat keeps its own agent and model (change them in that Chat's [model window](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/chats.html#choose-the-agent-and-the-model)).

| Option | What it does |
|---|---|
| Agent and model › **Choose…** | Opens the same model window as a Chat's: every agent and every model your sign-ins, plans and keys give, with search. Pick there, and choose **Default for new chats** in its **Apply to**. (It opens once a Chat has started in this window.) |
| Agent | The agent (harness) of new Chats: Hermes, Prime Agent, Claude Code, Codex or Antigravity (only the ones that can run here are listed). |
| Model | The model of new Chats. Type to search, or type any model id the agent's provider knows (for example `openrouter/xiaomi/mimo-v2.6-flash`). |
| Provider | Only for an OpenRouter model: **Auto (Wazza OS's routing)**, or one of the companies OpenRouter offers that model from (choose one for its price, speed or data policy). |
| **Use for new Chats** | Saves the three as the default. The line under it says what new Chats start on now and where it comes from. |

With no default saved, new Chats start on a free model when one is available to you; signed in to a Wazza OS account, they start on MiMo. A Chat's agent takes a new default at its next start.

## Time limits

![Time limits tab: Command time limit 600 seconds, Tool call time limit 60 seconds, Save](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/img/settings-chats-2.webp)

Settings › Chats & agents › Time limits, with the defaults.

| Option | Range | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| Command time limit | 10 to 7200 seconds | 600 s (10 minutes) | A shell (bash or terminal) command an agent runs that takes longer is stopped; the agent is told it timed out and goes on. |
| Tool call time limit | 10 to 1800 seconds | 60 s | A tool call that takes longer is stopped the same way. |

**Save** saves both (it checks the ranges first). Wazza OS's own tools take a change at their next call; a Chat's own commands at the Chat's next start. Raise the command limit for long builds, renders or downloads. From a terminal: `wazza --gui timeouts set --command 1800 --tool 120`.

## Network & keys

![Network and keys tab: Local services switch off; Provider gateway Auto or Off, Auto selected](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/img/settings-chats-3.webp)

Settings › Chats & agents › Network & keys, with the defaults.

| Option | Values | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| Local services | **Off** (default) / On | Concerns Chats that run on your computer (not in the VM), such as a Computer Control Chat. Off: they reach the Internet and Wazza OS, never your computer's own services. On: from their next start they also reach services on your computer (`localhost`: a development server, a database), while your keys and sign-ins stay hidden from them. Only you can turn it on; an agent can only turn it off. |
| Provider gateway | **Auto** (default) / Off | Wazza OS's gateway lets every agent use every provider you have: for example Claude Code and Antigravity with a model of your ChatGPT plan, or any agent with a model of an API key or a custom API ([Home › Sign in](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/signin.html#logins) says, for each plan, which agents reach it directly and which through the gateway). Off: each agent uses only the providers it supports by itself. A Chat takes the change at its next start. |

The keys themselves are on [Home › Sign in › API keys](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/signin.html#api-keys).

Page: Skills & learning (Settings)
Address: https://os-guide.wazza.ai/settings-skills.html

# Settings › Skills & learning

Whether Wazza OS learns from your Chats and from how you use apps, how often, with which model, what it learned (with Undo), the skills agents load, and personas.

What skills are and how learning works, with examples: [Skills, learning and personas](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/skills.html). This page explains each tab and option.

## Learning

![Learning tab: Learning Off, This computer, This computer and your account (selected); Least model that learns Lite and up, Standard and up (selected), Strong and up, Frontier only; Learning model field; Status Ready; Spent today 0 tokens in 0 calls](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/img/settings-skills-1.webp)

Settings › Skills & learning › Learning, with the defaults.

| Option | Values | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| Learning | Off; This computer; **This computer and your account** (default) | What Wazza OS keeps from your Chats. Off: nothing is learned. This computer: lessons and new skills are kept on this computer only. This computer and your account: they are also kept with your Wazza OS account (when you are signed in and syncing), so your other computers get them. |
| Least model that learns | Lite and up, **Standard and up** (default), Strong and up, Frontier only | Smaller models neither teach nor learn: a Chat whose model is below this level is not reviewed with it. Raise it if you see poor lessons; lower it if you only use small models. |
| Learning model | Empty (default: each Chat's own model), or a model id, with **Save** and **Use each Chat's own** | The model that reviews Chats. Leave it empty to use each Chat's own model. Set one for Chats whose model is below the bar, or is reached only through its agent's own sign-in (the Status line says when a Chat waits for a learning model). |
| Status | A reading | Whether learning is ready, and why not when it is not. |
| Spent today | A reading | The tokens learning used today, and in how many calls. Learning runs on your models, so it is part of what your provider bills you. |

## How often

![How often tab: Every so many turns 10; Every so many minutes of work 30; After a Chat is idle 10 min; When a Chat ends on; When a Chat is compacted on](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/img/settings-skills-2.webp)

Settings › Skills & learning › How often, with the defaults.

When a Chat is reviewed for lessons. Each number set to 0 turns that trigger off. Changes apply at once.

| Option | Default | A review happens… |
|---|---|---|
| Every so many turns | 10 | after that many of the agent's turns in a Chat. |
| Every so many minutes of work | 30 min | after that much time of agent work in a Chat. |
| After a Chat is idle | 10 min | once a Chat has been quiet that long. |
| When a Chat ends | On | when its tab closes. |
| When a Chat is compacted | On | when a long Chat is summed up to save room (see [Compact a long Chat](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/chats.html#compact-a-long-chat)). |

One Chat can be left out, or reviewed now, from its own model window: **Chat settings** › **Learning in this chat** and **Learn from this chat now**.

## Learned changes

![Learned changes tab: Nothing learned yet, Refresh](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/img/settings-skills-3.webp)

Settings › Skills & learning › Learned changes, before anything was learned.

Everything learned from Chats, newest first. Each change shows its kind (a lesson added to a skill, a new or updated skill, a removed skill, a skill moved), where it applies (an app, with its icon; General; or a project), and its source Chat with **Open its Chat**. Its details quote the evidence from the Chat, show the exact change (what was added and removed) and the model and tokens it took. Per change:

- **Undo**: takes the change back (the skill returns to its version before).
- **Move to General** (or to an app): a learned skill that should apply more widely, or only to one app.

**Refresh** reads the list again.

## App journal

![App journal tab: Learn from how I use apps switch on; Today 0 notes today with Pause and Refresh; Delete notes with Delete today and Delete all](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/img/settings-skills-4.webp)

Settings › Skills & learning › App journal.

| Option | What it does |
|---|---|
| Learn from how I use apps (default: on) | Wazza OS notes the menus you open, the buttons you click and the keys you press in the VM's apps (never a password) and learns how-to lessons from them, for the agents that work in those apps. |
| Today | What was noted today, per app, in plain lines (for example "clicked File ▸ Export As… in GIMP"). **Pause** stops the notes (**Resume** starts them again); **Refresh** reads the list again. |
| Delete notes | **Delete today** deletes today's notes; **Delete all…** deletes every note (it asks you to confirm). |

The journal is yours alone: no Chat reads it or can pause it.

## Skills

![Skills tab: a grid of skill cards, each named with shipped and an Edit button: airtable, apple-notes, architecture-diagram, arxiv, claude-code, codex, docx, github, google-workspace and more](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/img/settings-skills-5.webp)

Settings › Skills & learning › Skills: the skills every Chat may load (the grid continues below).

The basic skills every Chat may load, each with its name and where it comes from (*shipped*: comes with Wazza OS). **Edit** opens the skill's text: a shipped skill opens as your own copy, which then replaces it on this computer (Wazza OS's own reserved skills cannot be edited). App skills, the know-how of one app, are edited in that app's **Edit app** (see [Edit an app's skill](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/custom-apps.html#edit-an-apps-skill)).

## Personas

![Personas tab: the New persona form (name, description, when to use it, a skill search with Add skill, Create persona) and the persona 3D artist (Blender) with its skills lib/3d/blender-modeling and others, each with Remove, Edit description and Attach skill](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/img/settings-skills-6.webp)

Settings › Skills & learning › Personas: the form for a new persona, then the personas (here 3D artist (Blender) and Film director; the list continues below).

A persona is an agent role: a description of how it works and a group of skills it loads. A Chat picks one in its model window (**Chat settings** › **Persona**), or an agent works as one; each persona learns from the Chats that work as it.

| Control | What it does |
|---|---|
| New persona | Name (its role, for example "Release notes writer"), Description (who it is and how it works), When to use it (optional), skills (search the skill library or type a skill id, then **Add skill**), then **Create persona**. |
| Each persona | Its description, when to use it, its skills (each with **Remove**), what it learned, **Edit description**, and **Attach skill** (search, then attach). |

Editing a persona changes only its description, its use line or its skills; what it learned is kept (as its next version, which **Undo** in Learned changes can take back).

Page: Files & sharing (Settings)
Address: https://os-guide.wazza.ai/settings-files.html

# Settings › Files & sharing

Whether files may be copied and pasted between your computer and the VMs, and the company file servers your Chats may read.

How to move files in practice (drag and drop, copy and paste, the Explorer, agents): [Move files](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/files-move.html).

## Between this computer and VMs

![Between this computer and VMs tab: From this computer to a VM Ask Allow Off with Allow selected; From a VM to this computer Ask Allow Off with Ask selected](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/img/settings-files-1.webp)

Settings › Files & sharing › Between this computer and VMs, with the defaults.

| Option | Values | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| From this computer to a VM | Ask, **Allow** (default), Off | Files you copy on your computer (in your file manager) and paste in an app of a VM (its Files, for instance), and an agent's copies into a VM. Allow: they are copied when you paste, or at once for an agent. Ask: Wazza OS asks you each time (a notice with **Allow**). Off: no files are copied this way (text still is). |
| From a VM to this computer | Ask (default), Allow, Off | An agent's copies to your computer (into `Downloads/From the VM` by default, as new files, never over one of yours). Ask: Wazza OS asks you each time (default). Allow: without asking. Off: nothing leaves a VM, your own copies in its apps and your drags out of it included. Your own copy in a VM's app (`Ctrl`+`C`) never asks. |

These two rules are about files. Copied *text* goes both ways between your computer and the VM in every case. Your own drag and drop and the Explorer's Copy, Paste and Download need no allowing: your gesture is the consent. Every way to move files, and what each rule covers: [Move files](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/files-move.html#what-the-file-copy-settings-cover).

## Company folders

![Company folders tab: No company folders yet, Refresh, and the Add a company folder form with Name, How it is reached SFTP, Server, Port 22, Folder on the server, Server identity, Chats may read it on, Plain FTP on this network off, Add folder](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/img/settings-files-2.webp)

Settings › Files & sharing › Company folders, before any folder was added.

A company folder is a folder on a file server (your company's, or your own NAS) that Wazza OS connects to. A folder the Chats may read is in every VM at `/home/ubuntu/Company/<Name>`, **read-only**, so agents can read your company's documents without being able to change them. The list shows each folder with its name, how it is reached, its status in words (connected, needs your login, not reachable…) and its buttons.

### Add a company folder

| Field | What to enter |
|---|---|
| Name | The name it gets in the VM (for example *Acme drive*). |
| How it is reached | SFTP (over SSH), FTPS (explicit TLS), or SMB (a Windows share or a NAS). |
| Server | The server's name or address (for example `files.example.com`). |
| Port | Empty: the usual one for the protocol (22 for SFTP). |
| Folder on the server | The folder to show (for example `/shared`); for SMB, the share's name. |
| Server identity | SFTP: the server's SHA-256 key fingerprint (`SHA256:…`); FTPS: its certificate's fingerprint. Wazza OS connects only to that server, never to an impostor. |
| Chats may read it | On (default): the folder is in every VM, read-only. Off: it stays on this computer only, never in a VM's Chats. |
| Plain FTP on this network | Off (default). For FTPS only: allow unencrypted FTP to a server on your own network that has no TLS. |

Click **Add folder**. Then use the folder's row:

- **Log in**: your own login for that server, kept only on this computer, encrypted.
- **Connect** and **Disconnect**; **Forget my login**.
- **Pin this certificate**: for an FTPS server whose certificate no authority of your computer signed, once you checked the fingerprint shown with the server's owner.

With a team account, the team's owners and admins add folders for every member (each member then logs in with their own login); without a team, the folders you add are your own.

Page: Sync & team (Settings)
Address: https://os-guide.wazza.ai/settings-sync.html

# Settings › Sync & team

Sync your skills, files and Chat history with your Wazza OS account (the vault), and, with a team account, your team's settings and what your team can see.

## Sync

![Sync section: Vault, your skills, files and Chat history synced with your account, Not connected, with Sync now, Connect and Sign out; Chat history switch on](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/img/settings-sync-1.webp)

Settings › Sync & team before connecting: *Not connected: your skills, files and Chat history stay on this computer only*.

| Control | What it does |
|---|---|
| Vault · **Connect** | Connects this computer to your account's vault: the website's sign-in opens in Wazza OS's private sign-in tab, where you approve this computer. Then your skills, files and Chat history sync with your account. The line next to *Vault* says the state (not connected, syncing, up to date…). |
| **Sync now** | Syncs at once instead of waiting for the next automatic sync. |
| **Sign out** | Signs the vault out on this computer. What the vault does not hold yet is kept here, nothing is deleted. |
| Chat history (default: on) | Your Chats sync to your account (personal only: never shared with a team unless you share one yourself). Off: Chats stay on this computer. |
| Held-back deletes · **Confirm deletes** | Shown only when needed. When many files were deleted on this computer at once, the sync holds those deletes back instead of deleting them in your vault too (a brake against accidents). **Confirm deletes** sends them: what was deleted here is deleted in your vault too. |
| Unsent team changes · **Restore** | Shown only when needed: changes you made to team files that never reached the vault. **Restore** puts them back in your own files, in a folder named Unsent team changes, so nothing is lost. |

Sync needs a Wazza OS account: [Home › Sign in](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/signin.html#your-wazza-os-account).

## Team

This section shows only on a team account (an organisation on the Wazza website). What you see depends on your role:

| Part | Who sees it | What it is |
|---|---|---|
| Team | Every member | Which organisation you belong to and your role, the organisation's policy (an owner or admin edits it, a member reads it), and a **Private session** switch when the policy allows private sessions. |
| Activity | Off unless the policy turns it on | An admin sees each member's daily totals: active and idle time, and how many keyboard and mouse inputs, never what was typed, clicked or shown, and no hourly detail. A member sees *Your team can see your active time* and their own daily totals. |
| Shared sessions | Admins | The Chats members chose to share with the team (each Chat's **Share this Chat with my team**), with a viewer that replays one message by message. |

> Team files are kept in the team's vault, which every member of the team can read: activity totals and shared Chats included. The words in the app say so ("Your team can see…").

The company file servers of a team are in [Files & sharing › Company folders](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/settings-files.html#company-folders).
