Page: This computer (Settings)
Address: https://os-guide.wazza.ai/settings-computer.html

# Settings › This computer

What your computer gives Wazza OS, how much of it is used right now, and how to remove Wazza OS's data.

## Check

![Check tab: six checks all ok (Hardware virtualization (KVM), systemd user session, X11 display (XWayland), Chat sandbox, Graphics driver, VM display buffers), the line Wazza OS checked this computer: everything it needs is here, and Check again](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/img/settings-computer-1.webp)

Settings › This computer › Check on a computer where everything is present.

The same six checks as the [first start](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/first-start.html#step-2-checking-this-computer). A line that is not *ok* also says what was found, what does not work while it is missing, and its fixes: a command with a **Copy** button (paste it in a terminal), a step to follow, or a button that opens the Wazza OS setting that fixes it. **Check again** runs the check now (for example after you fixed something). The line under the list says when it was checked, on which system, and how long it took.

Wazza OS also runs the check once at every start: while something is missing, a notification says what and opens this section.

The fixes for every check: [What is checked](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/first-start.html#what-is-checked). In a terminal: `wazza --check` (or `wazza --check --json`); it exits with 1 when something is missing.

## Usage

![Usage tab: linux; This computer CPU 3%, RAM 63%, VRAM dash, DISK 16%; vm-1 CPU 1%, RAM 14%, VRAM 64M, DISK 2.0G](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/img/settings-computer-2.webp)

Settings › This computer › Usage.

| Meter | This computer | The VM (the one this window shows) |
|---|---|---|
| CPU | How busy your computer's processors are. | How busy the VM's processors are. |
| RAM | The share of your computer's memory in use. | The share of the VM's memory in use. |
| VRAM | Your graphics card's memory in use (— when it cannot be read). | The VM's video memory. |
| DISK | The share of your disk in use. | The size of the VM's disk now. |

The live VM card at the bottom of the Home menu shows the same for the VM, with its memory limit ([The VM card](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/window.html#the-vm-card)).

## Remove data

![Remove data tab: Remove Wazza OS, uninstall its package with your system's package manager; Remove all data, your VMs, settings, sign-ins, Chats, logs and caches on this computer, for good, your own files stay, with the Remove all data button](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/img/settings-computer-3.webp)

Settings › This computer › Remove data.

### Remove Wazza OS

Wazza OS is removed with your system's package manager: see [Install › Remove Wazza OS](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/install.html#remove-wazza-os).

> **Removing the package also deletes your Wazza OS data**
>
> Uninstalling the package (`apt remove`, `dnf remove`, `pacman -R`, the tar's `uninstall.sh`) deletes Wazza OS's data on this computer too: your VMs and everything in them, Chats and sign-ins. To update or reinstall, install the new package over the old one instead: your data is kept.

### Remove all data

Erases all of Wazza OS's data on this computer and starts Wazza OS again as on its very first start, without uninstalling it.

1. Click **Remove all data…**. A box opens with what goes (Wazza OS's own folders and their sizes) and what stays.
2. Type `REMOVE ALL DATA` exactly in its field.
3. Click **Remove all data and restart** (it is grey until the words are typed). Or **Cancel**.

| Goes, for good | Stays |
|---|---|
| Every VM and everything in it (apps, files you made inside, the VM's settings), every Chat, every sign-in and key, every setting, logs and caches of Wazza OS. | Your own files on your computer (Documents, Downloads, Desktop, your home folder), including what Wazza OS saved there (Downloads/From the VM, backups), and your other apps. |

Wazza OS then closes, removes its data at its next start and starts as on its first start. If it cannot restart by itself, the row says that a removal is waiting, with **Cancel the removal** (until the next start, the removal can still be cancelled).

> Back up a VM you want to keep first ([Virtual machines › Backups](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/settings-vms.html#backups)): the zip is in your Downloads folder, which stays.


---

Page: The Update page (Settings)
Address: https://os-guide.wazza.ai/update.html

# The Update page

Wazza OS checks for a new signed version when it starts and every hour. When one is out, you download it, install it with your administrator password, and restart Wazza OS. Your VMs, Chats and settings stay.

## Open the Update page

Click **Update** in the Home menu (open Home with the **+** at the end of the tab strip). When an update is waiting, a notification says so too (Home › Notifications, filter **Updates**).

![The Update page: up to date, Wazza OS is up to date, No newer update, and the Check now button](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/img/update-page.webp)

The Update page when no newer version exists.

**Check now** checks at once instead of waiting for the next hourly check. The page says *Wazza OS is up to date* only after a signed update list was really read and holds nothing newer.

## Install an update

1. When a newer version exists, the page shows it with its version, its date, and the changes since your version (*Technical changes*, *Known issues*). Click **Download Update**.
2. Wazza OS downloads the package and checks it against its signature (*Downloading and verifying the package*, with the bytes downloaded). **Cancel Download** stops it. When it ends: *Download complete and verified. Select Install Now to continue.*
3. Click **Install Now**. A small confirmation window of Wazza OS asks you to confirm (**Install Now**, or **Install Later** to keep the download for later).
4. Your system asks for your administrator password (the installation goes through your system's package manager). The page follows the install: copying the verified package, checking it against its signed hash, installing, setting up the new version, with a percentage.
5. When the page says *Installed. Restart Wazza OS to finish.*, click **Restart Wazza OS**. Wazza OS closes and starts again on the new version; your tabs come back.

Coming from alpha 2 or earlier, the first start of the new version says once: *Wazza OS now uses wazza.ai: sign in again*. Earlier versions signed you in on a test website by default; sign in to your Wazza OS account again in Home › [Sign in](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/signin.html#your-wazza-os-account).

Closing the Update page does not cancel an install, and the update is installed exactly once. After the restart, [Settings › General › About](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/settings-general.html#about) shows the new version under both *Running* and *Installed*.

> **You can also update with your package manager**
>
> Install the new package over the old one, exactly like the first install ([Install › Update](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/install.html#update-wazza-os)). Never remove the old package first: removing it deletes your Wazza OS data.

## What the messages mean

| The page says | What it means, what to do |
|---|---|
| Wazza OS is up to date | No newer version. Nothing to do. |
| Wazza OS has not checked for updates yet / Not checked yet | The first check of this start has not run yet. Click **Check now**. |
| The update server could not be reached (offline, or it timed out). | No Internet, or the server did not answer. Check your connection, then **Check now**. |
| The update server is limiting requests from this computer. Try again in a minute. | Too many checks in a short time. Wait a minute. |
| A download failed a moment ago: Download Update is available again after a short wait | Wazza OS waits 30 seconds, then 2 minutes, then 10 minutes between attempts. The button comes back by itself. |
| Four downloads completed this hour | A limit against loops: **Download Update** comes back after the hour. |
| The package on the server is not the size its signed release names. Nothing was installed. | The download did not match its signature, so it was refused. Try again later. |
| This version is no longer published: a newer one replaced it while it downloaded. | Wazza OS checks for the newer one by itself. Download that one. |
| Downloaded and verified, not installed yet: select Install Now. | The download is ready; click **Install Now** when it suits you. |
| Install Now was not confirmed. The update stays downloaded and verified: select Install Now again. | The confirmation window was closed or answered Install Later. Nothing is lost. |
| The confirmation window got no answer within 30 seconds. | Click **Install Now** again and answer the window. |
| Wazza OS's window was not in front, so the confirmation could not be shown. | Bring Wazza OS to the front, click **Install Now** again. |
| Waiting for the administrator password, then installing | Type your password in the system's prompt. |
| Installed. Restart Wazza OS to finish. | Click **Restart Wazza OS**. |
| Wazza OS could not restart by itself | Quit Wazza OS and start it again from your app menu. |
| The original installation result is unknown. Check status; do not repeat it. | Click **Check Installation Status**: Wazza OS reads what your package manager installed. Do not install a second time. |
| Your version is not in the update history, so the list of changes since it may be incomplete. | Only the list of changes is affected; the update itself is fine. |

Still stuck: [Troubleshooting › Updates](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/troubleshooting.html#updates).


---

Page: Privacy and security (How it behaves)
Address: https://os-guide.wazza.ai/privacy-security.html

# Privacy and security

Wazza OS protects your computer by giving agents a computer of their own: the VM. Agents work there freely; what reaches your real computer (your files, your screen) goes through you.

## What runs where

| Where | What runs there | What it can reach |
|---|---|---|
| The VM | The apps (GIMP, Chromium…), the Hermes agent, every agent's commands and file work | The VM's own files and the Internet. Not your computer's files, not your screen. |
| Your computer, inside Wazza OS's sandbox | The agent programs of some Chats (for example Claude Code and Codex), and the Computer Control Chat | Their own folder (bubblewrap and Landlock), the Internet and Wazza OS. Not your other files; not services of your computer unless you turn on [Local services](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/settings-chats.html#network-and-keys). |
| Your computer | The Wazza OS window, the VM's engine, Wazza OS's own services | Its own folders; it never changes your files (what it writes is always new files). |
| The AI provider you chose | The model | What the agent sends it: your messages, and the content the agent reads or looks at to answer (files, pictures of an app). Its own policy applies (your plan's or key's). |

## Agents in the VM work without asking

A Chat's agent runs its commands and edits files in the VM without asking you each time: Wazza OS has no "ask mode". The VM is the protection: what an agent does there cannot touch your own computer's files. For mistakes inside the VM, Wazza OS keeps the versions of files that get overwritten and a checkpoint of every file a Chat edits ([Versions and undo](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/files.html#versions-and-undo)), and you can back up a whole VM ([Backups](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/settings-vms.html#backups)).

## Where Wazza OS asks you

Inside the VM, agents never ask: they run commands, install and uninstall apps, write to other tabs' Chats and take steps that cannot be undone (deleting, sending) without a card. When you want to approve something first, say so in your message ("show me the plan before you install anything"). What reaches your own computer is different:

| When | What happens | Who decides |
|---|---|---|
| Files from your computer go into the VM (your paste, an agent's copy) | By your rule in [Files & sharing](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/settings-files.html): Allow (default), Ask, or Off. Attaching a file to a Chat is your own pick in a file chooser. | You |
| Files from the VM go to your computer (your paste, an agent's upload) | A question each time by default (Ask); they land in `Downloads/From the VM`, never over your files | You |
| An agent wants to see or use your screen | The [Computer Control](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/computer-control.html) consent card, per tab, and again after every restart | Only your own click on Start |
| A sandboxed Chat on your computer wants to edit your files | **Let this Chat edit my files** in its model window (with a confirmation); off again at every Wazza OS start | Only you |
| Local services, importing your Chrome profile | Settings switches and buttons that only your own click turns on (an agent can only turn Local services off) | Only you |

## Keys and sign-ins

- API keys, plan sign-ins, custom API tokens and your Wazza OS account are kept on your computer, in Wazza OS's encrypted store.
- Agents in the VM never get the key itself: their requests go through Wazza OS, which adds it.
- The Sign in page shows a key by its last characters only; the command line takes keys on standard input only, never as a word of a command.
- Company folder logins stay on this computer, encrypted; web app sign-ins live in the VM's browser (Sign out of all web apps ends them).

## What leaves your computer

| What | To where | When |
|---|---|---|
| Your messages and what agents read to answer | The AI provider of the Chat's model | When you use a Chat |
| Your skills, files and Chat history | Your Wazza OS account's vault | Only when you connected sync (Chat history can be turned off) |
| Feedback | Wazza, without your account (only Wazza OS's version is added) | When you send feedback |
| Update checks | Wazza OS's download server | At start and every hour (updates are signed and checked before install) |
| Team activity totals (active and idle time, input counts; never content) | Your team's vault | Only on a team account whose policy turns it on |

The app journal (Wazza OS noting the menus, clicks and keys you use in apps, never a password) stays on your computer to teach agents; pause it or delete it in [Settings › Skills & learning › App journal](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/settings-skills.html#app-journal). To erase everything: [Remove all data](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/settings-computer.html#remove-all-data).


---

Page: Memory, CPU and disk (How it behaves)
Address: https://os-guide.wazza.ai/memory-cpu.html

# Memory, CPU and disk

Wazza OS does not reserve your computer for its VM. The VM starts small, takes memory and processors when its apps need them, up to a limit, and gives them back when it is idle. Your own apps keep working, and heavy work in the VM still gets what it needs.

## Limits, not reservations

| Resource | At the VM's start | While it runs | The limit, by default |
|---|---|---|---|
| Memory | What its desktop needs, fitted to what is free | Grows when its apps need more, gives back when idle | 75 % of the memory free now (counting what the VMs hold), never below 8 GB when your computer has that much |
| Processors | 2 | More while its programs wait for processor time | 75 % of your computer's threads |
| Disk | The space it already uses | Grows as files are written; never shrinks | 50 % of the free space of the drive that holds it |
| Graphics card | Shared with your computer | Used as its apps draw | Graphics memory: 50 % of what is free, where Linux can bound it (6.14 or newer) |

A high limit costs nothing until it is used. Change the limits in [Settings › VM resources](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/settings-resources.html); with several VMs running, the limits are shared between them.

## See what is used

- **The VM card** at the bottom of the Home menu: the VM's CPU and its memory used of its limit now ([The VM card](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/window.html#the-vm-card)).
- **A tab's card**: hold the pointer over a tab to see what it uses: memory and CPU, split between its app and its Chat ([The tab card](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/window.html#the-tab-card)).
- **Settings › This computer › Usage**: CPU, memory, video memory and disk of your computer and of the VM.
- From a terminal: `wazza --gui vm-resources`, `wazza --gui vm-memory status`.

## When memory is short

Wazza OS keeps 10 % of your computer's memory free for your computer itself. When the VM would need more than that leaves, it stops growing, and a notice says so:

![The notice: Wazza OS keeps 10% of this computer's memory free; the VM stays at 3.1 GB. Open owning tab](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/img/memory-notice-toast.webp)

The VM held at 3.1 GB on the 8 GB test computer while an app was installing.

| Notice | What it means | What to do |
|---|---|---|
| Wazza OS keeps 10% of this computer's memory free; the VM stays at … GB. | The VM wanted more memory, and your computer has no more to give without slowing down. | Nothing, if the VM's apps keep working. Otherwise close apps on your computer, or tabs in Wazza OS you do not need. **Open owning tab** shows the tab that asked for memory. |
| Your computer is almost out of memory and the VM may stop. Close apps you do not need on this computer. | Your computer itself is running out. | Close apps on your computer now; save your work in the VM. |
| Not enough free memory to start the VM | At start, too little memory is free for the VM's desktop. | The card names the apps that use the most memory: close one or two, then start again. |
| The VM can use up to N processors after its next restart. | A change of processors waits for the next start. | Restart the VM when it suits you ([Restart](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/settings-vms.html#this-window-shows)). |

Memory also limits how many agents work at once: past the first helper agent, no new one starts while the VM is short of memory ([Several agents at once › Limits](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/parallel-tabs.html#limits)).

## Laptops and small computers

- Lower the memory limit (for example Auto 50 %) and the processors (Half · 50 %) in [VM resources](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/settings-resources.html#memory-and-cpu), then **Save and apply** (memory and processors apply at once).
- Lower [General › Max frame rate](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/settings-general.html#display) to 60: drawing app tabs costs less.
- Close tabs you do not use: each open app runs in the VM.
- Glass **Off** and **Reduce motion** save a little drawing work too.

## Disk space

The VM's disk is a file on your computer that grows as the VM writes, up to its limit, and never shrinks: deleting files in the VM frees space inside the VM, not on your computer. To see its size: the VM's row in [Virtual machines](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/settings-vms.html#the-vm-list). To get space back, move what you want to keep out of the VM, then reset or remove that VM (vm-2 to vm-8), or back it up first. Wazza OS itself takes about 8 GB.


---

Page: Troubleshooting (Help)
Address: https://os-guide.wazza.ai/troubleshooting.html

# Troubleshooting

Find your symptom below. Most problems come from something the computer lacks, which `wazza --check` names with its fix, or from a key or memory running out.

> First step for anything about starting: run `wazza --check` in a terminal. It checks KVM, the systemd user session, the display, the Chat sandbox, the graphics driver and the VM display buffers, and prints the commands that fix what is missing ([What is checked](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/first-start.html#what-is-checked)).

## The window does not open

- **No X11 display**: Wazza OS's window needs X11, which Wayland desktops give through XWayland. `wazza --check` names the package to install for your distribution (for example `sudo apt install xwayland`).
- **Already running**: a second start only brings the running window to the front. Look for it on another workspace or screen.
- **On a server**, start it with its own screen: [Wazza OS on a server](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/cli-server.html).

## The VM does not start

| What you see | Why | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| The check says *Hardware virtualization (KVM)* is missing | Virtualization is off in the firmware, or your user may not use `/dev/kvm` | Turn on VT-x (Intel) or SVM (AMD) in your computer's firmware settings; `sudo usermod -aG kvm "$USER"`, then log out and in |
| The check says *systemd user session* is missing | Each VM runs in a memory-capped part of your user session | Log in through your desktop; on a server, `loginctl enable-linger "$USER"` |
| The check says *VM display buffers* is missing | The VM's picture needs larger system buffers | `sudo sysctl -w net.core.rmem_max=4194304 net.core.wmem_max=4194304` (the package sets it at boot) |
| *Not enough free memory to start the VM* | Too little memory is free for its desktop | Close one or two of the apps the card names, then start again ([When memory is short](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/memory-cpu.html#when-memory-is-short)) |
| It stays *starting* for long | The first start of a VM prepares its disk and takes longer than the next ones | Wait; then Settings › Virtual machines › Restart ([This window shows](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/settings-vms.html#this-window-shows)) |
| Your disk is full | The VM's disk grows as it writes | Free space on your computer ([Disk space](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/memory-cpu.html#disk-space)) |

## A Chat does not answer

- **No key or sign-in**: Wazza OS comes without an AI key. A Chat on Hermes then answers at once *Add an OpenRouter key under Sign In › API keys, or sign in to your Wazza account*: add a key, sign in to your Wazza OS account, or log in with a plan you pay for ([Sign in, keys and plans](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/signin.html)).
- **A model your keys do not reach**: a Chat keeps the model it started with. If no key or account of yours reaches it, the Chat says which one it needs: *This model runs on an OpenRouter key: add one under Sign In › API keys, or pick a Wazza model*, or *This model runs on your Wazza account: sign in to it, or pick an OpenRouter model*. Add it, or pick another model in the Chat's model window ([Choose the agent and the model](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/chats.html#choose-the-agent-and-the-model)).
- **Out of credit or rate-limited**: `wazza --gui provider-keys list --credit` shows what OpenRouter and DeepSeek keys have left. Add a second key or account: when one runs out, the next takes over ([Several keys or accounts](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/signin.html#several-keys-or-accounts)).
- **A long job**: a command an agent runs may take up to 10 minutes before it is stopped ([Time limits](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/settings-chats.html#time-limits)). The Chat's steps show what it is doing; the stop button stops it.
- **Chats on your computer do not start** (Claude Code, Codex…): the check's *Chat sandbox* line is missing or limited. Its fixes reload Wazza OS's AppArmor profile or allow user namespaces, for example `sudo apparmor_parser -r /etc/apparmor.d/wazza-bwrap`.

## An app tab stays black or frozen

1. Wait a moment if the app is starting: the tab says so, and large apps take a while the first time.
2. Right-click the tab › **Reload**: the tab's app starts again ([The tab menu](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/window.html#the-tab-menu)).
3. Reset the picture between Wazza OS and the tab, without touching the app: ask the tab's Chat to "recover this tab", or run `wazza --gui drive recover --tab TAB`.
4. Look at the VM card at the bottom of Home: if the VM is not *running*, start or restart it in Settings › Virtual machines.
5. Every app slow or black: check the graphics. The VM card's last line names your graphics card; *llvmpipe* there means software graphics. `wazza --check`'s *Graphics driver* line says what to fix; to rule the card out, set Settings › VM resources › Graphics › GPU to **None (CPU only)** and restart the VM ([When 3D is slow](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/gpu-apps.html#when-3d-is-slow)).

## An app does not install

- The tab says why, with **Retry installation** and **Show log**; Wazza OS already retried once by itself. Most failures are the VM's Internet connection or a download server that is down: retry later.
- The VM's disk or memory is full: see [Memory, CPU and disk](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/memory-cpu.html).
- An app you added: its install script failed; read the log, fix the script in **Edit app…** and install again ([Edit an app](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/custom-apps.html#edit-an-app)).

## Files do not copy

- Settings › Files & sharing: a direction set to **Off** copies no files (text still copies). With **Ask**, look for the question ([Files & sharing](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/settings-files.html)).
- Files from the VM land in `Downloads/From the VM` on your computer, as new files, never over yours.
- An agent can copy only files below your home folder, and no hidden ones.

## No sound

- Only the tab you are on is heard. Check that tab's menu › **Sound** (muted, volume).
- The VM's sound needs the *Sound card drivers* tool, installed on the first start: Apps › System; install it again if it is missing.
- Your computer's own output and volume apply as for any app.

## Everything is slow

- Your computer is short of memory: close apps and tabs you do not use ([Memory, CPU and disk](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/memory-cpu.html)).
- The VM may use too few processors for heavy work: raise them in [VM resources](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/settings-resources.html#memory-and-cpu).
- 3D apps: [When 3D is slow](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/gpu-apps.html#when-3d-is-slow).
- The window itself: lower [Max frame rate](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/settings-general.html#display), set Glass to Off.

## Sign-in problems

- A plan login opens your browser: finish it there, then come back; an attempt that is not finished in time ends by itself, and you can start again.
- An API key is refused when it is checked: copy it again from your provider's site, whole, with no space.
- Several accounts: the order and the rotation are on the Sign in page ([Several keys or accounts](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/signin.html#several-keys-or-accounts)).

## Updates

- Each message of the Update page, with what to do: [What the messages mean](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/update.html#what-the-messages-mean).
- The update downloads but does not install: **Install Now** needs your confirmation, then your administrator password. Keep Wazza OS's window in front while you confirm.
- The page cannot reach the update server: check your connection. You can always update with the install command, or download the package from `https://os-downloads.wazza.ai` and install it over your version ([Install › Update](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/install.html#update-wazza-os)).
- After an update, restart Wazza OS: until then the old version keeps running.

> Never remove the Wazza OS package to reinstall it: removing it deletes your Wazza OS data (VMs, Chats, settings). Install the new package over the old one.

## Start fresh

- Show the first start's steps again: `wazza --gui setup reset-first-run`, then restart Wazza OS.
- Reset one VM other than vm-1, or remove it: Settings › Virtual machines ([Remove or reset a VM](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/settings-vms.html#remove-or-reset-a-vm)).
- Remove all of Wazza OS's data on this computer and start like the first time: [Settings › This computer › Remove all data](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/settings-computer.html#remove-all-data).

## Send feedback

Home › **Feedback**: say what happened and what you expected. Wazza OS adds its version, never your account ([Feedback](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/window.html#feedback)). For a problem with an agent, say which tab, which agent and model, and what you asked.


---

Page: Glossary (Help)
Address: https://os-guide.wazza.ai/glossary.html

# Glossary

The words of Wazza OS, in plain language, each with the page that explains it.

**Agent:** An AI that works for you in a Chat: it reads your message, uses tools (commands, apps, files) and answers. See [Chats](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/chats.html).

**API key:** A secret code from an AI provider (OpenRouter, OpenAI, Anthropic…) that lets Wazza OS use its models, billed to your account there. See [API keys](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/signin.html#api-keys).

**App:** A Linux desktop program of the VM (GIMP, Blender, Chromium…), or a web app in the VM's browser. Each opens in a tab. See [Apps](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/apps.html).

**App journal:** Wazza OS's notes of the menus, clicks and keys you use in the VM's apps (never a password), from which agents learn how-to lessons. See [App journal](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/settings-skills.html#app-journal).

**App skill:** The skill files of one app: what the agent of that app's tabs knows about it. See [Edit an app's skill](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/custom-apps.html#edit-an-apps-skill).

**App tools:** An app's own tools for agents, from its MCP server: GIMP has 40. The Chat of a tab where the app is open gets them. See [Give your app tools](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/custom-apps.html#give-your-app-tools).

**Chat:** The conversation beside a tab's app, with its agent. Every tab has one. See [Chats](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/chats.html).

**Company folder:** A folder of your company's file server (SFTP, FTPS or SMB) that every VM sees, read-only, at `~/Company/<Name>`. See [Company folders](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/files.html#company-folders).

**Compact:** Summing up a long Chat so it fits the model again; the Chat goes on from the summary. See [Compact a long Chat](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/chats.html#compact-a-long-chat).

**Computer Control:** A special Chat whose agent may see and use your own computer's screen, keyboard and mouse, after your click on Start, until its tab closes. See [Computer Control](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/computer-control.html).

**Custom API:** An AI endpoint you add by its address (your own server, a company gateway, a local model). See [Custom API](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/signin.html#custom-api).

**Drive:** How an agent looks at an app's screen and acts on it with the mouse and keyboard, in any app. See [Drive](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/drive.html).

**Explorer:** The file browser of the VM's files, at the far left of the tab strip. See [The Explorer](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/files.html#the-explorer).

**Harness:** The agent program that runs a Chat: Hermes, Prime Agent, Claude Code, Codex or Antigravity. Each works with the models its logins and keys reach. See [The agents](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/chats.html#the-agents).

**Helper agent:** An agent a Chat starts for part of a job: *visible* in its own app tab, or *hidden* in the background. See [Several agents at once](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/parallel-tabs.html).

**Home:** The menu at the left of the window: Apps, Settings, Sign in, History, Update, Notifications, Feedback, and the VM card. See [Home](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/window.html#home).

**KVM:** Linux's hardware virtualization, which runs the VM at full speed. Your computer must have it turned on. See [What your computer needs](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/install.html#what-your-computer-needs).

**Lesson:** A short piece of know-how Wazza OS learned from a Chat and added beside a skill, with its evidence. See [How Wazza OS learns](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/skills.html#how-wazza-os-learns).

**Login (plan login):** Signing in with an AI plan you already pay for (Claude, ChatGPT, Grok, Google…), instead of a key. See [Logins](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/signin.html#logins).

**MCP:** The Model Context Protocol: the standard way agents get tools. Wazza OS gives every Chat its tools through its MCP server. See [The Wazza OS MCP](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/mcp.html).

**Model:** The AI behind an agent (for example MiMo, Claude Sonnet, GPT), from a provider. Each Chat has its own. See [Choose the agent and the model](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/chats.html#choose-the-agent-and-the-model).

**Native GPU:** Lending one of your graphics cards to the running VM, for full-speed compute. Experimental. See [Lend a card](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/gpu-apps.html#lend-a-card-native-gpu).

**Persona:** An agent role (3D artist, film director, writer…): how it works and the skills it loads; it learns from its Chats. See [Personas](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/skills.html#personas).

**Provider:** A company that runs AI models (OpenRouter, OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, xAI, DeepSeek…).

**Recipe:** How an app installs in the VM and starts, with its optional tools and skill. See [Add your own apps](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/custom-apps.html).

**Seat:** Where Drive acts: an app tab of the VM, the agent's terminal, or (Computer Control only) your computer.

**Setup file:** A JSON file that does the first start's steps from the command line. See [Set up without clicks](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/cli.html#set-up-without-clicks).

**Skill:** Written know-how an agent loads before it works: procedures, checks, pitfalls. See [Skills, learning and personas](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/skills.html).

**Sync:** Keeping your skills, files and Chat history with your Wazza OS account, for your other computers. See [Sync & team](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/settings-sync.html).

**Tab:** One app of the VM with its Chat, in the strip at the top of the window. See [Tabs](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/window.html#tabs).

**Tool:** One operation an agent can call (open an app, export an image, click). In Apps, a *tool* is also a package with no window that gives the VM a capability (Git, GPU for apps, Search).

**Virtual screen:** An invisible screen Wazza OS brings when the computer has none, on a server. See [The virtual screen](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/cli-server.html#the-virtual-screen).

**Virtualized GPU:** The default way the VM's apps use your graphics card: shared with your computer. See [Desktop apps and the GPU](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/gpu-apps.html).

**VM (virtual machine):** The computer of its own that Wazza OS runs on yours: Ubuntu, with its desktop, apps and files. Apps and agents work there. vm-1 is the main one; you can add vm-2 to vm-8. See [Virtual machines](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/settings-vms.html).

**VM card:** The card at the bottom of Home with the VM's state, CPU, memory and graphics. See [The VM card](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/window.html#the-vm-card).

**Wazza OS account:** Your account with Wazza OS (email and password, or online): sync, teams, and Wazza OS models. Optional: Chats work without it. See [Your Wazza OS account](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/signin.html#your-wazza-os-account).

**Web app:** A website that works like an app (Gmail, Google Docs, Word, Teams), opened in the VM's browser as its own tab. See [Web apps](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/signin.html#web-apps).
